generated_text: Oh, did I ever tell you about that night out Grace had? It nearly became an all-nighter! She and the lads decided to ditch the pub at 10 and ended up at a late-night chicken shop! That's typical of her, isn't it? Going from one thing to another without a plan and ending up somewhere completely out of the blue. Absolutely! But actually, that night out gave me an idea. Our niece is turning 5 next month and keeps coming up with these wild ideas for her party. You'll need to hear her latest, she wants a unicorn-themed party! Unicorns! I can just imagine her trying to explain why she can't have a real unicorn in the garden for her party. Exactly! And to be fair, it could be a really fun idea if we can make it happen. Maybe we could order a cake shaped like a unicorn, or even have someone dressed up as one. Oh, that would be magical! And I heard there's a new business in town that does cute unicorn-themed party decorations and activities. I could look into it. That would be fantastic! The kids these days love the 'unicorn culture' so much. It’s a shame though, we never got the chance to properly celebrate our birthday plans. Ah, the birthday plans. Between work and trying to keep up with all the plans, life is just always so busy. But you know what’s always a highlight? Going to Mum and Dad’s for Sunday lunch. Oh, that’s always a treat! Especially since we both have our own families now and it’s a good excuse for everyone to get together. I just wish we could do it a bit more often. Speaking of which, have you checked with them about this month? It’s going to be a chaotic week with both kids' birthdays and the entire family changing plans because of that wedding. Not yet, I was thinking about it this morning but I had so much to do for work. I will make sure to give them a ring today so we can make sure they're available if we want to plan a proper family dinner. That’d be great. And maybe we can even plan something bigger if we all fit in. You know how relatives are when everyone's together, always so lively and full of energy!

Right, so I'm going to apply for this research grant, and part of it requires me to spend a few months in Paris to collaborate with a colleague there. That sounds like a great opportunity. Is this something you've talked to your boss about and do they support you doing that kind of research? Yes, and they're actually really enthusiastic about it. They've always been supportive of my career and professional development, which is lovely actually, as it can be quite rare in academia. That's brilliant. You know, I've actually been meaning to apply for my PhD to be based in Paris. There are some fantastic labs there for my research, and the EU funding opportunities are very generous. Absolutely, the EU is very dedicated to funding excellent research. But actually, while we're on the subject - have you traveled extensively in the EU? I mean, aside from the usual tourist spots, have you experienced living or working in a different European country? Yes, I have. While I was completing my master's, I worked in a lab in Berlin for a summer. That's really cool! I've traveled a fair bit, mostly within the UK or to Paris for short stays as a student, but never really lived anywhere else. I'm curious about everything. What was the biggest surprise about living and working in Berlin? For me, it was how much technology is integrated into everyday life, even for jobs as 'mundane' as being a lab technician. Automation isn't in-your-face, but it's everywhere, and it really aids in efficiency. Also, the food and drink culture is insanely rich. I was surprised by how many times I'd have beer and the locals would say, 'You're buying this imported lager? Haven't you tried our local craft beers?' Haha, that sounds hilarious! And, of course, the food. I've always loved German cuisine, even if I do say so myself. The idea of being able to try all of those local specialties regularly would be a dream. You'd also find a lot of British expats over there, especially in some of the cities. It's actually quite easy to find a bit of a home from home if you need it. That's good to know. But have you found it difficult to settle into a new culture?

Oh, did I ever tell you about the time I made my own apple pie? It was more like a disaster but it was so fun! I talked about it in the tea and cake social club at school. Did you win a prize for being the most disastrous baker? Not exactly. But I won the prize for "Most Creative Attempt"! What happened? Was it a really bad pie? Oh, it was a bit too sweet, the crust was burnt a bit, and the apples... well, they just didn't want to cooperate. Sounds like a pie from Monopoly, actually. You know, the ones that are "extra delicious" but always come with a twist? Exactly! But despite all that, everyone enjoyed trying it. I think I'd like to try baking a pie. Maybe next week we could do a family baking day? That's a great idea! We could make enough for a week. And who knows, maybe we can even have a little competition. Can the losers pay rent in the game of Monopoly? Maybe we could have a little "pie tax" system. The loser has to buy all the ingredients for another round of baking, and the winner gets to pick the dessert that everyone else makes. But it's not fair! I haven't played Monopoly yet and I'd lose for sure. Don't worry, there will be lots of practice and we'll learn together. Plus, I can even explain the rules again if you want. While you talk about pies and Monopoly, has anyone checked if we have enough change for Monopoly money? Let me check. Ah yes, we've got plenty. Gran, can we spend some of that money to buy desserts real soon? Perhaps. But remember, desserts don't grow on trees or trade hands in Monopoly either. We need to budget for them wisely. We could even make the desserts part of the game. Each person who lands on a certain spot has to bring the next dessert to the table. That's a clever idea! We can definitely incorporate that next time we play. Okay, so dessert baking day is planned for this weekend. And next week, we'll play Monopoly and see who is the best baker and banker. Can we also paint on the cheesecake recipe and save it for a real cheesecake later? Absolutely! We can make it a fun and educational activity too.

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new policy they're introducing at work? Makes me so mad, really. What's the deal with it? Hadn't really had time to look into it yet. Is it affecting our roles or something? Not directly, but it questions some of the older procedures and seems to be moving towards less face-to-face interaction. As a corpus administrator, that means a lot of what we do could end up online or via AI. Oh, I see... So more tech-based approaches? That could be quite interesting. You'll need to rethink your role slightly. Exactly, and the problem is I'm not sure if I'm ready for that. I like the analytical bit, but sometimes I wish we could just talk through a problem together, you know? Totally get that. Sometimes a face-to-face discussion is the best way to understand where everyone's coming from and get creative solutions. But technology can also be a big help, can't it? Provides so much more data and analytical power. That's true, but it's the human aspect of this job I'm worried about losing. We're not just about numbers and data; we're about understanding how people communicate and all that. You're right, but the shift is inevitable, perhaps. It's not necessarily about replacing human interaction, but enhancing it through technology. Perhaps there are ways to balance both? I hope so. There's one thing I've learned: as long as there's a human understanding of the data and a consideration for humanity in the working environment, technology can be a real asset. But it's hard to see that from the place I'm at right now. I agree. It's hard when you're so used to a certain way of doing things, but change can also bring opportunities. You might end up enjoying some parts of it more than you think. Yeah, perhaps. It's just uncomfortable figuring out what those will be. You'll figure it out. You always do. Plus, you've got advanced degrees – you're more than capable of navigating these changes. Thanks for the vote of confidence, but it doesn't always feel like that inside my head! Haha. You could use this as an opportunity to upskill or reskill in certain areas. There could be parts of your role that remain, and then new areas that emerge which could be really interesting for you.

Right, so I've been reading about this new program the council's trying to start up. It's called 'Back to Work'. From what I can gather, it sounds like they're offering more training and support than what we've had before. That sounds hopeful, but we need to remember we've had quite a few disappointments over the years. Back in the 80s they offered a similar program and not many of us saw real benefits from it, especially the long-term unemployed like us. Oh, I agree with that. But maybe it's different this time? This program seems to have a wider range of options. There was even something in the paper about apprenticeships for people our age. I used to run a nursery in Harrow, so something like that could be very tempting. You're right, that could be a good opportunity. I did well with hands-on work when I was a civil engineer. But we should also be cautious. It's important that we don't get our hopes up only to have them crushed again. That's a very valid point. Past experiences should make us wary, but at the same time, we can't just sit here and do nothing. One thing they mentioned was a support system, like mentors or peer groups. That could be a big difference this time. Exactly! It’s the support that matters, not just the jobs or courses on offer. If they can connect us with people who understand our challenges, who have faced them themselves perhaps, that could be really beneficial. I see what you mean. Communication and support can make a big difference. We might not be looking for traditional jobs anymore, but maybe there are community projects or roles that could use our skills and experience. There could be, but until we actually see if this program delivers what it promises, we should maintain our hope measured with realism. As we've lived through, times of unemployment are tough. If they're offering support and training, perhaps we could use this opportunity to explore other interests or passions we never had a chance to pursue. That’s a good thought. I've always wanted to learn more about woodwork. There's a local workshop I've been meaning to visit. If they're training people in different skills, maybe there's a chance for me to learn that.

Hi Sarah, I hope you've been well! How was your day? I've been meaning to catch up with you about your business, Honest Skincare, I've been thinking a lot about marketing strategies. You know I've always been quite fascinated by that. How are things going? Oh, Rachel, it's been a real rollercoaster! Some days make me want to pull my hair out, but others make it all worth it. Honestly, I've been doing a bit of everything to get the word out about my products — social media keeps me busy, alongside a bit of local advertising. You'll probably be pleased to hear, though, sales are slowly starting to pick up. That's great news! I wasn't sure if you'd consider it, but would you be open to some professional guidance from a marketing perspective? I've worked with a few companies as a freelance consultant and even taught a marketing module during my postgrad, I could share some insights with you. Really? That's so kind of you, Rachel! But honestly, I'm not sure where to start. I'm still trying to wrap my head around a lot of it. No problem at all, it's no trouble for me. Plus, I find the process pretty fun. Where do you think you might need the most help? Is it in understanding your target audience, creating a brand identity, building your online presence? All of it, really! I want to make Honest Skincare feel unique, but also accessible. Like, in my mind, I have a clear idea of who we are, but getting that across — that’s harder. Plus, I don't really know how to measure success. That's completely normal, Sarah. Let me think on it for a bit, and maybe I can come up with a structured plan. But one thing that's really beginner-friendly and a good start, if you haven't done it yet, is analyzing your web traffic. You can use tools like Google Analytics for that. It's free and really insightful. From there, we can see what's working and where we need to improve. Oh, that sounds like a great idea. I had no idea! But Rachel, I have so many ideas, but I always feel stuck because I don't know how to execute them properly. We can tackle that step by step.

Ah, hello dear! I've missed you so much! It's been ages since we've caught up like this. How's life treating you in the city? Hello, sis! You're right, it has been a while. Life is good though, the usual routine. How about you? How have you been settling back into quiet life? Well, settling might be a bit of a strong word, considering I've never settled into employment actually. But I've never had much to worry about financially. Which is rather fortunate, I suppose. Oh, we know, you've always had your lazy streak, sis! But seriously, how are you coping with not being part of the workforce anymore? You know, it's been a bit odd at first, but I've found other things to keep me engaged. Keeping up with the news, trying to learn about this and that on the internet... That's good, sis. But you must feel a bit isolated at times. As for the news, I've been quite concerned about the recent cuts in our healthcare system. I don't know about you, but it seems like it's been affecting a lot of retirees. Yes, I've heard the same. It's certainly worrying to hear stories about people having to wait for weeks to see their GPs or families struggling to afford prescriptions for chronic conditions. A bit scary for those who still have to rely on it in their later years really. It’s all about prioritizing budgets and "efficiency" nowadays, isn’t it? But it seems like it's the wrong things they're cutting. As a teacher, I see it in education too. It’s hard when resources are so tight. It’s strange, isn’t it? We always talked about the future being better for everyone. We were brought up to believe in progress and equality. But it feels like we are sliding backwards in many ways. True, but changing the world takes time. We just have to do our part where we can, I suppose. I try to support the community through my work, of course. But it’s hard when the structure isn't so supportive. You know, it makes me think of our parents. They always emphasized education as the key to a better life, and I've certainly done that. I remember your academic achievements during your time at university.

Oh, it's been ages! I've missed catching up with you all. Hope you all had a great year and are well. Cheers, well, despite the uncertainty of 2020, I'd say we all made do, eh? But let's face it, this kind of atmosphere is way better. Though, I did have to put the heating on pretty early this year. Absolutely, and it's not just the early heat keeps coming in. This year has been quite unpredictable. Have you heard about the mulberries from [Speaker_1]'s garden? Apparently, they were just perfect for those hot summer days. Oh, the mulberries from my little patch were a hit even among the squirrels. Though I have to say, they seem to enjoy them a bit too much. That's the spirit! But honestly, we're heading into the holiday season, and I'm still not sure what Christmas will look like. Hopefully, we won't need this heating on too much, as I've been saving up for that wooden fire pit for the garden. I know what you mean. With the weather uncertainty, I've been tinkering with building a miniature greenhouse for my workshop. Who knows, might actually keep my workshop at a nice temperature for when I need to craft something. That's a brilliant idea, [Speaker_4]. Speaking of which, have you all played any good board games lately? I recently picked up "Catan" and it was quite a hit with my family the other night. Yes! I just discovered "Ticket to Ride" and it was surprisingly fun, especially together. But I just tried to explain the rules to [Speaker_4] over email and... well, it proves books are better than words sometimes. True, but changing the subject to something less intellectual for a change might be a good idea. Maybe for now. I've been thinking, though, about retirement. As much as I love my current job, I've started to consider plans to set up a little workshop on the outskirts of the city. Not sure if I'll actually follow through, but the thought of having a space to retreat to and work on personal projects sounds quite appealing. Oh, that sounds like a great idea. I've been feeling the same way about setting up a small studio in the garden. Maybe that's what I'll focus on next summer... when it's actually warm outside.

Oh, Dad, don't you remember? We have these two spare sets; one is silver and one is stainless steel. But they don't match, so we don't use them. Is that why we never get the matching knives and forks when we're eating together? I remember those sets. They were quite a part of my history with the family. Do you remember those, Dad? All that set for us when we moved into our first house. Oh, yeah, those. Your mum spent ages choosing them I seem to recall. Indeed she did. Everyone thought we were the most well-dressed dinner table around. Well, you guys want a matching set, do you? It would be nice. But maybe it's not that simple? Maybe there are options we haven't considered. Perhaps we could even consider recycling. Now that we've moved this side of fifty and we see the impact of our waste. That's a good idea, Mum. And while we're on the subject, what about the old dining table and chairs? We've been meaning to change them for years now. Absolutely, let's prioritize that. Hey, why don't we plan a weekend project? We could sort everything out, buy the matching cutlery if we decide it's needed, and even get new furniture. I'm in! I might even recommend some local places that sell handmade or second-hand if you're interested in recycling. That sounds wonderful. How about we finalize the plans over the next few weeks? If you think it will bring me back into some active life, then count me in too. Yes, making some changes would be good for everyone, I imagine. I can start looking for local furniture stores and see if I can find what we're after. And maybe we can all pitch in to help with the project. That sounds good. Let's make sure we all contribute based on our abilities. Definitely. You know, change can be good. For the house, for each other. You're all doing so well. I'm just... I'm proud of our little family. We're doing great, aren't we? Absolutely. We're still a family, and that's what matters most. Right. So, to recap, we'll plan a successful project for the dining table, cutlery, and possibly some other bits and pieces we've been wanting to change.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my day? I discovered today that the new accounting system they introduced last quarter will require even more paperwork than before. I swear, sometimes I wonder if they're doing it to keep us busy because they can't think of anything better to do. Oh really? What kind of accounting system? I don't know, honey, but it looks like a never-ending maze. All very fancy and high-tech, but at the end of the day, it's still just numbers and paperwork. Well, numbers are fun! I just had a class about adding numbers at school today. That's what I love about you, even in simple things you find something exciting. Now, let’s talk about something fun. What do you think about our skiing trip next month? The snow has already started falling, and it’s going to be a white Christmas, hopefully. Oh yes! I want to ski! Can I ski next to you or Daddy? Absolutely, you can ski next to both of us if you want. We'll make sure to stay close and help you while you learn. And Daddy has promised to carry you around a bit if you're feeling tired, right, dear? Speaker_2's partner: Absolutely, we'll make sure you're always in sight and safe. And maybe we can even make some snow angels and have a snowball fight. How about that? Yay! Snowball fight! But can we also build a snowman? I want to build the biggest one together! Of course we can! You can be in charge of decorating it with small stones and sticks we find around. We can also take it slow and safe, so you don't get too cold or tired. Speaker_2’s partner: We can make sure there’s hot chocolate waiting for you whenever you want a break. Either from skiing or building. Okay! But first, can we have a hot chocolate now? With marshmallows! Alright, one hot chocolate before we start planning more snow fun. How does that sound, dear? YAY! Hot chocolate with marshmallows! I was hoping you'd say that. And... ...while we're at it, let's discuss the finer details of the trip. Dates, transport, accommodation... Maybe we can also make it a bit educational and tour some interesting places when we're not skiing. Speaker_2’s partner: Sounds like a plan, successful holiday planning session in one!

Yo, how was maths homework yesterday? Did you finish it? Yeah, it was alright. Had to use algebra which I normally don't enjoy, but it wasn't too bad. Made sure to double check my work, didn't want any surprises like last time. Hehe, questions again this week? Going over cones or something? Yeah, we've moved on to circles. It makes sense but sometimes I'm just like, "Why are we doing this?" But I guess it helps us understand how trigonometry works right? Exactly! I just hate it when we have to do formulas. It feels so robotic. But at least with maths, I can see where it applies in real life. It just sucks when it doesn't. Right, but when you need to design or understand a project, it's useful. Hence why we have to learn it. Speaking of useful, I heard food tech is a fun class? Oh, it's my favourite! We get to actually make things we can eat. It's like chemistry and cooking mixed. Yeah! But last week we had this argument about if we should study Spanish for our GCSEs. Oh, did you decide anything? Not yet. I think it would be interesting and helpful if we want to travel, but I'm not sure. It would be so helpful, wouldn't it? I mean, it's not just a language in Britain, but really all over the world. Definitely. And jobs these days, especially in tech and business, they often require it. But it's tough to keep the motivation now, when it feels so far away. True, it’s hard to see the future applications. But I bet if you try it, you'll love it, and it'll be worth it. You think? I might’ve had enough of languages already with school, but maybe you're right. You never know until you try. It might be something you enjoy. Plus if I start now, it’ll definitely help when we're revising for our GCSEs next year. Makes sense to get a head start. Exactly! And thinking about it, could even help you stand out in job applications or university if you choose to do further education. University, yeah... that feels like a lifetime away. Haha, I remember when I thought that about secondary school. But here we are, almost there. True. We better get our grades sorted then.

Ah, I was just going over some of the latest film releases. I have to say, the number of new releases is quite overwhelming. It sure is! I mean, there's just not enough time to watch everything that comes out. Still, I do try to keep up with some of the top ones. Which one did you last watch? It was that new sci-fi film, 'Interstellar Now'. Absolutely incredible! I've got that one coming up on my list. I've heard mixed reviews, but it's supposed to be pretty visually stunning. It is, dear. I was really impressed. The visual effects were just out of this world, even for a film about space. Ah, yes - "out of this world" - perfect phrase for it. I imagine most of those effects relied heavily on CGI, but it's done so well you wouldn't know otherwise. Right! And the scientific accuracy they claim to have got right, for the most part, really helps to enrich the story. Oh, absolutely. I remember seeing 'Gravity' a few years back and it's the same. You feel like you're right there with the characters. Indeed. Speaking of which, I also really enjoyed 'Parasite' by Bong Joon-ho. Amazing piece of filmmaking. It really tore apart the genres in a great way. Oh really? I haven't had a chance to see that one yet. And what genre did that play with? I know it doesn't come across as clearly cut. Well, it's predominantly a social commentary but it masquerades as a thriller in the beginning and then veers into satire and satire's comedy in the latter half. I see. I'll definitely have to check it out then. It seems quite complex but intriguing. It’s quite a masterpiece actually. And the fact that it won so many awards really shows how well received it was globally. I suppose that's another thing. All these international films just keep getting better, don't they? And it's not just about Hollywood anymore. No, the film industry has diversified so much. It's more global now and it's fantastic to see all the different perspectives being put forward. Indeed, it is. And yet, don't you sometimes find that you still wish you could catch up with more of the old classics as well? Oh, absolutely! There’s always something timeless about older films.

Ah, Mum, it's so lovely to have you here. We've not had time for a proper catch-up in ages. How are you really doing? I'm fine, dear. These grey days can be quite challenging for someone who loves the outdoors, but I manage. How's life treating you? You've been working so hard with the language teaching, haven't you? It's been quite a journey, Mum. There's always something new to learn and I love meeting all the different students. But it can be stressful at times, especially with the new regulations and all. Oh, I'm sure. I've had my fair share of stress at the court, dear. There are days when you're in early and then the judge says the case is adjourned. You're waiting there for hours but of course, you can't leave even if the case isn't going on. It's a quiet kind of stress, but stressful nonetheless. That sounds challenging, Mum. I can imagine. But at least it's a steady income, which we're lucky to have. Indeed. I hope you're managing financially, dear? I know this job isn't the most lucrative, but at least it's secure. We’re managing, thank you for asking. Actually, I've been considering a part-time job over the summer to increase our savings a bit. Maybe some language tutoring or even pet sitting. That sounds like a good plan. Speaking of plans, how about a family trip over the summer? We could go to your parents' old cottage in the Derbyshire countryside and spend some quality time together. That sounds wonderful! I'd love that. We could even drive up there. Except, dear, I haven't driven in a while. I've mostly been using public transport and walking, so it might feel a bit rusty. Don't worry about that. Your father used to say, "A licence is like a driving licence for life." You've had one for years now! We could even borrow your father's old car for the trip. That would make things easier. I suppose I should start revising my driving skills before we leave. Exactly! It's not like you ever had a problem with it anyway. And we can always practice locally before heading North. Good idea. Maybe I could take a refresher course just in case, or ask one of my students to give me a few driving lessons.

I've got to say, it's been quite an adventure so far. The students are lovely, but the teaching load is intense. Do you think they have even less of a concept of time here than we do? Ha! I think so. Just this morning, one of my modules questions if we could just extend the due date by a fortnight and I had to remind him "No, that means you have exactly five days left, right now, as we speak." Oh my. That's so... British of me, isn't it? But we've grown, haven't we? From our initial culture shock to... well, I still stumble with the language sometimes. Oh, you're not the only one. Every time I try to order something from the "supermarket" they still look at me with this puzzled expression. It's amazing how quickly you forget language nuances. True, true. But it's lovely to see the similarities and differences. And the people here are so kind. Almost like every interaction's a little social contract. I hope we don't scare them off with our... this is it, our British formalities? I think most of them are too polite to say anything. Besides, we've made quite a few friends at work. I'm even hoping to invite some over for dinner at our place soon. Ah, that'd be lovely! We could try some of those recipes we discovered. I fell in love with that spicy Sichuan dish at that restaurant we went to last week. Oh, I know! That was amazing. But let's not forget the awful "Western" food we've tried too. There's a reason we stick to the local cuisine here. More spicy chicken, ramen, and dumplings for me then. But it's fun exploring the different flavours. Yes, definitely. And speaking of exploration... While you were dealing with the teaching today, I had a look around the nearby shopping area. There's this quirky store that sells these amazing silk scarves for a decent price. Oh, truly? I've been meaning to treat myself to something local for some of my students. Maybe show them a bit of Britain right here. Exactly! It'll make a unique gift. Plus, I think you'll really love it. The colours and patterns they have... That sounds perfect. Can you take me there? Might as well get a bit of shopping done.

Alright, girls! Let's move on from books for now. Who'd like to tell us about what they're planning to do after dinner? Ooh! Ooh! I want to tell! After dinner, Aunt Sarah is going to do face paint because we asked her to! She's going to make me into a unicorn! Yeah, I want a dragon! Can she make me a dragon too? Well, she'll do her best, okay? But first, let's talk about your haircuts. Do we need to organise that for you two in the week? Might have to wrap up by 5. But why can't Aunt Sarah just do it? Yeah, and do my hair too? Well, it's just that Aunt Sarah is quite good at this sort of thing, but maybe we should ask permission from your parents first, okay? Yeah... okay. And you, while the rest of us figure out the haircut situation, do you want to help me with the photoshoot plans? It's going to be quite fun, promise! A photo shoot? With costumes? Can I be in it too? Of course! What do you want to be? A princess! Or a fairy! Or both! Let's discuss that when everyone is together. But for now, shall we go through what's happening after dinner? We've got the face paint, right? And it'll be nice if we can sort out some other activities for you two before bedtime. I want to play a board game after dinner. Can we? Definitely. What game are you in the mood for? I like snakes and ladders. It's fun! How about you? What would you like to play? I want to play dress up! Can we still do that after dinner? You will get to dress up. You'll get your unicorn face paint, and we can set up some dress-up clothes and props. Yessss! I'll choose the best unicorn dress! So, let's recap. After dinner, we've got face paint, possibly haircuts with parental permission, a board game for one of you, and a dress-up session for the other. Can I please please please please be the unicorn first? I want to be a dragon when it's my turn! Alright, alright. We'll make sure you both get a turn being whatever you like. Now, let's all help with dinner.

Yo, how was your morning? Mine was a bit of a bumpy ride. Got up super early, tried to do some last-minute studying for my exam tomorrow, and then of course, the bus was late. You know how it is. Same! But hey, at least we've got this lovely sunshine isn't it? I mean, totally puts me in a better mood. And, I have to say, King's canteen actually got a decent chicken tikka last week. You should try it. Right, let me write that down. I swear, the highlight of my week is lazy Sunday brunch at home but today is just day-in-day-out nothing really stands out. Yeah, same. I mean, apart from that one really good lecture last week. Our lecturer for criminology was super interesting. He started talking about how crime is actually a cultural concept so sometimes it's just society defining what's right and wrong. That's so fascinating! Makes you think. And it's funny because it also applies to uni rules. I mean, what's a 'reasonable time'? Is it 11am, 12 pm or whatever? It all depends on whose society you're in. True! I think the university should clearly define that. I mean, we can't all be bright and chirpy at 8:30 am, can we? Definitely not. I've been trying really hard to keep up with my uni life, but it's not easy. You working on any projects or anything? Not really. I've just been reading for that exam. The only 'project' I've been working on is getting my notes done in time. More power to you! I was just thinking, maybe we could do something for the weekend? You know, ease off a bit. Like go to a pub meet-up or something? That sounds great! I've heard about this pub in Kingston that supposedly has really good food and a chill atmosphere. We could check that out. Yeah, and besides, it's been a week since our last chill session. We definitely need a meme review and a catch-up session. Definitely! And speaking of memes, have you seen the latest ones about procrastination? They're hilarious! Oh yeah! Totally makes me feel less bad about doing everything late. But at the same time, I know that can't be healthy. Yeah, balance is key.

Yo, lads and lasses. What d'ye think about's holidays? I'm really looking forward to mine. Well, I'm still sorting out my plans, but I've heard great things about this place in Cornwall. Oh, Cornwall is stunning – I love the beaches there. Absolutely, and the food? Bloody brilliant, innit? Have you both tried any proper Cornish pasties before? Yeah, innit. The best! There's this one place near Falmouth. You should try it if you ever go to Cornwall, Stu. Right, Cornish pasties, seafood, that's the life. And proper Cornish cream teas - you cannot beat 'em! Yeah, but I suppose you can’t have holidays without a bit of exploration, bru? True dat. I mean, we should also check out the local spot around here, innit? Offa's Dyke, anyone? Been there before, but it's really nice for a hike. Yeah, it is. And what about the TV? Anyone catch that new series that’s coming out? Stunned at the moment, so hasn’t had much time for TV. Oh, I’ve been meaning to watch ‘The English,’ I heard it's great. Yeah, really good. One of my mates is an actor and they said they love filming it. Hmm, I should check that out. What about Netflix or BBC iPlayer? Either, but I think it’s on BBC. Maybe we could have a TV night together? Yeah, that could be nice. Okay, that’s a plan then. Next week or so? Sounds good. Just need to check my schedule. Yeah sure, I can join. Cool. I’ll bring some food, something traditional like fish 'n' chips or just general nosh, take your pick. That sounds like a plan! Can I suggest getting some proper Yorkshire puddings and gravy? Yeah, definitely! That’s the real deal. Always love a good Yorkshire. Nice. So, final plans – TV night next week, likely Friday or Sunday. I’m free this Sunday. I'm likely free that evening too. Then it's a done deal. See you all then, make it a happening! Definitely, we’ll keep it going till late, no doubt. So, no going home early on Sunday, right? Not unless you're going to take some leftovers! Haha, true, but I might need an early night unless they're fish 'n' chips. LOL, fair. But let's hope we're all up for a late one.

Right, so I was thinking we might take a trip to London soon. Took my granddaughter there a few years back and she loved it. The noise, the people, the food... the whole experience. Made me feel young again, you know? Oh, London! It's a wonderful place, isn't it? I'd love to go back and see the sights again. I suppose the trouble with taking a trip to London is the cost, though. Isn't it? Nowadays, I'd need to budget for petrol, for food, for... well, everything really. Well, if you book ahead, you can save a bit. I've been using websites like Booking.com and TripAdvisor to book our last couple of London trips. And we like to stop by Buckingham Palace, take a walk through Hyde Park, sample some food at markets like Camden. Ah, yes. I imagine the food would be a treat. Perhaps we could go to one of those nice restaurants by the river. Make a proper day of it, you know? Or even spend a night or two there. Perhaps we could even take advantage of any discounts? I remember this one youth hostel we stayed at in Cornwall a few years back. Not exactly the Ritz, but fun and very affordable. Maybe something similar in London? There are plenty of budget options, really. You could look at staying in a hostel or using Airbnb. There are also some really good deals if you book trains or buses in advance. You're right, of course. An early bird catches the worm and all that. But you know what I'd really like us to do? Visit a horse racing event. I used to go to the flat races at Newmarket, but I haven't been for ages. Maybe there's something in or near London? There are a few racecourses around the capital. I'd have to check the calendar to see when the next couple of events are. Oh, horses and racing! That takes me back to my childhood. My grandfather used to take me to the races. I must admit, it's a bit more of a social event for me now rather than a serious interest, but there's something quite special about it. Absolutely. The atmosphere is great. Besides, it's a good opportunity to see some of the countryside around London. Speaking of countryside, we should consider looking at some horse riding centers around London if you're keen.

So, how's everything going with the little one? Oh, you know. It's been quite an adventure. The early days were chaotic, but now she's getting the hang of things. You wouldn't believe how different each day is. I can imagine! You know, questions are always coming up and it seems like a new challenge every day, right? Absolutely! Feeding is the current big one right now. Breastfeeding is proving tougher than I expected and it's so emotionally draining when things don't go smoothly. I remember those days! And yes, it is emotionally challenging. But remember, every baby is different and it's normal to have ups and downs in early feeding. It just takes patience and support. Thanks, that really helps. I feel like I'm the only one who's struggling. No, no, it happens to every new mum. Trust me. But you also know your mum is always here to help when you need her. And if there are issues, professional support from healthcare specialists or lactation consultants can really make a difference as well. That's true and it's good advice. I guess I just need to remind myself of that. You know, feeding aside, the biggest surprise for me has been just the entire routine of a new baby. It feels like the baby's the one in charge sometimes. Ah, totally. The whole concept of time becomes so different, doesn't it? But isn't it amazing how quickly they grow and learn? It is. But it's also bittersweet. Just the other day I was thinking, it's already been three months and that feels like just a blink of an eye. It's just the beginning. And it will go quickly. She'll be walking in no time. True. She'll be our little human in no time. It does make me feel a bit overwhelmed sometimes, though. I miss our old routine but I know I wouldn't trade this for anything. It’s normal to miss your old life a bit, but you're forging a completely new experience. And I know you're doing an amazing job. Thanks, sis. Your support means a lot to me. Again, if you could use any help, just let me know. I'd be more than happy to take her for a while and give you some time off.

Good morning all. How are we all feeling today? Good morning. Feeling pretty well, thanks for asking. Just about to start my day with a big mug of tea. Got some work on my to-do list, including a meeting later to discuss the new project plan. Morning! I had a bit of a late night last night brainstorming ideas for a new campaign at work, so I'm a bit tired but I'm feeling pretty productive right now. Now, shall I start on getting the kids ready for school or would anyone like another cup of tea before we get moving? Oh, we could all do with a brew. I’ve been up since 5 with the early morning shift, so I’m starting to feel a bit sluggish. Speaking of which, what about the dog? Did we remember to walk him last night? I should've done that, but it slipped my mind. I want to get into the routine of walking him before the children leave for school. Ah, that's a good plan. Since we're already talking about it, would anyone mind walking him while I or Jess take care of the breakfast? I can scramble some eggs or toast some bread. I can walk the dog. It'll be a nice bit of fresh air for me too. That's so kind of you, Jess. Thanks. I can get the breakfasts started then. Ah, and while we're at it, could we sort out who's doing the bins and recycling in the evening? I missed last week, didn’t we? I'll do that tonight. No problem at all. Great! Well, I'll get the dog. Who's up for finding some new recipes for dinner tonight? There's been a bit of a chicken rut lately. Jess has been raving about this new cookbook she got. I can lend it to you. That's a good idea. We should try something new and maybe even involve the kids if they're not too busy. Speaking of which, is there anything new at school for them? Well, for my daughter in primary school, she’s really into this new reading program they’ve started so she’s been coming home with books all the time. That's brilliant! Is it something they could use some help with? Maybe we could set aside an hour or so in the evening where we all sit down and read together.

Yo, I can't believe we have another week of school before the holidays. I'm so over tests and GCSEs. Yeah, me too. I'm worried I'm going to fail my maths test next week. Just relax, you're fine! We've practiced this kind of questions so many times. Plus, let's talk about something more fun, like the Ed Sheeran concert we're going to this Christmas! I know! He's amazing live. But speaking of fun stuff, how is that stamp-collecting project going? Oh, okay. I've been buying new stamps for it at St Mary's Market. I've been really into the science ones. There's one with the periodic table on it. Brilliant! I love how the designs are. And the names of the elements. Hence my love of chemistry. It's amazing how much you can learn from stamps. Exactly! Plus, there's a special one for Cambridge University too. It's so cool. I heard they released some new ones recently. Did you get that one about the Cambridge Botanic Garden? Yeah, I did! Plants are pretty awesome. Reminds me of our own garden at home. I've been helping mum with the Christmas decorations. She's trying to make it look like a winter wonderland. Ah, nice. I'm not sure I'd know where to start with Christmas gardening. It's not that hard actually. It’s all about adding some evergreens and fairy lights. Mum said we might even get a real Christmas tree this year. That would be so good! You know, I've been wanting to learn more about plants and gardening. Seems like the perfect opportunity. You should ask your dad about it. He loves gardening. Maybe he could teach you or we could even do a joint project over the holidays. That's a great idea! Maybe we can plan something next week before school finishes. Definitely, let’s do that. By the way, have you prepared for our uniform inspection on Friday? I've washed all my uniform last weekend. Hopefully that's enough. You could use a quick touch-up with an iron if you're being thorough. Good point. Maybe I should do that tomorrow. Definitely! Let's prep together, maybe over my house. We could even talk more about plants and that gardening project while we iron. That sounds like a plan.

Right, so I had this strange idea of using a rat puppet. I have no idea why. I think it was something I saw on telly. Thought it'd be a good icebreaker, you know? You two remember anything like that from your childhood? Rat puppet? That's quite the idea. I don't remember anything like that. I wish I could think as freely as you, John. I'd probably laugh till my sides hurt. Well, you never know. It could be a hit, you never know. Maybe we can have our own little amateur theatre with rat puppets and all. And handbell ringing as our music. "Two little rats, playing in the park..." And we'd travel on buses, bringing our show to the world. Brilliant. We'll travel far and wide. I'm sure this is a decision that changes lives. You know what they say, right? All of life's a stage. Speaking of stages... have we made an appointment for our eyes' check-up? Oh, silly me. I completely forgot about that. Yeah, I spoke to the optician and they have us booked for next Thursday. But it's good you reminded the both of us. We're not getting any younger, and our eyes aren't getting any better. Definitely, I just thought, maybe we could do it together. Grab our rat puppets and head over to the opticians. It'll be fun. I'd like that. It sure beats sitting at home doing nothing. Plus, I need to get new glasses. I've been having trouble reading the small print on buses. And maybe, afterwards, we can have a bus journey. Or perhaps you can ring the bells and entertain us. I love that idea, ringing bells and using a rat puppet. We'll be the happiest bus passengers. But first things first, let's book that appointment. And this time, let's not forget. Don't worry, I've got it down in my diary. See you both next Thursday then. Maybe we can have a tea and a chat after? That'd be lovely. We can even discuss our rat puppet show's storyline, while we're at it. I can see it now, a duet of rat puppets, a single handbell, and a bus journey playing out in our granny flat. Brilliant! It starts here. Every journey begins with a single step.

Alright, so what was your idea about how we're going to spend the day in Venice? I've got a few hours after this and then I need to head back for a lecture. Well, it just so happens that this café is one of the places I used to frequent back in the day when I was studying here. There's a whole lot to see and do, but let's start with a quick tour of the Dorsoduro area. The Campo Santa Margherita is still my favorite spot for a casual coffee and get a feel for the local rhythms. You'll really see Venezia's soul, if you know what I mean. Sounds perfect. And then what? You know I like my tours to have a bit of adventure. Ah, yes - adventure. Well, I suppose you could say that even the locals here find exploration exciting! After the Dorsoduro area, if you're brave enough, we can take a vaporetto to Murano. You can see the famous glass-making on the island. It's changed quite a bit since I left, but the essence remains. Brave enough, ha! Alright, I'll give the vaporetto a go if it means seeing the famous glass. What about food and drink in Venice? I'm all about trying local things. Ah, that's a good question. Food's a big part of Venetian life. Honestly, as a local, it's always tricky to pick one place that's really authentic. But I can recommend Al Covo. They have fantastic cicchetti - that's a type of Venetian snack, very similar to tapas. And if you're around in the evenings, you must try a spritz, but make sure it's made with Select instead of Aperol or Campari. The Select gives it a unique, a bit sweeter taste. Circehti and spritz it is then! And do you think we should try any of the local cafes for a coffee or changing the pace from Italian coffee to espresso? Definitely. You should try a classic Venetian coffee experience. Caffè Florian in Piazza San Marco, although touristy, has an old charm to it. For a local experience though, try Caffè Quadri, it's right next to the Basilica and almost as old. But if you want something real unique, we should consider Caffe del Doge. It's not far from here and has a cozy, local feel.

So, I hear you've seen some of the latest first-class's fitness equipment at your new job. What are you thinking about joining the gym where I go after seeing what they have at Bupa? Oh, I really like Bupa's gym now, but I have to say, your gym is pretty neat too. I've had friends who have joined and they've totally hit the jackpot with their progress. Yeah, right? I was thinking of recommending it to Sam too. They've recently revamped the studio classes and it's amazing. That sounds great! I'm actually struggling a bit with my current gym as it's getting pretty crowded these days. It's really hard fitting in early morning yoga sessions. So, Sam was telling me that in the past when your ex started working at the gym, the rush got even worse. Ha! Exactly! It's all his fault, right? No, just kidding! But seriously, the gym has become overcrowded since his friends started working out there. Heh, I hope he's not causing any trouble? I haven't seen him for ages, actually. Not to my knowledge, no. He seemed pretty chilled while I was there. Though, I might be more chilled around him after we stopped seeing each other, can't say the same for some of his mates. I see... A mixed bag of reactions, huh? Speaking of which, I've been trying really hard to keep up with my gym routine, but it's been tough with work. How so? Well, as a project co-ordinator, work can get really hectic. I find myself stuck at my desk for the entire day. Sometimes I just can't get together the motivation to go after work. That totally sucks. I've dealt with that too, but then I realised that if I just get changed into my gym gear, it's like I'm already changing my mindset. It helps motivate me to leave work behind. That does make sense. Plus, I need to start eating better. I've been ordering Nandos for takeaway so much, it's not healthy for anyone! Oh, I know right. We can totally go healthier... but this peri-peri chicken is like... I know, I know! It's like a vice! We should get something healthier then. How about we arrange something fun for the weekend?

Ah, I hear you've seen some of the latest news from France. I was just today talking to a few French friends who've come over for the holidays. They say the land prices are through the roof down there, but somehow still manage to have one of the most beautiful countryside and villages. Indeed, France has a unique kind of charm. You've likely heard of the French bureaucrats, they're a breed of their own. It makes one wonder how things get done at all! Absolutely, and it's not just bureaucrats either. You have anarchists, artists, entrepreneurs - it's a fascinating mix, I suppose, but sometimes a bit chaotic. However, they seem to thrive nonetheless. It's a country of extremes, that's for certain. But then again, so is our own Britain in many ways. I've always been fascinated by France's position as a bridge between the north and the south of Europe. The influences from various regions and historical events make it so culturally rich. That's true. It's fascinating that similar characteristics in people can lead to such different societal structures and approaches to enterprise. Speaking of enterprise, I'm curious about the impact on the British visitors to France. Have they found it different from running a business here? Some have certainly mentioned the benefits of lower tax in certain industries, but others complain about the red tape, not unlike the French themselves. It seems to be a trade off for the quality of life. Indeed, it's always about finding a balance in life, isn’t it? One never fully understands the intricacies of another country until you've lived there or taken the time to learn about it properly. Absolutely. Speaking of learning, have you heard about the Chichester Cathedral spire? It's been in the news the past few days. Apparently the architect was one Porden, a rather renowned figure. Ah yes! I remember. The spire is one of the tallest in England. It's a great example of our architectural heritage but also brings into focus the changing attitudes towards preservation and restoration. Right. I think there was an open day for the diocese or something like that. I might have a flyer somewhere. And they're also planning a photo exhibition on the restoration work. That's wonderful! I recall when they renovated the North transept back in the 90s.

Yo, lads, check out these dumplings! They's look tasty. Yeah, they do! I was thinking we could order more, this food is the real deal. Agreed! I love it here, the atmosphere, the staff, and of course, the food. Totally! But, have you guys seen the homework we've been getting lately? It's crazy, I'm just hoping the school year ends soon. Yeah, keeps coming right? I swear, it's like they're trying to stuff our heads full of more information every day. Honestly, I just can't focus lately. I was just looking at online comics to try and take my mind off it all. You guys into comic books or something? I'm not really into comics, but I do watch a lot of anime. The action scenes and stuff are pretty cool sometimes. Same, I watch a little bit of anime, but I spend most of my free time on the PlayStation these days. Sometimes I think I should focus more on school work, but it's hard to stick to it when everything else is so much more fun. True. Where did you all study while the 'Rona was on? Like, how was that for you? Well, for me, it was a bit of an adventure. We had online lessons for a while, but I'd say it's better to be back in school. It's much more social, you know? I know what you mean. Online learning was painful. Plus, doesn't feel the same as being in the classroom. For sure. There were times when we'd do all these Zoom calls and it would feel like a TV show or something. More like a joke than actual learning. Speaking of jokes, do you remember when Mr. Jackson accidentally fell into the sink while trying to demonstrate something in chemistry? Oh my god, yes! It was hilarious. It was one of those moments where everyone was like – should we laugh or be shocked? I was there! I thought it was pretty funny too. And later, we all made a meme of it and sent it around the class. Yeah, and he just played along with it the next day. He's actually pretty cool. I wish all teachers were like that. True that. But between you and me, we need to figure out our diet. Someone mentioned there's a new healthy eating trend that's gaining traction.

Ah, I can't believe how much of a mess we've got here. Look at this cabinet; it's been filled up since who knows when. I don't think we've even opened the tea box down there since before I retired. Oh, absolutely. It's time for a bit of a clear out. Maybe we can get some new items to replace the old ones? Or donate some of it to charity? And while we're at it, can we plan how to better organize our space? Maybe it's time for those new 'smart home' items to become part of our routine. Smart home? What’s that even mean? Ah, our younger generation - oh, Jonathan, I suppose you’re a bit of an expert now? Well, not really, but sometimes Ronny talks about how our school got some new tech last year that can pretty much control everything from his phone. That's great! For us, it could be about making our day-to-day lives easier. Like automatic lights, perhaps? Exactly. And don't even get me started on the efficiency and energy-saving aspects. We could also consider a digital calendar for our family events and holidays. I love that, especially for something like planning a birthday in advance. We really need to start thinking ahead, don't we? We have Jonathan's birthday coming up soon. But it's not just about the tech, you know? Just last weekend, I helped Darlington Women’s Group design a new logo for their branding. You know, it's all about reflecting who you are and where you come from. Which reminds me, we should also think about rebranding our own space here. Maybe update the furniture, or even the entire look of the place. It's been the same for years. Oh, yes, that would be lovely! But moving house would be a whole different task, wouldn't it? Moving house would indeed be a big step, and it might be a good opportunity for a mass clear out. But we’d need to plan this very carefully. Actually, Darlington has some fantastic new developments out by our old house. They even have community gardens and that could be a great change for us. We could really revitalize our lives with that kind of change. Wait, what about moving away from Newcastle? I’d miss my friends and the school.

Yo, so I'm kinda over PE at the moment, can's anybody have a perfect school day; every GCSE option's got its downsides. Thoughts? Definitely unrealistic. You can't have a day without at least one class you dislike. Like the clarinet, I swear, sometimes I just questions if this was a good GCSE option. But I guess it’s part of the balancing out part. HAHA, I'm right there with you. Speaking of GCSEs though, have you decided what jobs you even want to do? I still haven’t a clue. Not really, but I'm considering jobs related to English Literature. Maybe even try my hand at being a you tuber or a blogger. Though, let’s be honest, is that really what we want to read about in the news when we grow up? Famous people making bogs and bloggers being famous? Fair point! But, I mean, there are a lot of famous you tubers and bloggers out there. Some are even big names now! Maybe there’s potential in this kind of thing, if you can make content that people love or find useful. True, but maybe it's just a phase for now. Plus, I’ve heard they often have to work really grueling hours while the 'glamour' of the job isn't as substantial as people think. I hadn't thought of it like that. But I guess, whether it's as a you tube or a bogger or something entirely different, it's all about being really good at what you do, right? Exactly! Plus, I don't think anyone can realistically say that it's a perfect duty the whole time. As for famous people, do you think we'll ever be as famous or just as cool? Maybe not, but who cares? Our own Cambridge school, for instance, has given us so many opportunities already. Isn’t that cool enough? Plus, we can make our own history regardless of fame. True, but changing the world from Cambridge sure sounds cool. Maybe we can be like those famous people who use their platforms to bring some positive change. Like who, though? Us, as kids, trying to make change might be a meme waiting to happen, But still, could be interesting. And if you think about it, just being friends like this right now is pretty cool in itself. I mean, who knows where we'll all end up or what we'll do, but we're thinking about it together.

Ah, marvellous weekend. I managed to get out into the countryside and spotted a wild hare, quite rare to see them around here. You lot who don't live in the city might think it’s exciting but it just reminds me of all the hours spent searching for something to occupy my time outside of the house. Come on, Tom, even wildlife has its charm. It's better than watching the same TV shows I've watched 10 times. Right, let me not get too excited here but seeing that hare actually made my day. I’m glad you enjoyed it. Though, let’s switch gears to something slightly more modern. Do any of you still struggle with modern computer software? Oh dear, now you talk about something that makes my head buzz. Last week, I tried to watch a particular documentary on my new tablet but the app kept glitching. I barely managed to figure it out. That's nothing compared to my troubles with online banking. It changes so frequently, I feel left behind. I can relate. My grandkids are always trying to 'teach' me to use these newfangled apps but by the time I've got the hang of it, they've already moved on to something else. Well, as a lecturer, I ensure my students are comfortable with these technologies. Maybe I can hold some informal workshops here if you'd like? That’s kind of you, sweetheart. But to be honest, all these upgrades make me feel like I’m in over my head. I’d appreciate that. But speaking of over our heads, remember when car engines were simpler and didn't have all these fancy sensors? Ah, yes. I used to take pride in fixing my old Ford Zodiac's engine on the weekends. Can't do that these days. Well, cars have evolved indeed, but that doesn't mean you can’t enjoy them. And most modern cars have built-in navigation and entertainment systems which almost makes them like mini-computers on wheels. You just need to know how to use them. Oh, great. More thinking required. Sure, but I suppose it’s a trade-off. No more getting stranded because of a faulty distributor or timing belt. True, but I miss the simplicity of tinkering around in a garage on a sunny Saturday. We could at least watch some YouTube tutorials together, see if that helps.

Ah, speaking of schools, I used to teach at the school's youth club back in my day. It was a real eye-opener, you know. Had to deal with so many different kids, all of various backgrounds but somehow still managed to keep them all in line. That's fascinating! I had a bit of a similar experience when I was a childminder, though it was quite a while ago now. I remember the little terrors I had to deal with as much as I enjoyed them, though! You two were a bit too hands-on with the kids, weren't you? I stick to the books. I've always found it easier to just stay in class and teach. Yes, well, sometimes the kids need a bit more than just from behind a desk, don't they? What's that phrase? "For every minute spent organizing, an hour is earned"? I reckon that applies to looking after children as well. Absolutely spot on, mate! And these days, it seems like the schools are so bogged down with their own bureaucracy, or as I like to say, "silly uniform nonsense". One moment they're telling you to wear this, the next they're saying it's wrong. Where's the consistency in schools these days? Well, I think it's also about the changing world. As a teacher, I've seen so many new rules and policies come into play, all for the betterment, no doubt. It can be a bit overwhelming at times, but progress is never easy, is it? Absolutely right. And then there are the wardrobe issues. I swear, every time my granddaughter goes to school, she needs new clothes because "it's not in style" or "it's too last season". The worry those things put a family through, it's a right old headache! Oh, absolutely! The last time my own daughter said she needed a new uniform for school, I was ready to scream. But then she came home and we did a little sort out of her old clothes – more than enough for her school needs. A good old fashioned clear out does wonders! Reminds me of when I was a kid. Our wardrobes were always minimal because the money wasn't there to spend on clothes. But we made do and I've no complaints about that. That's the spirit. Speaking of making do, have you both noticed the quality of deliverymen these days?

I've never seen Cambridge so white! We've got enough snow today to make a decent snowman. Snow in the UK is always a surprise, right? I've managed to squeeze in a bit of gardening this morning, though. The plants do love the cold! Speaking of plants, have you been watching "Come Dine With Me" lately? There was one episode recently where the contestant's garden won them extra points. They had this beautifully manicured lawn and perfectly arranged flowers, nothing like our little patch... I have to say, I've been avoiding "Come Dine With Me". After a certain point, the tensions and pretentiousness can get a bit much. But the garden bit is always a nice touch - though making a DIY garden might be a bit of a challenge here in this snow! True, creative gardening seems out of the question when it's knee-deep in snow. But hey, at least we can plan ahead - like those next couple of weeks, when we might be able to actually get this garden into shape. Planning? What's on the agenda then? A new 'Come Dine With Me'-inspired garden makeover? More like a bit of pre-holiday planning. But while we're on the subject... A couple of our friends are organizing a stag party next month in Wales, and I've been asked to help with the arrangements. I was thinking maybe we could also plan a little getaway trip for us, post-hen party. That sounds like a plan! Except, we've been meaning to design our own 'Come Dine With Me' night soon. More garden festivities, maybe a BBQ, if the weather cooperates. Both sound like fabulous ideas! So, next week, after the hen party, let's meet up and decide on the menu and theme for our 'Come Dine With Me' party. And after that, we should start looking at holiday plans. Have you given any thought to where you want to go? Honestly, the stag party is more of an upsetting factor right now. Wondering if we could just do a quick weekend break somewhere, maybe Cornwall? The weather there is usually a bit more cooperative. Cornwall does sound lovely. And it's not too far if we drive. We can plan a road trip and... explore the local cuisine! Exactly! A holiday away from all the trappings of 'Come Dine With Me'.

Right, now I'm going to make sure to put beans on's Dad's plate. He's nearly 80 and he needs all the protein he can get, what with his old chicken bones breaking all the time. Oh, beans are good for that now, aren't they? I remember when I was working as a childminder, the kids and I would make those big bean stews. It was so simple and everyone loved it. Now, don't start talking about childminding. You're retired! You get to enjoy dinner without worrying about how much time you've spent in the kitchen, unlike us, lecturers who are lazy enough to order a takeaway from time to time. Hey, I've got a student journalist down to research for a piece about the rise of takeaways in our village. It's interesting how even the older folks here are going for that convenience. It's a funny old world, innit? Now everyone wants convenience over tradition. Back in my day, we'd make our own meals from scratch. But times change. Though I still can't understand why people would prefer a takeaway over a proper roast dinner with all the trimmings! It's different for busy people, I reckon. The modern pace of life. You need quick meals. Still, I think the secret to a good life is to make time for the simple things, like making your own food. That's true, but I think it's also about balance. I do enjoy trying new things, like these fancy food boxes they deliver now. It’s all about convenience and exploration, right? Plus, it gives me ideas for my cooking classes. I think it's about how we grow food and our attitude to it, isn’t it? People’s relationship with food has really changed. Now it's measured in terms of calories, nutrition, and, of course, time. I noticed a lot of my students say they can't cook because they’ve never learned but they are interested if it's quick and easy. That's a shame. You can't just sit down to a pre-made meal and call it a family dinner. What’s the fun in that? Well, it's not all so dire. I’ve seen some of the younger folk here take a great interest in traditional cooking, experimenting with recipes.

Oh, Dad, this dinner was definitely worth waiting for. Your shepherd's pie is just as incredible as I remember. Can't complain about that, right? There's nothing like a home-cooked meal to remind us of good old times. And don't even get me started on the gravy, Maud. You really outdid yourself today. Just goes to show, it doesn't matter how old you get, as long as you still know how to cook like my wife once did. Oh, just keep that going, Dad. I'll get in early with your retirement just to keep up with this kind of culinary performance every day. I suppose you could say your cooking has gotten slightly better over the years? Let's just say, there's a little bit of experience involved in perfecting a recipe. Now, where's the tea? And those delicious homemade biscuits you baked, Forbsie? Forbsie did indeed deliver with the tea and biscuits. I'm on my second cup. Speaking of Forbsie, isn't it remarkable? She's always been such a talented home cook, even when she was younger. I remember my A-levels were much more bearable thanks to her cooking in between study sessions. Absolutely. It’s always been our family’s secret weapon during exam times or when we just weren’t feeling up to the mark. There’s just something about finding comfort in a home-cooked meal. It’s strange, isn’t it? We’ve lived in so many different parts of the country over the years, but no matter where we were, me and your mum would try to recreate your motherly cooking. She’s got a style that’s uniquely British, yet universally comforting. Well, I suppose that’s the secret to a happy family. Good food and a willingness to share it, no matter where we are. Speaking of sharing, I’ll have to start learning those recipes. Your mum almost makes it look too easy. Wonder if I could get a tutorial next time we’re here, or perhaps even a cookbook? I doubt it will be just about recipes. You'll have to learn the stories behind the food too. Each dish has a story or a particular reason it was made for one of us at some point. Yeah, like the time you made a batch of her famous Yorkshire puddings for my birthday, youth group, and then kept the leftovers for everyone to enjoy.

I've been thinking a lot about our idea for an online platform for collaborative learning these past few days. It could really disrupt the way young people learn, wouldn't it? Absolutely, I love it! Using the concept of viral content to spread learning modules could really make it engaging and encourage participation. It could be something truly revolutionary. Exactly, and not just for the younger generation. I believe older students who might feel set in their ways could also benefit from it. It's all about breaking down the routine and making learning fun again. That's a key point. I think the problem-solving techniques we discussed could really be integrated into this platform too. It could encourage students to think critically and laterally about the material. Absolutely! Problem-solving as part of the learning process could make it much more practical and applicable to real-world scenarios. It could be a game-changer, literally. And imagine if we could also involve educators from diverse backgrounds to contribute modules. It would really enrich the platform, making it more inclusive and global. Now that's a great point. We could make it so that educators can contribute on a voluntary basis. It would encourage goodwill and make the platform even more comprehensive. And we could tie this in with existing start-ups or current companies who might be looking for innovators and problem-solvers as future employees. It could be really beneficial for both parties. That’s a fantastic idea. It could ease the transition from education to the workforce and give the students real-world experience even before they leave the platform. I was also thinking about the potential for less fortunate students from around the world. Could we make the platform free for them, or perhaps partner with organizations that support disadvantaged students? Now that's a great humanitarian angle to consider. From an entrepreneurial standpoint, it could benefit the business too by gaining goodwill and brand recognition. Plus, it aligns with a higher purpose that could really drive our vision. It's always good to think about how our ideas can be for the greater good. And speaking of that, have you already set up any meetings with some educators you know here? I’ve made a few calls. I managed to arrange a meeting with a professor from the University of Sydney who’s known for his innovative thinking in education.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my Halloween plans this year? It’s practically tradition now, but I’m planning a party at our place. It’s going to be epic! Thinking about decorations, food, and some spooky music. Still deciding though, if we should involve a costume – do you have any suggestions? That sounds amazing! I’ve been thinking about my costume too, but I haven’t settled on anything yet. We could plan out everything together, though. Maybe set a menu or create a playlist? Right, let me pull out my notes. Oh, and Thanksgiving is coming up next. I’ve been thinking about cooking a little something special. I’ve been wanting to try a new recipe. Might just sneak it in between Halloween preparation. You’re always on top of things! I’ve been wanting to try that new pastry shop in town too. They make amazing pie crusts. Perhaps we could go check them out and get supplies together for the holiday? That sounds like a good plan. We could also hit the farmer’s market and get some fresh ingredients. I’ve heard their pumpkins are the best this time of year. Now that’s a busy weekend planned. Speaking of fun plans, though, I’ve been meaning to ask. How’s work treating you at the project co-ordination job? Everything running smoothly? To be honest, it’s been a mixed bag. Some great developments but also silly administrative tasks creeping up all the time. One of my tasks is trying to get all the team meetings organised and working efficiently. Despite the hurdles, it’s a good learning experience. Growing is the name of the game for this role. I can imagine. I just had a tough week at work. Seems like the demand for mental health services has been higher than ever. That can’t be easy. You’re making such a difference though. Do you think we can combine our vacation plans in the near future? Or should I just look for a week where you’re free and plan something? I’d love that. I need a break for sure. I was thinking we could look into planning something around spring next year. After the long winter, a bit of sun would be wonderful. Spring could be perfect. We could almost guarantee less cold and rain in the UK.

Ah, I hear that your weekend was quite eventful, wasn’t it? I hope you didn’t have too much trouble getting to all those places. Oh, yes, well, that's just life here in the big city isn't it? But, the concert was fantastic! The tickets were sold out two weeks prior, so I was really lucky to get them last minute. Lucky indeed! I wish I could’ve joined you. I never got to see those live, though I’ve listened to their music so many times. They were as good as ever! The crowd, vocals, the whole atmosphere was electric – it was quite an experience. Sounds wonderful! London’s got a knack for making even the most ordinary things seem extra special, doesn’t it? I remember when I was young we used to travel to London to see the shops and whatnot. It was such a treat. That was a different time, wasn’t it? Back then, barely any big names used to play in London. But now it’s like every other day there’s something big happening here or there. Indeed! I'm curious, what’s next on your social calendar? Are you busy the next weekend? Nothing too big. Just some work in the evenings, but over the weekend, I think I’ll probably just relax. I’ve got a meeting with my team on Monday, so I need to make sure my production schedules are ready, you know. Oh really? Your job is quite hectic, isn’t it? What do you and your team do exactly? I know it doesn’t come up that often but I’m always interested in how people make a living. Well, I work as a production controller in a manufacturing firm. Essentially, we produce the parts for furniture companies. It’s quite varied, some days are routine, other days can be quite chaotic. That sounds really interesting! I never thought about what goes on behind the scenes of all the chair and tables we use. It sure must be a big responsibility. It’s quite a challenge but also rewarding in its own way. I have a team, we work together, and so long as everything goes smoothly, it’s quite satisfying. You know, I’ll have to ask about those production lines sometime. I once had a friend who worked in the manufacturing industry. She always used to talk about the little problems she’d encounter and how she’d deal with them.

Yo, how's studying going over here? Thought we'd move's things have changed so much since we left GCSEs. Oh, it's alright, I guess. I've just been hooked on this one module about scientific methods. It's fascinating, the way you can prove things with experiments and questions. Wow, I knew you liked Science, but scientific methods, that's deep! I wish I could wrap my head around things like that. It is complicated at first, but once you get the hang of it, it's pretty cool. I mean, we're talking about actually proving stuff in the real world, not just sitting in a classroom thinking about it. I guess that's why I ended up doing Humanities. I prefer the abstract side of things. But, I've started reading up on a bit of Psychology. It's quite interesting, how people think and interact. That sounds interesting! Psychology is so varied, you can explore so many different branches. Did you know that similar methods are used in it too? It's not all just about what people say, there's also a lot of statistical analysis involved. Yeah, I see that now when I read about research studies. It's quite unexpected. You think it's all therapists and couches, but then you see they're using scientific techniques to prove their theories. Exactly. It's all about making sure what you're saying is actually true. Not just guessing or assuming. Right. Speaking of assumptions, have you been keeping up with football? They played the Arsenal game and it was chaotic. I know, doesn't it feel like every game is a potential disaster now? It's like we've been riding a rollercoaster. Last-minute goals, penalties. Seems like the whole team is together in spirit but just can't click on the field. I really hope they sort their issues out soon. For sure. It's frustrating for us fans, and must be for them too. But I guess that's part of the fun . No, it's not fun in the moment. But looking back, those tense games are what make it so exciting. Reminds me of the times we used to argue over who would win between the Yorkshire teams and the Southern ones. Yeah, ha! It's like our own little rivalry. But I love it. Always brings back memories of cheering on the Cambridge teams back home.

Ah, I can't believe what happened yesterday at work! I was making my way to a meeting when I saw a gigantic spider right at the door. Literally, the size of my hand. I had to take a step back, breathe, and slowly back away. Oh, that sounds terrifying! I've always had a bit of a phobia for spiders, ever since I was a child. But, I must admit, I'm more terrified of mice than spiders. I had an infestation at home a couple of years ago and it keeps coming back. Mice? Oh no, I wouldn't wish that on anyone. I've always had a bit of a problem with them in the garden. They've eaten almost all of the plants I've taken care of. But as much as they can be pests, they do create quite a nuisance, don't they? They most certainly do! But, I suppose they're part of nature as much as anything else. Absolutely, they are. But it's not as black and white when they're running through your kitchen at 3 AM, scaring the life out of you. Oh, I can imagine! Speaking of nature, have you noticed the number of birds in the garden over the past few months? It's incredible, isn't it? Yes, absolutely! They're everywhere, it seems. I've started leaving some bread crumbs out for them and they seem really happy with that. That's lovely. I always enjoy watching birds, don't you? There's something so peaceful about them.
