Yes, it's quite calming. I do find myself watching them for longer than I should when I'm doing the cleaning around the house. I can imagine that. I've even started learning to recognize different species by their songs. It's quite therapeutic. That sounds very interesting. You know, despite all our troubles with pests, there's a lot of beauty out there in nature. Definitely. It's just sometimes when you're cleaning or dealing with them up close, it's easy to forget that. True. Maybe you should consider setting up a bird feeder or two in your garden. That's a good idea! Perhaps I will. And maybe a traps for the mice? You're right, I should really deal with that... It can be done in a humane way, too. Yes, I know, but it's one of those tasks that keeps getting put off.

Ah, lovely to finally meet you. I'm Emily, from Dorchester. I've been meaning to reach out to some of the relatives and reconnect. It's been years since our last family gathering, hasn't it? Yes, indeed it has, Emily! I'm Millicent – Millie, if you prefer. I'm from Bristol and moved to Wales later in life. But of course, my roots are here in Britain. I'm glad you took the initiative as well. I've found tracing back family history quite fascinating recently. Have you done much research on yours? I have actually, although I'm afraid I've not been as thorough as I'd have liked. But I've been meaning to get back into it. My mum passed away a couple of years ago, and she was keen on our ancestry. Since her passing, I've tried to gather as many of her notes and stories as possible. It's a bit of a puzzle, but its being rewarding. Oh, I'm so sorry to hear that, Emily. But good on you for keeping her memories alive. I've been meaning to ask, what was the nature of your mother's illness? I remember this side of the family tree having some issues with... is it diabetes? Or was it something else? No, it was actually Parkinson's. It was a tough battle for her, and for the family, of course. It's an awful disease, but she had a lot of fight in her. Honestly, I feel like I still grieve for the person she could have been without it. I'm so sorry, Emily. That must have been painful to witness. How old was she when she passed? She was only 67, which felt incredibly young, given everything she had lived through. More reason for us to treasure our family stories, isn't it? I wish I'd taken more detailed notes when my own parents were alive. But I've found that even the smallest scraps of information can be rich with meaning when you look back. It really can be, and I'm sure your family would be interested in hearing about your career, for instance. I know a bit from when we were children, but I'm sure there must be many stories you could share about your time as a teacher. Oh, those were some of the best years of my life!

Oh, what a lovely day we've got. The sky is so clear. Imagine how beautiful it'll be to see a hot air balloon from up here. It certainly would be ideal. I once saw a hot air balloon floating over the horizon when I was on holiday in the countryside. It was quite the sight. What's got you interested in those, out of curiosity? I was just thinking... I'd love to take a trip in one someday. But even just watching from afar, it gives a perspective on things, doesn't it? Reminds you of the beauty in the world. Indeed, it does. It's similar to watching a dog walk. It just seems to have a certain freedom, unhindered by the worries of life. That's a beautiful analogy. Speaking of dogs, I've been thinking of getting one. But I also love wildlife, especially in the English countryside. Knowing someone like you, who probably deals with wildlife often at work, do you ever find that their presence affects what or how much you can do in certain parts of this countryside? Well, different wildlife can pose different challenges. You might have to avoid areas while the birds are breeding. Or, in the case of badgers, avoiding to disturb their setts. It's actually quite fascinating. But it also means we need to respect their space. I understand, but it's hard isn't it, when as humans, we have our own ideas of what 'space' means. And with the spread of power lines across the countryside... doesn't that disrupt the natural habitats for some species? It does, and it's a delicate balance. Some power lines can actually be designed in ways that minimize impact. But true, there are those that can be quite disruptive, especially for bird species. I've seen studies on how different power line designs can minimize collision rates or affect nesting patterns. That reminds me, where's the best spot to camp around here? I was thinking of a trip soon, somewhere not too spoilt by touristic activity. Ah, there are so many great spots. I've camped near the river Waveney before. The scenery was stunning, and it's relatively quiet. But there are almost too many good spots to choose from here. We could also do a more complete camping trip if you'd like, with backpacks and all.

Ah, lovely to see you over here after the exercise class. We've had some mixed weather lately; hasn't it? Yes, absolutely. Here in the Solihull area, we seem to be enjoying some quite pleasant spring time. Still, just last week we had a bit of a storm roll through. It's been the same in Hitchin. One moment it's raining, the next the sun's out and it's lovely again. That's life with English weather, isn't it? I've just finished a particularly tough series of meetings with the various club managers, so I was looking forward to today’s class to blow off some steam. I completely understand. It must be challenging to manage multiple gyms. Do you find there’s a difference in how various areas respond to different coaching techniques? Definitely. You'd think you could just apply the same approach everywhere but it's not as straightforward as that. Different backgrounds, different ways of learning, different priorities. It's been a learning curve for me. I've noticed something similar as a language teacher. For instance, teaching this morning it was clear that some of the students prefer a more structured approach while others do better with more relaxed, conversational methods. It's all about tailoring your technique to the individual’s needs and abilities, isn’t it? Absolutely. And it must be so similar in your field, understanding the diverse learning styles of your students. Speaking of which, how do you find the current level of English language skills in your students? Well, it's a mixed picture I'd say. Some students come in with quite a strong foundation from their schools, but there are others who have gaps or need to build confidence. It’s really about identifying these issues early on and creating targeted lessons to address them. I see, and of course, it’s not just about the language. It’s about helping them feel more comfortable and confident using English in their daily lives. That's something you can't easily quantify but is so crucial. Definitely. And on that note, do you ever find there’s a connection between education levels and willingness or preparedness to learn new languages? That’s an interesting question. From what I’ve seen, it often seems that those who have had good levels of education - and this almost goes across disciplines, not just language studies - are more open to learning new languages.

Ah, marvellous to see you both again! You've had a safe journey today? The traffic sounds like it's been a bit of a nightmare from what I've been told. Yes, quite a squeeze on the A1 now and then! But we made it – no major questions on the exam just now. Aye, well, that's grand to hear. I've been wondering, how's the new job going? The maths exams, I mean. It can't be too easy, right? Oh, it's got its moments! I mean, the mathematics itself isn't the problem, dear. I used to love it at school. But marking hundreds of papers – keeping your concentration up, not letting any bias slip in, making sure each student has a fair shot even if their writing isn't perfect… that's the challenge. It's rewarding when a student gets it though. Yeah, I could imagine. But maths is pretty straightforward. You're either right or you're not – unlike history or English! Aye, this young man here is quite the mathematician, isn't he? He could have his own maths club if he wanted! He's quite the enthusiast, isn't he? He's good at it, but I'm working hard too. Grandma, you still good at maths? Could you help me with these homework problems sometimes? Oh, would you like that, would you? But it's been a while for me now. I remember the basics, but I'm afraid I'd be more of a hindrance than help. Still, it's just lovely to see the next generation so enthusiastic about learning. You're doing well, remember? Aye, and healthy competition is always good! But first things first, we've brought some good ol' Yorkshire tea and biscuits. Oh, thank you both! You know just what we need, don't you? Of course! You lot are always after a good strong cup. There's nothing better than Yorkshire tea. Speaking of things we need – we've been meaning to discuss some plans for the house. I've been thinking of doing a bit of gardening this spring, maybe this summer. Would you... I can lend a hand with that! I like gardening – it's like maths, but with mud instead of numbers! Well, that's one way to put it. I'll keep an eye on you, though. Don't go getting your hands too dirty!

Right, so I'm going to take A66 first, then onto the A1. It's a bit of a longer route, but it should be less traffic-prone this time of the day and we've got a pretty long drive ahead of us to get to the gig. That's fine by me, Sheila. I just hope the GPS takes us on the shortest route and we don't end up taking a detour like that one time where we ended up right in the middle of a cattle field! Oh, that was hilarious! You know, I've actually been meaning to update our satnav before we left, but I never got around to it. Technology, dear. I swear it's been designed by someone who just loves to watch us humans scratch our heads. Perhaps. But can't say we haven't had our share of excitement with it. Like the time you tried to navigate the town's one-way system with Siri? That was ridiculous! Next time, I grab a local map. You know, old-school. So, have you packed any snacks? I’m really hoping there won't be any roadworks or accidents holding us up. I’ve heard they've got some fun ceilidhs in the area this weekend. I brought a thermos of tea, some biscuits, and a bit of local cheese. Should keep us going if need be. And yes, ceilidhs are always a blast in these parts, really get the community together. We might see if we can grab a quick look at the local wool shop on our way back. I’ve always wanted to learn that spinning technique. You and your crafts, Sheila! I just hope it’s not going to rain too much. More specifically, those ceilidhs! Oh it should be fine, they say clear skies for this weekend. But regardless, we should be prepared for all weathers. While you’re on changing the subject, did you manage to sit down and write anything new this week? Ah, I’ve been in a bit of a block, but just yesterday something started working its way through. And I finally figured out how to properly use that new microphone I got. Did you use the new stand? I thought it looked quite pricey. Yeah, and I was hesitant at first, but trust me, it’s worth it. Totally worth it.

Oh, did I order Avocado toast again? I'm so predictable. You haven't talked about anything else the whole morning! I guess it just comes naturally. You know, kind of like how questions about communal living just tend to pop up when we're talking about our work. I'm actually struggling right now with a project brief I'm trying to get through at university. It's about designing a communal living spaces. Oh, that's actually really interesting. I've heard about a few projects like that, especially here in London where housing is a huge issue. Yeah, that's exactly the kind of big-picture thinking the brief required. What's been keeping you up at night about your communal living project? It's the balance between providing enough personal space for individuals, and fostering a sense of community among the residents. You know, it's all about those tiny details that make a place feel like home. Absolutely. It reminds me of a project we worked on together during our graduate studies. It was for a community housing development. We had to think about everything - the layout, the shared spaces, even the color palette. It was a challenge, but so rewarding to see it all come together. Oh, I remember that project. You were so obsessed about incorporating green spaces. I don't think anyone would ever forget that, especially the client who kept saying how we were turning it into a 'hipster jungle'. Right. But it worked, didn't it? Our final design won the project. It did. It proves that sometimes, taking risks with unconventional design elements really pays off. Speaking of taking risks, we might want to do that with our next project. I've been wanting to explore more biophilic designs. Biophilic design is on the rise, isn't it? Incorporating elements of the natural world into architecture. Yes, and not just for aesthetic reasons. Research shows it can reduce stress, improve productivity and even reduce the need for artificial lighting. So, what stops us from introducing it more often? Sure, there are budget constraints, but given that biophilic design can also save on energy costs in the long run, it's a win-win. Exactly, but from what I've seen, most clients aren't aware of the long-term benefits, or they're worried about the initial cost. Well, that's where we can make a change.

Oh, so many topics we've got to cover. I just can't believe how fast time flies. It feels like just yesterday we were struggling to balance work and parenthood, and now you've got your sixth form coming to a close. Yeah, it does feel kind of surreal. You remember when I was just starting and you were still working out how to manage everything with junior and big sis? Absolutely. You were such a trouper for us. But even with how busy we get, it's always great to catch up. It really is. I have to ask, how's the traffic been treating you? It's been a nightmare lately. Oh, we've had our fair share of wars with the roads. And the drivers! Some days I think we're living in a world of aggressive ants instead of human beings. Oh, I know, right? I saw something last week that just blew my mind. Some guy cut me off, then next minute he's honking because I was taking a moment to account for it. Honking? That's so last century. These days everyone should know that we're on 'connected' roads. If in doubt, just make sure you're not blocking anyone, right? Well, technology is certainly helpful, but basic etiquette is even more important I think. Speaking of which, how was your trip in London? London? That's a whole different story. Despite the congestion charges, doesn't seem to stop reckless driving. I swear the lorry drivers forget they're not the only ones on the road. Sounds like a nightmare. Seems like the More Care Less Stress campaign isn't reaching everyone, huh? Exactly. Anyway, let me get this tea made and we can dive deep into life, the universe and everything in between. While you're here, how about we catch up with our friend Sarah? Sarah? I haven't seen her since the summer. That could be fun. What's she up to? She's been organizing this social activity group for young professionals. You know, networking, socializing, the whole bit. Might be an interesting way for you to meet people and maybe job prospects as well. That sounds like something I could definitely be into. Job hunting can be so isolating sometimes. Exactly! You never know what connections can lead to new opportunities. Anyway, Sarah mentioned a meet-up coming up this weekend.

So, I hear you're considering applying for a media role, isn't that right? Yeah, that's right. I've been finding the radio side of things really interesting and thought I might be good at it. But I'm also nervous because it's quite different from what I normally do. Of course you are! It's always daunting when you're looking at a new field. But with a postgrad degree and journalistic experience, you've got a great start. Thanks! But how do I even get started with the job application? First, you need a strong CV. Make sure you emphasize any relevant skills, like writing, interviewing, or editing. Also, highlight your broadcasting or journalist experience, even if it was as a volunteer or part-time role. Yeah, I've been thinking about that. I have a bit of experience writing for a local magazine and being on a university radio station. That's perfect. Use specific examples to demonstrate these skills. For instance, instead of saying "writing experience," say "published articles in the XYZ magazine" or "ran a weekly interview segment on university radio." Oh, I see. That makes more sense. The specificity is what I need. Exactly. For a media role, they want to see you can produce content and tell stories. Also, spend some time researching the company and job to understand what specific skills or experience they're looking for. That's really good advice. I didn't even think about researching the company. Absolutely. It doesn't just show that you've done your homework, but it also shows how much you're interested in the role and understanding what the job involves. Makes sense. Also, I worry about the job interview. I've never done a media interview. Ah, job interviews can be intimidating, but they are usually less confrontational than media interviews. However, it's a great idea to prepare answers that are concise and to the point. Think about common questions, such as "Why do you want this role?" or "What experience do you have in this field?" I thought they might want to see how I handle a tough or unexpected question. They could, but for most media roles, this is more about being able to give a clear and concise answer. You want to showcase your skills and enthusiasm without going on too long or losing focus.

So, I've been thinking a lot about changing career paths recently. The entrepreneurial world has always fascinated me, but it's also quite daunting. Have you ever considered pursuing a completely different career trajectory, and if so, how did you navigate that process? Actually, the thought of a career change has crossed my mind quite often too. Going from teaching to a new field seems like a big leap. But I guess life's too short to stay in a position you're not truly content with, don't you think? Absolutely! There's an Australian proverb, “Lay it in Malley's wake,” meaning to take a new direction when one path is not serving you. What initially sparked your interest in making a change? Well, to be honest, it's been a combination of feeling stagnant in my current role and a desire to have more autonomy and work-life balance. As a teacher, it's expected to be on-call almost 24/7—even outside the school hours. That sounds grueling! So, you're looking for something with more predictability and stability, yet still challenging and fulfilling? Exactly! I’m really interested in working with people, but maybe not in such an intensive, high-stress environment. Plus, I’d love to incorporate my passion for environmental issues. That's a great starting point, really focusing on your passions and what you want out of your work life. I've been exploring the possibility of starting a small business, maybe something related to sustainability or environmental products. That sounds really cool, and a great way to combine your interests and aspirations. How do you plan to break into that market, and what kind of steps have you taken so far? I’ve done some research and planning, but I’m still in the initial stages of getting set up. I’ve been looking into the Australian market, particularly in Melbourne and Sydney because of their strong focus on sustainability. I’ve also been reading up on business plans, networking with people in the sector, and considering courses to enhance my skills. It’s great that you’re taking it step by step and being thorough. I suppose the hardest part for me would be the risk of it not working out financially. As a single parent, I couldn't afford to take on too much financial risk. True. Financial resilience is crucial.

I've decided I need a diet, I've been looking after this little terror and he's been teaching me all about how to indulge in deep-fried chicken nuggets and garlic bread. Hehehe, Mummy likes those too! Ah, the joys of parenthood right? I never thought I'd see myself talking about dieting in my 70s! As a teacher, I always stressed the importance of a balanced diet but it's a bit different when you're caring for a toddler who thinks chocolate is the main food group. Absolutely, it's a whole different world. Do you remember when we used to have big Sunday dinners at your place? What happened to all that? It's a different time now with family dynamics and diet culture. Let's not forget, there's barely any big family dinners these days. Everyone's so busy. Absolutely. Nowadays, it's more about arranging for food delivery than cooking a meal together. It's different but efficient in its own way. That reminds me, have you all seen the number of dieticians and nutritionists on social media? Advice on everything from keto to vegan, to the most obscure 'rainbow diet' you can imagine. It's a new era of dieting really. That's certainly true. Technology has taken over our lives in many ways. Even in areas where you wouldn't expect, like dieting. But on the positive side, it also makes it easier to research and learn about different things. Definitely, I just tried to learn more about a 'no refined sugar' diet and it's been surprisingly liberating. The thing is, with my son's love for fast food and my love for comfort eating, it's changing the dynamic at home. We're making an effort to be more involved in cooking though. Cooking? I want to cook, can I, Mummy? Maybe when you're a bit older, sweetheart. But we can start with some baking. You can help me mix this cake batter. I used to love baking with the kids in school. Making cookies and pies. It's a great way to engage with children, teaches them about measurements and patience. It could be a nice family activity for this household too. That's a great idea, there's a lot to be said for that. I remember when I was a publishing teacher, we used to have a section in our books where it talked about youth engagement and family activities, and cooking was always a great suggestion.

Ah, lovely to see you, Sarah. How have you been? We have had so many ups and downs in the past few years, and it feels good to catch up in peace. Right! It's been a roller coaster, hasn't it? I've been managing okay, though. The sales job keeps me on my toes, and supervising the lunchtime crew at the cafe is quite a challenge. And you? How are things with your marketing? All good? Yeah, well, let's just say I've had to adapt, like everyone. But I'm enjoying it. There's always something different, and I like the variety. Variety is what we all need, right? Was it just me or did the whole Brexit thing cause quite a stir? I still get chills thinking about the vote and everything that's happened since. Oh absolutely. It was such a difficult and divisive topic. I remember it so well. We had so many heated discussions in those days. I still find it hard to understand why people voted the way they did. It's certainly changed a lot for all of us, hasn't it? Yeah, and seeing it all in the news nowadays – all the politicians saying things to spin it their way – it feels like politics have become even more dirty. But I suppose it's always been that way, to some extent. True, but we’re used to a bit of politeness in the face of disagreement. I don't think anyone expected things would reach such a fever pitch. You're right. And what about concerts or plays during lockdown? We had less variety there, didn't we? No West End shows or the like. That's true. I did manage to get quite into piano though. My aunt left me her old piano, and I started teaching myself. It's been an interesting journey. Not as smooth as I'd hoped, but I'm determined! That's just like you! Doing something because you want to learn. I've heard it's quite therapeutic too. You’ll probably be the next Elton John by the end of the year. As if! But it's been really good for my mental health. That’s excellent. So, have you been hearing from any old friends from sixth form? We had a bit of a WhatsApp group going back then, but it died down after a while.

Ah, lads, it's been ages since we last got together. How have you both been keeping these past months? You know, I've been noticing a change in the way our company uses social media. More focus on analytics and engagement. It's been quite a turnaround and I thought you, as a Director of Studies, might have some insights on this. You'd be right, Andrew. It's been a transformation, that's for sure. I'm right in the middle of it at the moment. Actually, Twitter especially has become a key channel for us to share research and get people engaging with our work. I've noticed we've had a sharp uptake in usage. [laughs] I have noticed you've been quite avid on Twitter, Robert. Always keen to share your thoughts. It's good to see our study areas getting more visibility. As a Communications Manager, I've started seeing social media as a key channel for our company, beyond its traditional PR function. True. It's not just about PR anymore, it's about creating communities and platforms for discussion. And it seems to be working - we've had some really valuable feedback on our studies, just through this engagement. That's interesting. How have you managed to create such positive engagement? I assumed, while the 'official' company account would get good traction, but our personal accounts might not work the same way. It's all about authenticity, Andrew. People respond to real people, not faceless corporate entities, no matter how polished they are. I've been trying really hard to keep my account as personal as possible and focus on what I find interesting about our studies. I don't tweet about us non-stop - that would be boring and push the wrong kind of engagement. You make a solid point, Robert. I've seen studies that prove people prefer real voices and measured, personal content rather than a laser-like focus on the company ethos. Do you think that's also why professors and students seem so active online these days? It's creating new dialogues and maybe even breaking some barriers? Absolutely. It's democratizing information, really. Anyone who's interested in advanced studies can engage with us, influence our research in some way. For example, a recent tweet about a new paper we released got us several leads on potential collaborators from unexpected places.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my weekend? Work was crazy. Our biggest project is coming up and I was literally slumped over my desk by the end of it. Yeah, it sounds like the usual, but I kind of do love questions like this. I mean, and as if that weren’t enough, my colleague just decided to abandon their part of the project at the last minute. I had to fill in for them. Which means I had even less time to myself. That sounds like a nightmare. How are you finding the load? I used to be a project manager before switching to mental health, but I know how draining those roles can be. Exhausting. I’m usually pretty good with deadlines and everything, but this one is stressful. You know, there's a theory in psychology about juggling various roles and responsibilities. It's called multi-role juggling. Really? We could use a bit of that theory round here. True. Where did you end up eating on the weekend then? Honestly, I think the only home-cooked meal I had was a Friday night pie. The rest was takeout or just snacks at my desk. Well, as a good housemate, it is now my duty to ensure you have a proper meal tonight. I’ve been meaning to try out a new recipe anyway. Oh, you don’t need to do that. But, if you're planning to cook, consider making less. I just had a whole Sunday of sandwiches and won't handle a huge dinner. Alright, I’ll keep it light. Maybe just something simple and comforting. Yes, comfort food. Like a good jacket potato with all the trimmings? Actually, yes, that could be brilliant. So, how was your weekend? It was alright. Nothing too exciting, but I finally got to go for a walk by the river on Sunday morning. That sounds lovely. Do you always like going for walks there? Yeah, it's my little escape. People watching, listening to the water flow, it just clears my head. I need to find a way to get out of the office more often, you know? Oh, absolutely. Work-life balance is crucial, especially in our line of work. Yeah, when you’re used to being on the go, sitting at a desk all day doesn’t exactly feel like work. Well, that's one reason I changed.

Right, so I've been thinking. I don't think it's a good idea for ANON to have his brother Ian over for Easter. It's been a bit tense between them since his divorce, and well, let's just say they've got a bit of a history. Really? I hadn't considered that. I see what you mean, but we've always been a family that supports each other through thick and thin right? Absolutely, and it's important that we do. But coming right after the new year, when ANON's already adjusting to his new car, new routine, and all that – I'm worried it might just be too much. You're right. Might just want to have a bit of a family discussion about it first. We need to make sure everyone's on board and prepared for it. Speaking of ANON's new car, has he shown it to you yet? I mean, we all know how excited he gets when he buys something new. Oh, absolutely. He's had it for a couple of weeks now. It's a nice one, a VW Golf. He's been very proud showing off all its features. But enough about cars, has anyone noticed the spread we have here for this meal? Looks like ANON has really outdone himself this time. It certainly does look wonderful. He's always been very particular about his cooking, isn't he? Speaking of meals, how about the new restaurant we went to last week? John and Sarah from the school, and their friends, said it was "out of this world". Maybe we should all head there next. Oh, that sounds like a plan! Actually, that kind of reminds me, we should make sure to do things the way Ian likes too when he comes, right? No surprises that might put him off. Right, so we'll ease him in gradually. Perhaps we could all meet up at that restaurant for lunch or something and then head back here later? Brilliant idea. And perhaps we could plan a sort of itinerary for his visit, things he enjoys but also not too packed for him. I know he's always loved the countryside around here so maybe a short walk or something? Good call. We can show him around, and he can enjoy the peace and quiet Holsworthy has to offer.

Ah, I've been trying to learn Spanish for years now, and it's still so hard. I've tried books, apps, courses and everything. I don't know, maybe it's the grammar that throws me off, or perhaps I'm just really lazy. You're not lazy, dear. Learning a new language is one of the most challenging cognitive tasks out there, especially for us of a certain age. It's like trying to rewire your brain, isn't it? That's exactly it. But even with all these resources, I get stuck in the same routine. I memorize vocab, try to understand the grammar rules, but then when I'm in a verbal conversation, it's just like... nothing from my brain. That's because language learning isn’t just about memorization, though it does help. Real fluency comes from hearing and speaking the language regularly. That's where you need immersion or, if that's not possible, looking for a speaking partner. That's the hardest bit, isn't it? Finding someone to speak with. I tried a few language exchange events here or online, but it's hard to commit to this regularly. Exactly! The different learning methodologies are interesting, though. I came across this study while I was job-hunting years ago. It was about acquisition over learning, meaning that to pick up a language effectively, you have to use it, not just learn about it. I see. Hmm, maybe that's where I'm going wrong. I really need to find a way to actually use Spanish daily. That's why I like the Duolingo app - it makes you use the language right away. And as for immersion, there's always YouTube videos and podcasts if one can't travel. More technology! How did we survive before the internet? We couldn’t. Which brings another interesting point, about countries where people speak two languages. Have you heard of Catalan and Castillian? Oh yes, sure. I was watching something on TV about Catalonia, and they speak both Catalan and Spanish. I don't know how they do it. It's truly impressive. And it's not just for the Catalans; some countries like Belgium are also bilingual with Dutch and French. Really? That's quite fascinating. Wonder how they manage. They start young, of course. Languages learned in childhood are much easier. But even as adults, if we immerse ourselves, we can do it too.

Right, Dad, so I've got all these papers scattered around. We have flight tickets for the upcoming holiday, some documents that need to be scanned and sent to the bank, and a few more that just need filing. Ah, indispensable paperwork. Still have to do all this, even with all the digital paraphernalia we have now. You've got your scanner set up and ready, have you? Yes, I've got the scanner right here. Now, shall I start with the documents that need to be scanned and sent out to the bank? It's a bit of a task, but I need to do it, you know. Yes, start with that. The bank's been a bit fussy lately about paperless stuff, just like the computers. Once you get the hang of it, it's a lot easier. Then we can do the rest of the sorting. Exactly, and it’ll also give us more space here, as much as anything. You know, in the digital world, Kelly Brook might call it “decluttering”. But yes, it will make the room look better, at least. For sure. We could practically do with a bit more space, especially if we’re going to have to fetch some corpus linguistics readings from the university. I hope this doesn't need scanning, in case you're wondering. [laughs] No, Dad, the corpus linguistics stuff is fine, but the papers we need to sort are about banking, tax stuff, and a few other documents that the bank needs. Got it. So, scanning and sending over these documents first. Just make sure they come out clearly, it's the clarity and the content that matters more than the paper itself. Except, I suppose, with Kelly Brook's pictures. [both chuckle] [laughs] Oh, I'm sure the bank would be happy with her on their documents, but let's stick to the necessary paperwork. Quite. So, how you planning to cook when we're on holiday? Any particular recipes you want to try? Oh, that's a good question. I've been thinking about trying out some new recipes. Maybe something that doesn't take too much prep, given we'll be trying to see a bit of the area as well. Right, well, you know, we almost always end up sticking to what we know. But I swear, if I ever see another packet of ready-mix lasagne on the shelf, I’ll throw up.

Oh, did you see that?? That biker just swerved right into the petrol station. Ah, that's the typical Saturday morning excitement around here. I know it's kind of exciting, but also kind of reckless, right? Yeah, I'd definitely say that. But you know, driving and biking can both be pretty exhilarating. Definitely, and it can also be quite stressful, keeps you on your toes, doesn't it? Yeah, especially on a day like today – lots of traffic, lots of excitement. And I bet there'll be more, we're just waiting for the usual bikers' congregation at the next petrol station. Exactly, they love the big gatherings. It's a different world sometimes, isn't it? Absolutely! And you know, it's funny because it's so far removed from our daily lives. I mean, I'm just stuck in front of a computer most of the time, doing admin work. That's fun too, though, I'm sure. But yeah, driving in particular can be a real escape, a chance to break free from the daily grind. It's true! There's something about the open road that does feel quite liberating. And you know, in my job, I spend so much time dealing with the paperwork, I'm always relieved when I can just sit in my car and listen to some music or a podcast. Definitely, and it's a kind of escape that all of us can share in, no matter what career or daily routine we have. Plus, the fuel of the nation – I mean, petrol stations are such a staple of British culture, aren't they? Oh, definitely. While you're dealing with the admin side of things, I'm on the other end, dealing with machinery and systems – but we both rely on petrol stations in some way. Funny how different our jobs can be, but they all contribute to different aspects of our everyday lives. Yeah, definitely. Plus, the diversity of people you meet at them – just like the bikers we just observed. Yeah, and that's what makes driving and petrol stations so quintessentially British – they're meeting points, aren't they? For all walks of life. I suppose so. And while some might clump them altogether, there’s a lot of depth in the personalities, the DIY mechanics, the bikers, the just-returned-from-a-long-holiday families...

Alright, James, so first things first. I've got today's newspaper here and there's an article about Serena Williams. Thought you'd be interested. Yeah! Is it about her playing the Australian Open? Oh, haven't seen that one yet. But I've got a question. Is she still taking lessons or does she have her own coaching methods now? Well, she does have her own team but she still pursues training and keeps learning. It's a bit like how you're learning game tactics in your tennis, isn't it? Even professionals continue to improve. Cool! I've been trying out some of these techniques we learned with Rachel. Like, trying to get the ball to bounce just in front of my opponent. It's tough though! Indeed, James. It's about understanding the angle and speed at which you hit the ball. But persistence and practice are key, just like when you were learning to juggle. You couldn't do three balls at first, could you? No, it was really hard! I kept dropping them. But I kept trying... Exactly. You need to do that with the tennis too. And what Serena Williams or Venus do is often not just about skill or technique, but also about mental strength. They can stay focused and composed under pressure – like in a big match when everything's on the line. Good point. I've seen Serena really dig deep in those key moments of the game. Shows real character and discipline. So, what was their technique in that video where the ball just popped the net? Ah, that's called a 'topspin' or 'snap'. The ball will dip quickly after the net, which can make it a difficult shot to return. The key is to angle the racket slightly and strike the ball at the top with a bit of forearm movement. That’s quite advanced! I remember changing the racket grip years ago and my coach was like, "The key is not only how you hold it but also how you move your whole arm." Can I try that one day? It looks so cool when they do it. Absolutely. Just remember, technique is almost as important as practice. And don’t give up if you don’t nail it right away, James. And don’t forget match practice! It’s one thing to practice serves or forehands in isolation but it's another to actually play the game.

Yo, anyone got any ideas what we could do while we watch Downton Abbey tonight? Maybe we can have a competition to see who can remember the most about the episode afterwards? You're quite the competitive one, aren't you, ANON? But that's actually a brilliant idea. It will make us pay attention to the details. Besides, there's always the possibility that "Downton Abbey" might have some competition with this... Are you serious with the napkin? Looks like we've got our own little controversy here at the dinner table. Yeah, that's definitely a good conversation starter. But now, can we please discuss the real important topics? Like turkey and Christmas shopping? I've seen some fantastic deals online for Christmas shopping, by the way. Make sure you check it out guys. We could even plan a trip together this year. A trip? So, where were you thinking? Maybe somewhere within the UK or a short trip to Europe? Nothing too far, though. We should definitely make plans while the kids are still home. Speaking of which, I saw there were some cool deals at the airport. Maybe we can grab some travel-sized stuff while we're at it? A bit ahead of ourselves, but hey, it's always good to be prepared. You boys always dreaming about traveling. But I don't blame you. I wish we could've seen more of the world in our time. Though, my favorite traveling experience has always been on trains. Trains are actually quite romantic, you know. Especially those old ones with the compartments. Listen to you, old Lady. Just proves we’ve had enough adventuring in our lives, doesn’t it? Oh, sure. Sure. I know what you mean, though. The experience of cruising along a country, seeing all the little stations...bliss. Speaking of transportation, did anyone hear the Queen's speech this year? Or perhaps you're more interested in pop culture, like the music in the new films or music in general? The Queen’s speech always brings back nostalgic feelings. And as for music, I’ve been listening to Christmas classics. I like how this year, they had... uh, don’t you think that the music in “A Christmas Carol” was quite subtle but moving? Like the violin and all? Yeah, it was pretty. And it made the scenes even more powerful. I also thought about how everyone's Christmas Eve's went, like when I saw ANON partying with friends back at uni.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my culinary adventure last week? I tried making a traditional English roast and it was a bit of a disaster. I ended up burning the potatoes and undercooking the beef. You know, questions are always asked at home about the authenticity and aesthetic of the roast. "Mummy, is that supposed to look like this?" But actually, I've always found that burnt potatoes have a very special flavour. Right, let me not hear any complaints about burnt potatoes, darling! In our family, burnt potatoes meant we were just getting into the good stuff. Really? So, I was making food just the way you like it then! Well, perhaps not. But I think you need to learn the balance. You're going to end up with a fine roast once you get the hang of it. That reminds me, did anyone else try cooking something new these past few weeks? I made a rather delicious pasta dish last Tuesday. We could have it for dinner this weekend if everyone agrees? Oh, that would be amazing! I’ve been craving some pasta. Yeah, that sounds good. But we must remember to keep things balanced. A nice salad or roasted vegetables could go well with it. I’ll make sure to include those options. Speaking of balance, I’ve been working on my work-life balance lately. As a project co-ordinator, it can get quite stressful managing the different teams. But I’ve been trying to do better, setting clear boundaries, taking breaks, that sort of thing. Good on you, hon. It's important to look after yourself and know you can't do everything at once. You know, I’ve seen a lot of my staff struggle with that too. Some of them are consumed by work and often neglect their own health. Absolutely. And it affects not just them, but their relationships, family health, the whole lot. That's why I try to lead by example. As an examinations manager, I've seen the toll excessive stress can take on students too. It’s not just about work or study; it’s about being whole and healthy. Exactly. And don’t forget, family and friends are there to support too. That’s so true. Speaking of family, have we talked about Aunt Martha’s 60th birthday? We should make some plans. Oh Lord, yeah.

I've decided I need a new blender. Our old one can't handle these new recipes anymore. It's like it's out of Moore's law. Oh, isn't that the life, always replacing things. Speaking of replacements, heard about the new Marks and Spencer food range? It's been raved about. Yes! I was just considering ordering their pizzas online as our plan to pick up tonight was foiled by rain. And I even saw an interesting wine promotion alongside it. A fourteen-year-old Chardonnay, I kid you not. A fourteen-year-old wine? That sounds interesting. Is that a new trend or a bit of a gimmick? I'm not even sure how well that works. Hence my curiosity. But honestly, sometimes I want a drink that's more complex than a £5 bottle from the shop around the corner. Quite fancy. As long as it doesn't end up as next week's cat's water bowl. By the way, how was the appraisal at work? Well, that's a whole different kettle of fish. The team assumed we'd nail it given our recent project successes. But the higher-ups seem to be expecting more ambitious, long-term plans. It feels a bit like solving a crossword - you piece things together but sometimes you just need that one lucky guess, you know? Ah, crossword metaphors. I couldn't have put it better. "Three letters - First aid for a cut?" Or in your case, "A project's future directions that impress investors?" Yes, or "What do you do when you have three side projects ongoing and your boss wants five more by the end of the week?" Just be careful not to get personally invested in those side projects, or you might find you're forgetting to eat or watch your favourite shows. Speaking of which, have you watched the new season of Walking Dead or Trapped on Netflix? Walking Dead is such a guilty pleasure. I always manage to fit it in. Trapped is also on my list, though I haven’t started it yet. Walking Dead is always good for a mindlessness binge. I swear those show-runners outdo themselves every time. The dialogue, the plot twists, it's all fine entertainment. Absolutely. And seriously though, if there's one thing that can often drive me to distraction while watching TV... Our cat, purely?

Yo, lads!_check.in. What're y'all wearing's this eve? Nah, what's yours then? I'm actually don't know what to wear! I have all of this stuff but I need a opinion. I'm wearing this new skirt from a recent shop in Birmingham, it's kind of like a sundress and it's really comfy. Oh, that's nice! I've been thinking about wearing my favourite heels out, but I worry about comfort. You know what? I actually love heels if they're right. I swear, the right pair can totally change your confidence – and mood too! Yeah, definitely! I had a pair of heels like that, proper comfy, but they went bust last week. So, I'm actually thinking of going for flats. That's a good move, bruv, I'd do the same if I was in your shoes. What's the plan for the night, though? Any good places in mind? Mm, yeah, there's this new bar or club, whatever it is, that just opened this side of town. We should check it out! Ah, I'm all for that. What's the plan for drinks? I need some ideas. As for drinks, why don't we suggest different ones and see what we all decide? I'm thinking a nice gin and tonic perhaps? Gin and tonic does sound lovely, but I've also heard about this fantastic local ale, couldn't resist if it's from here. Oooh, that does sound good! I'm actually not too into beer, but I could live with a wine. Wine sounds lovely, less intoxicating than beer or spirits, gives a nice level, if you know what I mean. True. It does also depend on whether we end up snacking or having proper food. Snacking and night out go hand in hand for me. I know what you mean! But we should probably plan food, so we're not all starving mid-way through the evening. Definitely! So, are we all in for the night out? Or perhaps you're more interested in a chill at someone's house? I'm definitely game if it's a good vibe venue. A night out is always up to us. Agreed. But we should also consider what time we're meeting, like if this place has a dress code or whatnot. Good point, if it's a chill place, we might bring like guest outfits and then change if we want.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I was convinced I was reincarnated from ancient Egypt? You didn't mention that. Is this something new? No, this was a few years ago when I was going through this kind of spiritual journey. I read a lot about Egypt and felt such a connection, I was convinced that I must have lived there in a past life. That's quite the experience. I've always been fascinated by how our personalities could be shaped by something as abstract as a past life or reincarnation, don't you think? Definitely. I often wonder how much of our individualities are actually instinctual, just like how a puppy knows to bark or cats to pounce on string without being taught. It's almost as if we're guided by this immaterial soul or consciousness that survives beyond this life. It's a very interesting idea. But, do you think that could also apply to our relationships? Like, are we all potential soul mates floating around somewhere, waiting to find each other? That's a beautiful way to look at it. I mean, certainly some people come into our lives who have a profound impact, often more than others. Sometimes it feels like the universe is nudging us towards them. I think that's the core of the concept of soul mates. But it also raises so many questions about whether love or compatibility is something determined by fate or if we choose it ourselves. Precisely. It's a bit of both I think. Sometimes love feels like fate, like you two were meant to be together. But at the same time, you also have to work at it to grow and evolve together. Yes, and I guess that's the beauty of it too. The journey, not just the destination. Absolutely. Speaking of journeys, if we could visit any period in history, which one would you choose? That’s a tough one. I’ve always been drawn to the Middle Ages. It might not be the most appealing era to live in, but there’s something about the simplicity, the chivalry and the sense of community that appeals to me. And I think I'd choose the 1960s, either in the UK or the US. There was so much cultural change happening, the music, the art, the political movements... Yeah. It's amazing how much sense of history can change your perspective on the current day.

Oh, it's been ages! I've missed catching up with you. How's everything been since we last met at that business seminar in London? You know how it is. Work's been busy. Still trying to get the hang of this civil service – so far, so good, but I prefer the energy and creativity of the private sector. Have you started your own business yet, like you were thinking of? Actually, yes! I've been working on it part-time over the last few months. It's a bit of a challenge, but I'm really enjoying the freedom it gives me. Tell us more, tell us more! What kind of business is it? It's a specialized marketing and sales organization. I have some great contacts and ideas, and so far, it's being received well. That's fantastic! It takes a lot of guts to start your own business. You'll have to tell me all about it at some point, especially the sales aspect. I'm curious how you handle that side of things. Oh, I can go on and on about it. But maybe another time. Sure, we can't have the entire conversation just about business, can we? No, we can't. Speaking of different topics, I'm actually really into knitting now. I started a few months ago and it's been such a calming hobby. Oh, that's great! I used to do it when my kids were younger, but then I got busy with work and it fell by the wayside. Seems like the right time to pick it up again. Knitting? Isn't that a bit... stereotypical for us? Hey, no stereotypes here! I think everyone has something that helps them relax and we should embrace it. Exactly. And you know, it’s interesting because just because something is stereotypical doesn’t mean it isn’t beneficial or enjoyable. It’s like the whole 'unpaid holiday' situation most of us have right now. It's more about managing your work-life balance. True. I recently had to take a week off due to sickness – not fun, but it made me realize how much we take our health for granted. I know what you mean. Work can't control all of life, however much we might try. Remember that little episode we had with the air conditioning system at work last year?

Yo, lads and lasses. I need some advice or's something. I just got back from uni and realized my housing costs are skyrocketing again! I talked to my flatmate, and we're both freaking out. What's going on with all the housing now? Oh, haven't you heard about the new house prices? It's all over the news. The real estate bubble is bursting and students are getting squeezed, right? Yeah, truly. I've also been noticing that. I've heard loads of stories about students having to move out because they can't afford the rent. It's not just in our uni town, it's all over. Does anyone know more about this? Honestly, I was hoping someone would have a better idea but from what I've researched - oh, and did I mention I studied a bit of Economics at sixth form? - it seems the tax laws and all aren't looking too friendly on students. I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Grace's new tattoo? It's pretty neat. She's always been adventurous with body art. Yes! It's a beautiful design. But the emotional impact is often unexpected. You form strong bonds with families over such a short time and then... you've got to let them go into the world. Right, well I'm back from Cornwall after a week away, and I have to say it's been a real eye-opener. The scenery was breathtaking, and the peace and quiet was just what I needed. Is that right? I've never spent much time in Cornwall. How was it? Did you manage to get out and about? Oh, yes, I did get out and about. I even managed to volunteer a bit with the local YHA, you know, cleaning and stuff like that. It was quite rewarding actually. keeps me active and out of trouble. That sounds like a lovely idea. I've always thought about volunteering, but I've just never really got around to it. You've inspired me now. Might have to look up some local opportunities. You really should. Helps to meet new people and make a difference. And the scenery isn't half bad either. I've always wanted to visit Cornwall as well. The creative classes we have in school could benefit from it, you know? Maybe even grab some inspiration for the next project on lighthouses. Aye, that sounds like a brilliant idea. One of the places I visited was a lighthouse. Absolutely fascinating the way they're built and the history behind them. That's remarkable. St. Ives lighthouse perhaps? No, no, it was another one near Land's End. But the scale and ingenuity involved are simply magnificent. But it's not just about the lighthouses, it's about the journey, the sea, and all that combined makes Cornwall so special. I hope to get there together as a family one day, maybe for a trip. I've been yearning to cycle across Yorkshire in a day, but that's a bit ambitious, perhaps for us older folks. I agree, changing the pace and having more manageable goals would be a good plan for us. I'm sure we can manage. Just like when we used to walk up the hill together as kids. Reminds me, we should see if we can get together to go on a walk in the nearby countryside soon. Yeah, definitely. It'll be good for our health and spirits. Did you catch any part of that cycle race while you were down there by any chance?

Right, so I'm going to make sure to grab beans from the groceries tonight. You know how much I love northern cuisine. Ah, beans! I'm all for various forms of beans. Though I've really developed a taste for pasta now, ever since this one time when we were on holiday in Italy. Wow, Italy sounds amazing! I've always wanted to visit but my postgrad studies have been consuming most of my free time. Now, speaking of food, did you hear that new Italian place opened up in town? Yeah, I've heard about it! They say it's really good. But I'm quite partial to our Yorkshire dishes, just need to make sure to have them occasionally. So dedicated to your roots. It's good though, being connected to where you come from. Definitely. I've found that my upbringing in London has shaped a lot of my interests and also, how I approach work. I'm a little more fast-paced than people from the north often are, or so I'm told. Different strokes for different folks, I suppose. I appreciate it too, it certainly helps when coordinating events, you know? Everyone is from different places, but everyone should feel included, while still showcasing their heritage. Speaking of which, I've been feeling quite included in the group. It's good to keep in touch like this, despite us all having different jobs and interests. Definitely. It's been good having these dinners, it helps bridge the gaps and all that. And relationships, they're always a conversation topic around here, aren't they? I suppose they are. Actually, have you guys heard about that new dating app everyone's talking about? Some of my colleagues who just got back from a conference raved about it, they said it really helps match you with people based on shared interests. Yeah, I've heard of it too. I've been meaning to try it out but I guess changing the status from "single" on my Facebook might be a good start first? Clever way to handle it. But seriously, it can't hurt to try. Though, I've always found that if you're going to meet someone significant, it's usually in situations like this, where you can let your guard down and actually talk. True. And sometimes those are the best kind of connections because they're organic.

Oh, did I ever have an adventure over the weekend! Barcelona was wild. Oh, I wouldn’t say wild, but sounds like you had fun. It was just so much fun, though! The beaches, the food, the nightlife... it was all so exhilarating. I wish I could have gone with you. You know, if it wasn’t for work... We really should have planned a girls’ trip over there. You game sometime soon? Maybe Paris, Paris would be great. I’m not sure about Paris. Though, any time with you is great, but what about the work here? As a mental health nurse, my job can be quite demanding. I get it, you're really important to a lot of people. You need to balance work-life, too. But maybe over the summer? Or even next weekend? That could work. We could look at a weekend break. Now that I think of it, it would be quite relaxing. Relaxing? After all we saw on TV shows last week, I wouldn’t say it was all relaxation, but it was definitely not dull. Yeah, did you see the ending of 'Black Mirror' finale, it still has me thinking... Oh, that episode was wild. And scary. I don’t know if I could watch that again. Exactly my point. Speaking of scary things, though, less serious side of Barcelona was pretty intense. Our hotel just happened to be next to a bar that had a drag show every night. Drag show, really? Yes! It was so much fun. The music, the energy, it was all so vibrant. Did you attend? Yeah, we did. And it was an experience. I bet... Clearly, I need to show you the pics and videos. It was amazing! You will, I’m sure. Anyway, it’s good to be back to a quiet place. Absolutely. I miss the peace and quiet too. Yes, youth can be wild, but it's nice to also appreciate tranquility. Mmm, that's very true. Speaking of tranquility, what did you do over the weekend? Well, I worked some but I managed to catch up on some paperwork and a bit of gardening. That sounds lovely. A bit of peacefulness in a garden. Absolutely. And my family visited. We had a big family dinner on Sunday. That sounds wonderful. Were they all well? Yes, they were great to see. We caught up on a lot.

Ah, lovely to meet up with you again at this seaside gem. I've been meaning to try these freshly baked scones since they moved in. I've heard they use local ingredients which gives them that extra kick. Hi there! Yes, the scones are the best, but the views from here are even better. Can't believe I've lived in London for so long and never taken the time out to explore the coast like this. True. Life as a teacher never gets less busy, but I try to make time for these getaways whenever I can. It's not just about the knowledge I pass to my students, but also the experiences. I've always valued immersing them in real-world settings beyond just the classroom. Absolutely, valuable stuff. As an entrepreneur, I've had my fair share of experiences too. There's the thrill of the challenge and the gratification when you see your idea flourish, but it also comes with its own set of endless tasks and responsibilities. That sounds like a different world! Did you always want to start your own business, or was there something that pushed you towards that path? I've always been a bit of an innovator, I guess. I studied economics at university and even then, I was always interested in how the market worked beyond lectures. After my graduate stint in the City, I realized that I wanted the flexibility and the creative control that come with having your own venture. It's been a rollercoaster journey, but I wouldn't trade it for anything. That sounds like quite an adventure. I've always been curious, but the thought of starting something from scratch and managing all the risks... it doesn't come naturally to me. I enjoy the structure the teaching job provides, even though it comes with its own set of pressures, of course. Right, less stress about the commerce, more about the content. I see, I always thought being an entrepreneur was more fun since you get to choose your projects and so on. But each profession has its own unique stresses, isn't it? Absolutely. You've shared some anecdotes about the early days of your company. I bet that was a thrilling time for you. I can't imagine facing situations where a wrong turn can send everything downhill so quickly. Oh, the early days were wild.

Alright, I'm pretty sure our's is the loudest car in the county right now, love. Yeah, the music is off but our voices are still making some noise. Sorry, couldn't help but share that – do you remember when we started looking for housemates and ended up with those two? Oh absolutely. I'm still not sure why we thought it'd be a good idea. And here we are, stuck with them for a whole year. I guess, in a way, we're lucky. Could be worse, right? Oh yes. Could easily be worse. Like, even Emma's weird obsession with candles doesn't even come close to some of the stuff we've seen. True that. But what really confounds me is Tom, he's just so quiet and elusive. Elusive? He's just antisocial. Well, sure, but at what point do you start to feel a bit worried? He never talks about his day, never confesses his interests... He's just... withdrawn. I thought the 'anti-social but harmless' category was more his thing. I used to think so too, but over time, it's started to feel less 'harmless' and more... concerning. You mean like you think something is actually wrong, or...? No, I don't know if anything is 'wrong' per se, but the lack of effort to even engage or be part of the household makes me wonder if everything is okay in his world. That's true. He doesn't even seem to care if the kitchen is clean. If he does, he certainly doesn't show it. While I agree, changing the subject, we really should set up some house rules. For sure. Especially for kitchen cleaning. And maybe something for us to check in with them more often, just make sure everyone is doing okay. Again, agreed. We don't want anybody to feel left out or isolated just because they're... well, as introverted as Tom. Exactly. We need to make sure everyone is comfortable and connected. But at the same time, I don't want to pry. I know, it's a fine line. But we just need to communicate better as a household. Agreed. Maybe next week, we can arrange a casual 'house meeting' to discuss issues and expectations, see how everyone feels about everything. Groovy. There it is. We're officially housemates now, aren't we?

Ah, marvellous weekend. I managed to get some buns and some cheap veg. The Co-op was having a sale, and I got a good bargain. Oh, that's right. You got out today, isn't it? I must say, it's a welcome change of scenery after being cooped up so long. Indeed, it is. The walk did me good too. Though I'm glad to be back, as the weather's taken a turn. All gloomy and damp. You're right about that. This time of year it's usually crisp, but today was quite lazy. I was going through some old photo albums from when our children were young just last night. Oh, good Lord! Time really does fly doesn't it? It does. It made me realise how much life they've had without us. They're both grown-ups now with their own families, bless them. Off making a life of their own. I never thought I'd see the day. I'm just this side of 80, yet it feels like only yesterday that they were running around with silly grins on their faces. Life's funny like that. It puts its own spin on things, right? Well, it does. But I'm grateful. Grateful for every moment we shared, no matter how hectic or chaotic they may have been. I'm with you there. And we've got each other. That's no mean feat, living in these times where you hear about so many folks that are alone. Indeed. I do feel fortunate. People often speak of falling on hard times. But I suppose measured against what some folks have to deal with, we've been lucky. No major health scares, no big dramas. Just the couple of small things. We've had our fair share of struggles too, but I suppose the key is in how we deal with them. True. I often think back to our own parents, for example. They had a rough deal when they were our age. Wars, rationing, all that. We often wish we took their advice. They could have saved us from so many ups and downs. We could all do with being a bit wiser, I reckon. Our children now, they've got it pretty fine in comparison. I do wish for them and for us that we can find ways to make each day count.

Ah, marvellous to see you both again! You've had a safe journey today? The traffic sounds like it's been a bit of a nightmare from what I've been told. Yes, quite a squeeze on the A1 now and then! But we made it – no major questions on the exam just now. Aye, well, that's grand to hear. I've been wondering, how's the new job going? The maths exams, innit? Oh, it's still a bit of a task. You'll always find one or two surprises. But the students seemed quite keen today. Reminds me of the time I was taken to task for not knowing the correct side of the slide rule when I was at school. They even had an invitation to see the headmaster about it! Oh, Mr... was it Ron? Yes, we both remember that! Quite so. Now, how about you both help with the tea while I set this place up a bit? We need a nice quiet spot for our visitors. Sure thing, Grandma! The kettle, the biscuits, the tea pot... I think I'm all over it. Ah, careful now, lad! You wouldn't want to spill any tea on Aunty's favourite tea set. Remember, Yorkshire tea in the mug, English breakfast on the side. Oh, hush, now. We don't want him thinking that's a maths problem too complicated for him. Everyone laughs. Alright, if you're all set then, let's get this side of the room tidied up and a few treats on the table. The afternoon’s looking grand – warm sunlight and all. What do you think we should do later today? Well, I was hoping we could watch a film or something. Maybe something from the '60s? I heard you both have a lot of stories from that time. Ooh, yes, let’s do that! I’ve always enjoyed telling the stories of when the Beatles came to Hull. And I could show you young 'un the old vinyl records I’ve kept. Sounds like a plan. Dee could set up something on our old record player. Sure, can I help? Of course, but let me first... get you both a drink. While Speaker_1 gets the drinks, the others begin to make tea and biscuits. You know, there’s also the photograph album if you fancy going through that with the young lad.

Yo, lads, what've you all been up to since we last caught up? Yeah, not much really. I've been deep into this new series on Netflix and had some uni work. I've been playing this new PS5 game, it's sick man. Been hooked on it for ages now. Speaking of sick, have you all seen the new ads for health supplements? They're saying it can boost your metabolism and I'm really considering trying one. Yeah, keeps coming up on my feed. I've been considering it too but I'm a bit skeptical. What do you guys think? Honestly, I've been questioning health products in general. There's just so much to research and most of the time it's just based on hearsay or incomplete data. I see what you mean. It's almost like most of the time it's just a buzzword or a fad. But also, if you're in a health situation, it might be worth exploring. Totally. Someone should make a tech platform that helps identify or even automates the research for us so we know which ones actually have merit. That would be a game-changer. Or how about AI predicting health outcomes based on your genetics and providing personalized supplement recommendations? Perfect example of how tech could be used effectively. I mean, we're living in 2022, shouldn't we expect something like that? Evolution of the fitness trackers maybe? I mean, they started off just tracking steps, now they have Cardiograms and sleep analysis. Maybe a health analysis could be the next step. On a similar note, I've been looking at buying some new fitness clothes. Any recommendations? Lululemon or the More's? Both are decent but I found the More's to be more affordable and comfortable personally. I've had good experiences with both but if you want something budget-friendly, and honestly, you don't need a fancy brand for basic stuff like leggings and tops. I tried Adidas' new Studio line. It’s not bad, breathable and well-made. But it can be pricey. Yeah, but if you invest in good basics, they last longer and you won't be buying a new pair every month almost. Makes sense. Also, have any of you tried any new social media platforms? Instagram got a bit too mainstream for me. I tried TikTok but it's not really my thing.

Right, so I think we need to make a shopping list for tomorrow. I'm doing today's dinner and I realized we're running low on a few things. Oh, that sounds like a plan. I need to pick up some bandaids. A bit of varnish, maybe a new book for the questions grandpa asked me yesterday. You remember that one he was asking about the insects? Yeah! I was just watching a video about those things. Like, how there are so many species of insects. Right, let me not get started on that one! Alright alright, no need for a lecture. But yeah, thinking about insects, have any of you experienced anything lately with... erm... biting insects? Wasps, mosquitoes, something like that? Oh yeah! Dad got stung by a bee last week! It was really red and swollen. That's very concerning. Fire ants, wasps, those can be dangerous. You have to be careful. Exactly what I wanted to talk about. For me, it was a mosquito bite and it was so itchy. Anyone know any home remedies to soothe it? I remember my mum used to say put some vinegar on it. Vinegar can help, or baking soda paste. But if the swelling gets worse or if you start feeling unwell, it's best to seek medical advice. Vinegar? That sounds... ouch. Yeah doesn't sound ideal but apparently it works! Or you could use an antihistamine cream. Maybe we should have some of that in the medicine cabinet, just in case. Good idea, we should add that to our list. And by the way, while we're making this list and talking about things we should have, I think we need to address these bugs in our garden. You mean make a trap for them? Yes, and look into repellents, maybe something non-toxic. And we should definitely tidy up the garden, pick up any old leaves or cups. That stuff attracts them. Clearly, I need to do some yard work! Oh, funny thinking you didn't! I know that was his job since this summer began. So, when can we go to that park if we have a better garden? I want to play some football. Maybe next weekend then? We can still go if it's not too hot, I can check the weather. That would be great! We can also invite some of our other friends to come along.

Yo, so I had this absolute craic in P.E today. We have these two teachers, Mr. Green and Mrs. Smith, and they're normally so strict. But today, they switched it up and did this full on obstacle course outside! It was so much fun but now I'm mega knackered. Oh my god, that sounds amazing! But how did Mr. Green and Mrs. Smith pull that off? I mean, we normally just do circuits or something. I know right? And it was weird because even Tom, who normally hates sports, was actually enjoying it too. Maybe they knew something would happen and thought this would keep everyone happy? Idk, but today's P.E was definitely a highlight of my week. That's weird. Do you think they actually planned it from before or something? Also, have you seen that new YouTube channel called "FunScienceWithTrudy"? My mate sent me a link and it's actually really good! They explain science in such a cool way, it's crazy. No, I haven’t. But between you and me, I’ve never been a fan of science at school, so maybe this could actually make it fun for me? Yeah, lemme check that out. Definitely do! And while we're on the subject of educational Youtubers, have you seen "The School Zone" with Mrs. Jenkinson? She's like, so relatable, always giving advice on current school issues. Oh, yeah! I love Mrs. Jenkinson, really. She's always so understanding and cool, and her videos never feel like 'school'. Plus, she's from Cambridge doesn’t she? Yep! Exactly. She's from our town, and it’s cool to see one of us do things like that. But have you heard about this whole debacle with a teacher who was suspended for something on Instagram? She reportedly made some comment about students and it went viral, and now there's like a whole campaign for her to get reinstated. No way! That’s so crazy. I was on Instagram after school and saw some of my friends talking about it. The general consensus seems to be that she’s well-liked but it’s still unfair isn’t it? And it's always one comment that ruins things. Exactly! It’s like, everyone could have a slip-up and almost gone viral at some point in their social media life. But yeah, I think everyone’s hoping she gets back because she’s got a good reputation here.

Oh blast it, haven't been feeling great since yesterday. Jeez, what's up? You look rough. That cold's got you down? Yeah, I really don't feel like myself now, and this weather isn't helping – always something, isn't it? Going from one thing to another. But speaking of 'rough,' have you watched Lloyd Grossman's 'Through the Keyhole' episodes of late? Now that's entertainment if you're stuck at home. Yeah, I love when he does those. It's like seeing the lives of others when you're stuck in yours. But seriously, how are you going to cope with this cold? You're not planning to just tough it out, are you? No, I'm not. Went to the chemist and got some remedies. Also thought about getting a vaccination, but it's already gone out of season this year for the flu, right? That's right, vaccines are usually good for about a year or so. You probably should have gotten yours around October-November, but better late than never? Maybe next year. Agreed. Sigh, different story is the food poisoning I dealt with last week though. I was in hospital for a day. It was quite the experience. Never thought I'd enjoy the food there, but apparently the chicken soup was quite good. Glad to hear you're better now though. Health, it's something we often take for granted, isn't it? But until something happens, we rarely give much thought to it. So true. And talking about taking things for granted, have you seen the progress with hospital tech? The last time I was in one, I saw some really advanced cameras and equipment. More cameras? Yeah, there was an interesting debate in one of my PhD seminars about body language recognition in medical settings. It's fascinating how technology is getting better at reading non-verbal cues and it could really help with diagnosing conditions or changing the way we communicate with patients. That's quite fascinating. I remember on that episode of 'Through the Keyhole', Lloyd mentioned how cameras were set up in certain houses to show off the latest tech. I couldn't help but think of the implications for privacy and security. True. With everything becoming more and more connected and smart, the lines between convenience and invasion get finer and finer. But in a medical setting, especially where it could assist with diagnosis or improve patient care, it's easier to see the benefits.

I've used "queue" first move. "Q" is a great start, isn't it? Gets rid of that pesky high-point letter early. Quite right! And it’s nice to have the board all to yourself for a bit – before someone questions if "queue" is actually a word and debates for five minutes whether it should count. Of course it's a word, dear! It’s a rather common one in our language, especially alongside verbs like "queue up." You'll need it to discuss the Thanksgiving Black Friday sales in America, for example. You're right, of course, Headmistress. So, shall we keep the game on the nice, neutral themes for now? "Food", perhaps, or "Scrabble" itself could add a few more points? While we're on the subject of food, did you all see that article in this month's music magazine about the rise of exotic cooking at home or something like that? Oh, no. What was that all about? The writer argued that while the mainstream news media often dwell on the negative impacts of social media, platforms like Pinterest, Instagram, and even Facebook are democratizing access to culinary diversity for families like ours, who would never otherwise have known about or tried, say, sushi or pad thai regularly. An intriguing viewpoint. I must admit, I found myself trying a new recipe from Instagram last week myself. It's oddly... liberating the way we can experiment with new food and cooking techniques, without needing to be expert chefs or travel to distant lands. Definitely, I've tried a few of those "sustainable meal prep" ideas. It's another way to cut down on food waste and manage budget more efficiently, really. While I agree on changing the conversation to something more positive, perhaps we might steer clear from topics that could lead to family arguments? For instance, not discussing current political issues or today’s traffic jam at the shopping centre. A wise suggestion as always, Headmistress. It’s good sometimes just to focus on something almost universally enjoyable, like our game here or maybe... what music do you all listen to these days? Surprisingly, I still enjoy a bit of Bowie or The Beatles when doing something relaxing like cooking or gardening. I suppose it’s a nostalgic cling to better times. Me too. I find that music like theirs somehow elevates the mundane tasks, gives them a sense of purpose and joy.

Ah, marvellous weekend so far at the TME's working party near Taunton. It's been quite invigorating and such a delight to meet up with so many enthusiastic folks again. Yes, it's been nice isn't it? The atmosphere, though a fair size of work, has been kind of... refreshing isn't it? I find it fascinating hearing all the different stories, especially of successful careers that have led people to this point of life. Oh absolutely, truly fascinating.
