Which reminds me, during one of our breaks I was just telling someone about my early days in the art world, and now I'm reminded of our own kind of 'successful career' experiences. Though I must admit, mine is in a very different field to yours. Tell me, Speaker_1, what did you do? I've heard whispers of an artist and antique dealer, but I never heard you were so involved with inventing and marketing printing systems before. Oh yes, quite the story, actually. Right up until my retirement, I worked in the printing industry, mainly in the development and marketing side of things. We were one of the leading innovators in our field for a while, especially with offset and digital printing. That sounds exciting and no small challenge. Was it particularly demanding? It was its own kind of world, really. The constant grind of trying to stay ahead, technology racing ahead of us at times. But I loved it, especially the intellectual challenge and the pride of seeing a new system we'd developed really make a difference for customers around the world. That’s impressive. I’ve always been fascinated by how technology can change the landscape of industries. Your experiences must be immense. Did you ever work abroad or travel for your job? Yes, quite a bit actually. One of the highlights was our presence at various trade shows in Germany. It wasn't just a display of products, but also getting to know Germans and their culture. There's something about working in a foreign environment that really broadens your mind, you know? Absolutely. You learn not just about the product, but people's ways, their priorities. I suppose that's what makes it so rewarding and challenging at the same time, isn't it? Exactly. It was incredible to build those professional relationships and have conversations about how our technologies could improve their industries.

Yo, Dad, did you know that we're supposed to be studying about the etymology of words and pronunciation in English Language class this term? Ah, that's right, you mentioned that. Are you doing well with the class? Yeah, it’s interesting but kind of tricky. Especially because some of the words don’t make sense if you just look at the spelling. Like, "knight" is pronounced totally differently from how it looks right? Ah, absolutely. That’s a great example. The English language keeps changing over time and it’s influenced by other languages, like French and Latin, that came into the UK. It’s fascinating to trace where words originally came from, isn’t it? Totally, just like how "bicycle" was invented in France but Britain actually really adopted it and now we can't imagine life without them, even though we started with horses and carts. That's true. And with technology, sometimes words get creative too, like "selfie." It's crazy how words come in and out of fashion or change their use so much. I hope I remember all this for the exams! We’re also supposed to be discussing university courses and which ones we might be interested in. Indeed, you should. It's good practice. What kind of subjects are you considering at university? Maybe something like Linguistics or English Literature. I love analyzing how language works and how stories can shape people's lives. Those are great choices. And in Britain, we really have some amazing universities to consider, especially in the South or maybe even in the northwest like Manchester. Yeah, But it's tough deciding. I’ve heard Manchester University offers some really good courses on English and Linguistics, and it's not too far from home. An option indeed. Manchester is also great for events, festivals, and it's a relatively affordable city to live in. Just couple of years ago, they held this massive Miner's Last Lamp and it was amazing to see so many people changing the city. You sure are getting into all these subjects. Thanks, Dad. I really appreciate your input. You're welcome! Anyway, we should probably stop for lunch soon. There's a service station just a few miles up the road. That sounds perfect. I could almost eat a whole quinoa salad right now. You know how into quinoa I am, right?

Right, so I'm going to make homemade Yorkshire puddings. Dad uses to make them when we were little. They're perfect for roast dinners, but I use them for chicken and gravy too. You two excited? Aye, I am! Never had a traditional Yorkshire pudding, only the kind from batter. This sounds interesting. What's the recipe you use? Oh, I've heard about Yorkshire puddings, but I've never had them. Sam, can you tell us a bit about how you make them? Well, it's quite simple, really. You just need plain flour, eggs, milk, and a bit of oil. The trick is to get the mixture just right, not too thick, not too thin. And the cooking process? Is it like pancakes or does it involve different techniques? It's quite different, actually. You need a good, hot oven and a dripping wet tin. Make sure the oil is hot and that you pour in the batter just before it hits the oven so it's still bubbling. Then, you leave it until it's risen and golden. So no flipping or folding like pancakes? I can barely make those without disaster. No, no. Just pour, in and let the oven do its magic. Do you want to try your hand at making them sometime, or do you think you'll stick to the nice and easy roasted potatoes I’m about to start peeling? I’ll probably stick to potatoes, but I’d be interested in watching and maybe helping. I might learn something new, it's about time I got into the kitchen more. That's the spirit! Now, what’s your favorite food? We could make something side of that, or together as a total meal. I'm a bit of a pasta person. A good carbonara or bolognese is always a winner. I love a classic roast beef dinner. With all the trimmings. We can make that. Plus the puddings. It’s going to be a bit of a traditional meal, but I think we can make it work. You’ll need a good gravy, and plenty of veg. How about roasted parsnips and carrots with the beef? I love roasted parsnips! The caramelization gives them such a sweet flavor. Right, I'll get all that underway then. Sam, why don’t you start peeling potatoes while I get the veg and puddings prepared?

Yo, mate, been a while. How's life treating you? It's good thanks, Ian. Just teaching and such. Well, pandemic aside, of course. Right! That's been a nightmare for everyone, hasn't it? How's Hitchin faring? It's been tough, but we're managing. We're lucky to have some decent parks and stuff, so at least we can get out and enjoy some fresh air. That's true! Birmingham is great for that too. You ever try Malley's Fish Restaurant? Or, you know, the canal walks? Idk, I haven't been out much. But yes, Birmingham's a beautiful city. Sports is another thing, though - I read that Brum's teams are doing pretty well this season. Yeah, right? Aston Villa's been up and down but they've got some good players. And football seasons are always a nice distraction, you know? Definitely. Although, I'd never support Villa myself, I respect their passion. I'm a bit more into cricket. Ever played? Sure, I've played a bit. The different levels of the English counties is something fun to follow though, I think? Absolutely. And the finals at Lords - the atmosphere's always electric. Yeah, nice. I'd take you to Edgbaston for a match if you're ever in Birmingham. Now that would be cool, thanks for the invite. Just doing my part! So, how's it been with the new job? It's been great, I love teaching. I just finished my postgrad in linguistics and am enjoying applying it in the classroom. That's fantastic. I've always found language fascinating. Different dialects and all. There's something quirky about the way people in Birmingham say certain things, like 'Bostin' for brilliant. Yes, I've noticed that. It’s these small linguistic differences that can really give you an insight into local culture. Exactly! And sports like cricket are huge in Birmingham as well. Speaking of sports, I heard you're pretty good with the pool? Ah, I like a game of pool every now and then. It's something to do when I've finished working late shifts. But it's not as big a deal as it was back in uni. We had a great game room back in Hitchin. It was a staple spot for socialising. That's cool! I've been meaning to start driving lessons actually.

Right, I suppose we are running a bit behind schedule, innit? Our break time today is nearly over. Yes, it is. But there’s always the tea and biscuits to be had, right? Absolutely! But let’s not forget we also have some other matters to discuss today. Indeed, we do. I was thinking, perhaps we could start with our plans to go to Gambia next year. Oh, that sounds like a plan to me. I’ve always wanted to experience another part of the world, seeing the culture firsthand. Gambia is a great choice. It’s got beautiful natural landscapes and very warm, welcoming people. I read that the driving conditions can be a bit... interesting though. Well, that could add to the excitement! A bit of adventure never hurt anyone, did it? While we are on the topic of travel, did you both ever travel on those overnight buses from Munchausen's film, you know, like the Gambia ones? Ah, I'm not quite sure. Munchausen Syndrome is something different though, isn't it? Yeah, it's about people faking illnesses. That's right, the name actually comes from an 18th-century baron who was famous for fabricating his own exploits. Fascinating. I've heard of it but never knew the origins. It must be quite complex to deal with. I don't think anyone would willingly lie about such things unless... well, the psychological reasons must be very deep. Indeed. Speaking of complex matters, have you noticed the news lately about those donation boxes? The whole debacle about who receives the money. Yes, it’s a right scandal. Seems like they’ve been channelling funds away from the intended purposes. True, but changing the world takes effort. We could perhaps start small ourselves. I was thinking we could make our own donation box. For charity and all. A good idea. We could make banners too, to publicize it. Or even plant some flowers around the box. It could be a nice little community project. I’ll look into that. Perhaps we could even ring the church bell to announce it. You mean like when we used to ring for Harvest Festival? Exactly that! It’s a lovely tradition and it could be a unique way to get the word out. I’ll make some inquiries. How about we discuss the details over tea this afternoon? Sounds like a plan.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that mobile app I discovered today? Its like an interactive cookbook! Oh, really? Interacting with cookbooks on my phone? Is that actually helpful? You have no idea, it's kind of like having a personal assistant chef in your pocket! I'm going to get into cooking a lot more now. But can it actually cook for you? That would be truly amazing. Not quite, but it does give really good step-by-step video guides. Like, proper recipes – not just your usual pasta with pesto and olives. That’s actually pretty cool. Does it have any weird filters like the food apps on Instagram but for real recipes? Actually, that might be a good idea. But imagine if you could scan a real dish and it suggests a recipe? That could be a hit. Is it good for vegetarians and vegans? Some of these apps can be really meat-centric. For sure! It's really flexible on that front. You can select dietary preferences and it filters everything to match. That’s great! My friend has just gone vegan and he's always looking for good recipes to try out. Well, technology is certainly helpful in our lives. A bit scary too, sometimes. Yeah, scary movies never go out of style, do they? What's been the scariest you've seen recently? Honestly, I’m the one that can’t watch much horror. But my brother recently suggested I watch “The Babadook” and the trailer alone was too much for me. Oh, I saw that recently and it’s really more psychological drama than horror, but it does leave you feeling unsettled. I really liked “Get Out”. The whole reversal of perspective changing the tone from horror to scary social commentary was really smart. True – it’s scary for a different reason. But for me, I have a soft spot for old-school classics like “The Exorcist” or “Psycho”. They’re terrifying in a very straightforward way. Agreed! But sometimes it’s the atmospheric tension and the real-world setting that gets to me. Speaking of “real world”, any of you wanting to go on holiday together soon? I’ve been dreaming of a trip this summer. Maybe somewhere... beachy but also with some culture? Yeah, beach with a bit of culture would be perfect. Like, Ibiza, but less party and more historic sights.

Ah, marvellous to see you both again! I've been looking forward to today's visit. How was your journey here? Not too bad, old chap. Got stuck in some traffic but made it here eventually. Mind if I ask you something though? Sure, do go ahead. You used to make those fantastic model cars when we were children. You ever think about getting back into it? Ah, I'd love to, but time seems to slip away so quickly these days. And then there's the space required for all those models and tools! Tell me about it! After years of childminding, I found I just didn't have the space or time for any new hobbies. But talking about cars... did you see the new model of that 1965 Ford Anglia? No, but I've heard talk about it. It's supposed to be a beautifully restored model. Ron, you know how cars used to be my passion? Of course, we've all heard your stories about that 1965 Ford Anglia you had when you were young. Ah, yes, it was my pride and joy! Even the colour, Seafoam Green, was unique back then. It's amazing how different cars are nowadays, isn't it? So packed with technology. Yes, and while I appreciate the advancements, I sometimes miss the simplicity of older models. Precisely! Nowadays, even the most basic features are almost impossible to fix yourself. Just look at the intricacies of electronics in cars today! Exactly! Just last week, my niece had to take her car to the garage because the "check engine" light came on. More than half of the issue was just the fact she couldn't diagnose it on her own because of all the fancy computer systems. It's just not the same. Back in our day, you could easily diagnose a problem and fix it yourself in your backyard shed. Absolutely, sometimes I feel like they build cars not to last for forty years like mine did but to last just until the warranty expires. That's a bit of an exaggeration, Tom, but I see what you mean. Still, it's just frustrating. Cars are getting more and more expensive these days. I recently looked at a new car but the prices are just ridiculous. Exactly! And it's not just the cars. Look at the whole cost of living. I know we're not talking about that...

Ah, I can't believe we're finally moving house! After all these years of just dealing with the hassle of my teaching job, and then the quiet after, I think this could be the escape I've been dreaming of. Yes, it's going to be a big change, but I think it's for the best. And isn't it lovely that we'd be closer to the airport? Next time my sister comes over from the States, she can just pop over! Absolutely, and it will also help us out with keepsakes and sorting out all the stuff we've collected over the years. Speaking of, have you decided which car we're keeping and which we're passing on? I heard cars are very similar to houses in London - just a continuously revolving door of new ones. You're right about that. We discussed it and we think we'll keep our old Nissan because it's reliable and we've had it for ages. It's more like a family member now! But the Mini we bought last year might be a little redundant now. And you're absolutely right about this house move being an opportunity to declutter - although I must admit, I'm not sure I'm ready to part with all my teaching resources! Ha! Well, keeping the Nissan doesn't sound like too much of a challenge for 'decluttering'! But yes, the Mini - its days might be numbered, really. What about health-wise, though? Are we all set for this new location, or should we consider upgrading home insurance or anything? Health insurance in Britain is fairly comprehensive if you have an address, so I don't think there should be any changes there. Plus, I've been keeping up with my check-ups, and the new GP is supposed to be quite good. That's good to hear. We should probably also think about the different environmental factors. Walsall had more pollution in the air compared to what I've heard about the area we're moving to. Right, we should look into that. Although, I've been reading that some parts of Manchester are a bit better than others. It's good we're taking our time to do our research, though. I'm sure we'll be fine. Manchester's a big city but it has a lot of green spaces too.

Mum, I can't believe you mentioned it to me first! We've been looking for my bike for weeks now. How did you find it? Ah, little one, it was quite a surprise. I was at work when one of our neighbors came into the office and told me about a bike that matched your bike's description. What? That’s amazing! But wait, how did my bike even end up there? Apparently, there had been a police raid on a nearby warehouse. Stolen goods keeps coming in there and they were showing it in the local news. One of them, yes, was your bike. Wow, that’s crazy. Did they say who did it? No, they didn’t. The whole point of a police raid is to catch the thieves, not to announce who they were. Got it, I suppose that’s fair. So, you can go pick it up tomorrow at the police station. You’ll need to sign some forms and all, but they’re really helpful about stuff like this. Oh, that sounds quite formal. Do I have to go with someone? You’re old enough to go by yourself, but if you don’t feel confident, I can come with you. Do you want me to? No, I’ll be fine. But thank you for asking. Honestly though, I’m just glad it’s back. Me too, honestly, we’ve all missed it. What do you plan to do with it now that it’s back? Well, I guess the first thing I’ll do is have it thoroughly cleaned, and then I might as well take it out for a ride around Hastings. Seems fitting to celebrate, right? Absolutely. But be careful. I know Hastings is generally a safe place, but still, we’ve had enough bike thefts lately for us to be cautious. Of course, Mum. I won't go anywhere dodgy. Good. I’ll also make sure to teach you some new security measures. You know, like bike locks, marking your stuff with your name, stuff like that. It’s always good to be prepared. Yeah, good idea. I’ll go look into those this afternoon. Good. And since your bike is out of commission, how about we use this opportunity to talk about your college choices. You’ve been quiet about it, so I figure now would be a good time to discuss.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I was delayed by over three hours at Paddington due to signal failure? You mean the one where you had to cancel the dinner plans for the entire family and ended up ordering takeaway? And isn't that one where you got a free ride on the next available train and even got a refund for your ticket? Oh, yes, very funny. But I always say, keeps things interesting, doesn't it? Yes, very interesting. It was a bit chaotic, but we made the best of it, despite the annoyance. Sounds like you could write a novel based on train experiences, huh? Maybe. Though I have to say, our most interesting train story involved the children's contest during a journey from Cardiff to London. Our kids won a prize, but the competition was ridiculous! Children's contests on trains, now that's a dynamic. Yes, and then there's always the different railways in the UK. Each has its own quirks, while the 'Railway Pundits' on the news seem to know so much about the intricacies of train scheduling, but never manage to get their own train on time. Oh, exactly. Rail enthusiasts in Britain are as passionate as sport fans, but we’re always talking about delays and cancellations. Speaking of quirks, weren’t the redesigning the train carriage seat layout? I heard it’s supposed to make more space, but if one’s planning a family trip, it’s still a tight squeeze. The redesigns are supposed to be more efficient, but when you're traveling with four small children, who are already excited for vacation, it still feels like you’re trying to pack sardines. Yes, advanced ergonomics that often make for less comfort in practice for those of us trying to just sit and enjoy the view. And of course, the infamous Wi-Fi on trains – unless you're a hundred miles from civilization almost anytime. Clearly, advancements in technology don’t always translate to a smoother travel experience for passengers. You know, during our company outing to the Smoky Mountains last year, I read this really funny piece about clueless passengers trying to use the train Wi-Fi. It was hilarious. Like using the phrase, "The train is having Wi-Fi issues," and still expecting a reply as if the train is somehow responsible, or worse, apologetic.

I've decided I need a routine or I'll continue to spend my days lounging around and watching too much Netflix. Have you ever had days like that? Oh, all the time. It's like, the days just slip away when you're not intentional with them. I've decided to start with board games. Something about the structure, the challenge, it appeals to me right now. And it's nice, we can play together and it doesn't feel so... screen heavy. That's brilliant. You'll need to choose some good ones though. There are so many new ones out there, but some of them are just a bit too complex. Oh, I suppose we could make that part of the routine as well. We can have "game testing" days. And then decide which ones are worth our time. Brilliant. I vote we start with a classic. Let's play Carcassonne. It's not too complicated, it's strategic, and it's really fun. Sure, that works for me. I'm curious, what's your relationship like with board games? I mean, I grew up playing them with my family, but I know that's not always the case for everyone. Ah, I didn't grow up playing too much, to be honest. It was always computer games, you know? But as an adult, I've discovered a real love for board games. There's something about the company, the social interaction, that I really enjoy. Plus, doesn't hurt that they're a hell of a lot better for your brain than scrolling through social media endlessly. That's very true. I find that, for me, games like these also create a sense of community. I've been playing regularly with some friends from work. It's become a bit of a social gathering, which is really nice. Yeah, and that's one of my favorite things about games like Carcassonne too – it's not really competitive, not in a way that gets uncomfortable anyway. It's about building, about creating, about strategy. It's fun for all skill levels. Speaking of creating, what do you make of the current drinking culture? I mean, it seems to have grown significantly in popularity over the past few years. It's a mixed bag. On one hand, I like that it's promoting social drinking over binge drinking. It's encouraging a healthier way of consuming alcohol.

Oh, wow, this dinner was definitely worth the move. Totally agree! It's been years since we've had everyone together like this. Indeed. Especially now that the old house is a distant memory. I'm still getting used to having an actual kitchen of my own. And to think that I used to complain about the tiny kitchen in our old house. Speaking of keeps changing spaces, how are you handling the whole routine of cooking regularly? Well, to be honest, it's been quite the challenge. I mean, in our old flat, we had the advantage of a city with everything within walking distance. And now, we've got to plan grocery shopping even for the simplest meals. I know exactly what you mean. When we moved, it took me a while to get used to the different shops around here. But I've started following this great local food blog for recipes and shopping tips. Perhaps I could share it with you. That's a lovely gesture. But I think we all need a bit of extra help adjusting to the new place while the kids are still in school. Have you guys considered a storage unit? We've got so much stuff packed up in the loft, it's crazy. A storage unit, that's an interesting idea. I've been thinking about maybe buying some new furniture, but until I get a better idea of what and how much space we have, I don't want to rush into anything. Plus, this would be a good time to sort out what we really need and what we can get rid of. More breathing room in the house could be lovely, especially for the kids when they come back from uni. And while we're figuring out what and how to store items, I hope we're also thinking about medical care. New location, new doc, new everything. Oh, of course. I was just at the doctor's office yesterday, actually. She's really nice, but I'll admit, it's an adjustment. Change is almost always an adjustment, isn't it? I recently changed my GP and it took me a while to feel confident about their advice. But once I got comfortable, it was just as good as the previous one. I guess that's often how it goes. Yeah, you've got to build trust, which can take time.

Mum, I can't believe how much of a difference it's made having that new car. It's like night and day compared to my old banger. I'm glad you're enjoying it. It was a bit of an investment, but it's important to show you care about yourself – and your safety on the road. Definitely, and it's convenient too – fits my bike easily in the boot, and I can just chuck my laptop bag on the backseat. Speaking of keepsakes, I still have your grandfather's old TLS book. Wonder what he’d think of digital versions? I've been reading them on my Kindle – it's handy. Though, there’s something about holding a real book, isn’t there? There certainly is. And the dust, and the musty smell... But, oh, I love being able to carry a whole library with me. It's crazy how similar our choices are, isn’t it? You prefer books for the feel, I prefer cars for the ride. I guess it just shows we value experience over just functionality, even if different experiences. Makes sense. I was thinking maybe I need to start driving more on the motorway though – to get used to faster speeds, and like, road rage. Honestly? I think you’ll cope. Just remember: it's not personal, really. Everyone's just trying to get through the traffic. That's easy to say... doesn't make it easier, though. Last week I nearly had a go with someone who cut me off on the roundabout. Speed and distance, that’s the key – give them space, and keep your cool, as they say. Yeah, yeah, I know. It's just hard when you feel they're confronting you and it's your own space you’re trying to navigate. It’s all about practice. Plus I'm sure in France they handle traffic better anyway. You're always telling us about your sojourns there. They do handle it better, the drivers are generally more patient. Or perhaps it's more acceptance... but yes, driving in France is generally more... calm. Mmm, maybe that’s what I need – a calm driving trip somewhere out of London. Now that's an idea for a treat. A road trip to the coast, maybe? Or explore further into the countryside? Sounds great! I've always wanted to go to Cornwall by car though.

Right, so I'm going to kick things off with my holiday's most hilarious story. You know how I went to Barcelona last year and ended up accidentally being part of a local festival parade? No, I don't believe I do! You involve yourself in local traditions far too much! Oh, it was hilarious! I was out for a stroll and suddenly, this band of people came barreling towards me, and before I knew it, they handed me this papier-mâché hat and a colourful baton. Bloody typical, Amy. Always getting herself into something. ... and then I had to walk through the entire town while being interviewed by a local news reporter. My Spanish, or lack thereof, was stellar. Did you tell them you were the Queen of Barcelona or something? Exactly! Almost. I'm still waiting for my invitation to the palace. You and your Queen title, Amy. Ever thought of starting a new country with just you and your entourage? Stifle yourself, Tom. Do I ever really need an interview by now to get a sobriquet? Can someone, anyone, please explain how Amy can in any universe be part of a local festival? Fine, I don't exactly know how I ended up there. I probably just got the wrong queue. Everyone laughs. Alright, if one Amy can do it, I'm sure two Amys can do it together. I've always wanted to be a drag queen at Notting Hill Carnival. We should totally do it then! Make it a team effort. You'd do great, Sophie! I'm sure your natural flair would shine through. Oh, I've so much flair. I might just steal the show. You could even wear matching costumes. Like, this is a two for the price of one special. That does sound... fun. I'll start looking at outfits and researching tips on how to properly lip-sync. Make sure you're also ready for the inevitable transformation into a Wigan Pier witter. Don't worry, Tom; if she turns into a youth worker, I'm here to support. A Wigan Pier witter is exactly what I want to be. I mean, it would be so convenient, given I'm from that area. That's it! A Wigan Pier witter with a QPR cheerleader on the side. It sounds like quite the extravaganza. But seriously, deep down, aren’t we all just looking for our spot in the sun and our five seconds of fame?

Right, so I've been reading about this fascinating topic of wild winter camping. I discovered that many people these days consider it an ideal activity for disconnecting from the digital world, reconnecting with nature and even as a form of wilderness therapy. It really seems to promote mindfulness and increases our appreciation for nature. Oh, I've had patients who have used it as a form of therapy. Being out in the cold, with minimal comforts, has this... strange way of stripping away distractions. It's almost like facing your own vulnerability. But even so, it must be physically and mentally demanding, don't you think? Absolutely. I've come across several accounts from people who have done it, and they do mention challenges. But then again, those same accounts often reveal a rewarding sense of accomplishment and a deepened connection with nature. It's almost like a form of personal growth. Exactly, and it's not just about finding solace in the harshness of nature. In some ways, it's about reconnecting with our own physical limits and resilience. As someone who organizes study retreats, I've noticed that even a short time spent in nature can greatly improve mental clarity and focus. Oh, I can see that. When I was doing my research, I found this study about the effects of nature immersion on attention and memory. It showed that even a short walk can improve performance on certain cognitive tasks. And then there's the anecdotal evidence from people who spend long periods in solitude in nature, often coming back with a new outlook on life. That is quite interesting, and it might explain why some of my psychotherapeutic patients have recommended wilderness therapy doesn't it? It's a unique way to push the boundaries of one's comfort zone, and yet, it also provides a sense of safety and belonging in nature. More than that, it also provides an opportunity to learn new skills and adapt. For example, learning how to build a snow shelter or start a fire in low visibility conditions can be quite confronting but highly rewarding. It's like a science and art combined. It’s a sort of primitive, advanced skill – I suppose? Yes, I suppose it’s like that. And it truly tests patience, problem-solving, and resilience. It's a holistic experience that influences not just the mind, but also the body.

Yo, mate, did you finish reading that novel you've been banging on about? Yeah, I did. I think it's deep, you know? The themes and all. You should give it a go. Really now? What's it about? It's kind of like a dystopian future where everything is controlled and monitored. The protagonist, she's like a radical trying to shake things up, right? Sounds interesting. Reminds me of some of the films I've seen. You know how much I love films, right? Do we know anyone who's seen a film like that lately? Oh, definitely. I have. There's a new film just out, like it's even happening around us. Everyone's talking about it. It's big themes, big questions. That sounds right up my street. What's it called, again? It's called "The Fourth Wave". It's been getting a lot of attention. But honestly, if it's anything like the dystopian novels I've read, I think you'd really like it. Oh, that sounds quite good. Now I'm curious. The different settings in the films, the how they kind of show what the world could turn into. It's always fascinating to me. Yeah, exactly. And the literature can have quite the influence on them, too. There's always some book that prompts a film. Speaking of which, have you tried that new cereal shop downtown? They're doing a book and film pairing, and they have fantastic artworks and clips and stuff. No, I haven't! That sounds brilliant. Yeah, you should check it out. We can go together sometime. More food for thought, literally. I love the idea of matched food and literature. Exactly. They even have a section for movies that are based on literature. There's a section dedicated to the entire collection of the Harry Potter films next to the original novels. That does make things easier for people like me who like to enjoy both. You know, it can be a bit overwhelming at times trying to keep up with everything. For sure. And it's great because they're introducing you to new stuff almost unintentionally. Like, you go there for the cereal or the coffee and you end up reading about a new author. I can see that. It's like food for thought, but actually it's real food for thought.

Oh, did I ever tell you about the time I was trying to learn how to use Excel and I accidentally deleted my entire lesson plan for the next week? No! You didn't mention that! What did you do? Well, I freaked out for a tiny while. But then, I remembered this thing called "undo" and it saved the day! It was a right learning curve, but once I got the hang of it, it was so useful. Wow, it sounds like quite an adventure! I've seen you use that on your computer sometimes. It looks so complicated! Computers can seem that way, but they're just machines that we tell what to do. So, as long as we can figure out how to give them the right instructions, we're golden! Speaking of machines, I love your old typewriter. It sounds so different from your computer. Do you still use it? Ah, the old typewriter. I love it, but it's mainly for fun now. I use it to write short stories or poems. There's something tactile about the different keys and the sound it makes. Reminds me of when I was younger and my granddad used to show me his at our home in Dartford. Can we hear how it sounds? Can you type something? Sure, why not? "Once upon a time, in a land not so far away..." That sounds like a real story! But it's not just "typewriters that make different noises". What about our Lego? Haven't we been building a pirate ship during the weekend? More like "a structure that looks like a ship... but probably won't float"! Well, it's all part of the fun! You know, imagination is our best toy. Speaking of imagination, what was your Brownie Promise evening like? That was so much fun! We talked about what the Brownie Promise means to us and did some fun activities. And I even got some brownie points for helping everyone during the evening. What are brownie points, then? They're like rewards for doing good deeds or participating. It's part of the idea of being a "friend to everyone and a sister to every Brownie". That’s kind of like our promise, when you took us to that park and we promised to help clean up the litter. Wasn't it hard, though? It can be, but it feels rewarding at the end.

Ah, marvellous weekend. I hope you've had a good one, George. Coffee nearly ready if you'd like to join me. Ah, Alison, lovely to see you. Black and strong, if you please. As usual, George. I wish I could get you to ruin a lovely article about Yorkshire's fruit farms. This is a right scandal, if I'm honest. 'Deserted medieval village to become tractor park!' Can you imagine? I used to love those places. Yes, but development sometimes means progress. It's the usual complaint from village types though, isn't it? What's wrong with a couple of tractors and a history talk? It's just... you know, the character of the place. And it's going to be a nightmare with the roadworks on the A657 next year too. For me, the scariest part is the endless roundabout construction. Sends my GPS crazy enough as it is. Good luck with that. Strewth, the traffic jams will make you wish for a medieval village by comparison. Speaking of traffic, did you see that in the paper about selling ANON's old house? Not at all. How much did they get for it? Oh, a handsome sum, I'd say. I was surprised at the price. You know, I hope whoever buys it doesn't turn it into a monstrosity of a modern house. If they do, it'll be a classic case of 'not in my back yard', will it? You've said it. What’s for breakfast today? Scrambled eggs, toasted bread from the local bakery, and an assortment of jams. I liberated the last jar of Mrs. Higginson's raspberry jam from the back of the cupboard. Ah, now that's the real deal. Nothing beats a good jar of homemade jam. Quite true. You know, I've been thinking about growing some herbs in the garden. Just the practical kind for cooking, mind you. That’s a good use of space. Rosemary, thyme, parsley... They’re straightforward and useful. I'd also love to try growing some elderflowers if I could. I hear the cordial is lovely. Elderflowers? That’s ambitious! You're supposed to be growing herbs in your prime years, not foraging for wildflowers! I think a woman of my scientific background should be able to manage it. Of course, but remember, elderflowers are more trouble than they're worth. Well, if they’re good enough for the Queen when she goes to Balmoral...

Right, so I'm going to make sure to take my multivitamins more regularly. You know how it is, always too busy at work and home to remember. Oh, that's a good idea. I've found that taking the time to do little things like that really pays off in the long run. Yeah, and even if you don't take vitamin supplements, just remembering to eat a balanced diet and get enough of all the different food groups can make a huge difference too. True, keeps coming back to that, doesn't it? And, speaking of eating and drinking, have any of you been to that new Italian place in town? They say the pasta is fantastic. Might have to try it out. No, actually haven't heard of it. But I do know a great little pub just around the corner from my office that serves a wicked Sunday roast. Oh, I love Sunday roasts. Do you think they might do vegetarian options? Almost certainly, most places these days cater for all sorts or dietary requirements. That reminds me, I need to pick up some medication for my sister. She's finishing her antibiotics course and she's all out. Oh, in that case, make sure you get to the pharmacy before it closes. They can be a bit tricky to navigate at this time of day. Yeah, especially as it's late afternoon. And you really can only get certain meds if you have a prescription from the GP, I'm pretty sure. I know, doesn't help that my sister works in the morning and the pharmacy closes at 6. I'd advise you to just ring ahead and ask if they can have it ready for you. Most places will happily hold things like that. Right, good idea. Speaking of GP visits, has anyone else noticed how insistent they are to prescribe you a new medication every time you go? I mean, aren't there supposed to be some kind of over-arching guidelines for these things? I know what you mean. Sometimes, it feels like they just run through the usual tick-boxes without real consideration of whether or not the medication will actually benefit you. However, it's also worth noting that the care you get is generally very good and they do have to follow certain procedures. That's true, but still, I've had experiences where I've been prescribed something that hasn't exactly helped.

Oh, so many topics we've got to cover. I've got so much to share. How's your uni going, then? You're deep into this postgrad life, and I've just recently graduated myself, got a job as a copywriter now. It's going well, thanks for asking! The course is challenging but I'm loving it. A bit of a contrast with my undergrad studies. I've also started doing some programming on the side with occasional survey work to keep me busy. Ah, really? That sounds fun! I've been thinking about maybe picking up some programming skills myself, especially with coding becoming more and more relevant in my role. Maybe I can pick your brain sometime. Definitely, I'd be happy to help. So, how's the copywriting life treating you? It's interesting, I'll say that much! It's a bit more fast-paced than I expected, creative freedom is nice though. But my job involves working remotely most of the time, it's funny seeing everyone else on Zoom and me in their kitchen at home or a coffee shop. For me, a pub is a nice change of scenery. I'm sure it has its perks, but I can imagine how hard it would be if you're a people person, to be honest, not being around an office environment. Absolutely. Honestly though, I'm finding it's not as isolating as I thought it would be. Communication is key when you’re working from home all the time. I'd likely struggle with that, but you've adapted well then. Well, it's not all easy but I do appreciate the flexibility. Late night chats with the team or being able to just take a walk in the middle of the day, it has its advantages. But it can be tough sometimes. It's tough for sure. I've had my moments of struggling with studying and changing cities. Oh, changing cities, that sounds like a huge transition! I've only moved from Kent to London, but even that was a bit of a culture shock. Kent? That's still relatively nearby. I could barely handle Oxford, much less London. I bet. I started missing Kent a lot when I got here, everything was so different. But London has its own charm, it will grow on you. You're right, I hear that.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my online workout class? I signed up during the pandemic and honestly, it was such a lifesaver. It forces me to move, you know? You two should join me sometime! Hmm, online workout classes, really? I'd never have thought of that. I've got a pretty physical job, so I'm normally pretty active anyway. I know, I know. But it's not just about being physically active, it's about discipline. You set aside that time and just do it, you know? Plus, there's this fantastic group motivation too. These people, they're from all over the world - it's quite incredible. Interesting. I can see the value of that. But house prices though, that's something that has kept me up at night. Have you noticed how much it's gone up? It's just... Oh, absolutely! We're in the same boat. It's shocking. I swear, the prices around here are crazier than ever. Now that we've moved this side of London, it feels like we're being priced out of our own community. Exactly. I've just done a rough calculation and our mortgages have increased, not just the house price. It's a bit concerning, to be honest. It's not just mortgages, it's really all the costs that go into maintaining a home. We have to be careful and budget everything these days. I've been looking at cooking more at home to save some pennies too. Ah, cooking! I just discovered this new recipe book and oh my, the food is divine. Have you tried anything new, sisters? Actually, yes. I tried this pasta recipe last week and it's quite good. But Julie and I, we've both been a bit too busy to experiment much. We've mostly been relying on pre-prepared meals or takeaways. I know, right? I've been working from home so much, it's tempting to just grab something quick rather than cooking. You guys should try out this book. It's all about simple meals that are both healthy and delicious. I've made a few of the recipes already and they're fantastic. I'll definitely take a look at it. I might actually need to ditch the takeaway habit soon. How’s the pricing anyways? Well, it's not like we're rich either.

Yo, how's everything going with your side of work, Matt? I have to admit today's been a bit of a slog in the office. Our boss just resurrected this tedious old project and everyone is down about it. Ah, yeah it's all the usual, but I kind of like the questions it brings up. It's making me consider a lot of my own work, the principles and all that. I'm just hoping it gets cancelled or something. All this extra work and it doesn't even seem like it keeps changing anything. Well, it depends on how you look at it really. It might be about proving your value or just riding out the current budget cuts. Prove my value... that's a whole other issue but anyway, did you hear the news about the summer musical that's going on in town? No, didn't hear about it. What is it? I barely know, just saw something in the local paper. It's got a major cast and all that. Should be quite good, especially if it's a decent production of this year's hit show or something. I've heard they often cut costs on those local productions, but the cast is usually quite passionate so it can still be worthwhile. Absolutely. Passion can sometimes cover a multitude of sins. But seriously, even if it's not perfect, it's good to support local talent in any case, right? Agreed. What's been going on over at your end with the budget? It's tight, as usual. We're holding tight and trying not to make waves. But whispers of more cuts are starting to surface. That's always the case just before the final budget is announced. I've seen it happen a few times in my engineering projects too. It's usually a case of keeping things going long enough and hoping you can argue your case when the changing winds arrive. Well, I'm hoping it all goes well on that front. I'm sure we can weather it but I know a few colleagues who are already preparing for the worst. It's nice here. I used to almost live in these gardens when I was here at uni. Yeah, I've had a few walks with the girls from my lecture. Totally worth it, gives you a break from all the work.

Alright mates, thanks for joining me. I have to say today's task of painting the backyard has been quite therapeutic. Hopefully, it'll look much better than it does right now! Oh, you don’t need therapy yet, let’s focus on the physical pain – back pain – which I'm pretty sure we're all going to get out of this. Yeah, okay. But seriously, I’ve been thinking about how the city is changing. I used to love the old shops in town, the ones that had character. Now most of them have been replaced by chains. It’s all a bit soulless, don't you think? Definitely. It’s like they’re erasing our history. I mean, we’re both from Liverpool originally, right? That place used to be so vibrant. Yeah, it was. For me, it was the stories on the streets, the people, the whole culture that made it so unique. Where I come from now , they’ve got so many new developments, but they lack that heart. It’s all glass and steel. Speaking of heart, have you seen the new TV drama that’s really doing well? It’s fantastic acting. No, I haven’t caught up on much TV lately. Busy with lectures and papers. I do love a good drama though, especially one that uses the city as a character in itself. More reason for you to watch it! The way they use the urban landscape to tell the story is brilliant. Reminds me of classic movies we used to love, you know? Absolutely. You know, one of my goals is to write a series on that very topic for my next book: how film portrays and uses urban spaces. Wow, that sounds like a great project. You know, I used to act when I was younger. Might not have gone far, but it was fun and taught me a lot about people and places. I started driving a taxi because it’s like a different kind of stage every day, right? You could say that. Sure beats being stuck in an office all day. You get to see the true city life, hear everyone's story. That’s true. Although, I'll never forget when a famous actor got in my cab. He was very interesting to talk to. Stories, you know? Fascinating. So, how's the driving been going? We need a good taxi driver around, especially with all the changes going on in town.

Oh, look at that! Another beautiful mountain range. I never tire of these Polish landscapes. You're enjoying the trip, aren't you? These mountains are stunning. I really like this part of the trip, the drive through the Tatras – always something new to see. It's so different from what I'm used to seeing back in Cambridge, isn't it? I wonder how our budget's coming along for this trip? Well, we've managed to keep costs pretty low so far. Fuel's been our biggest expense, but since we're driving a campervan, it wasn't as bad as I thought it might be. We're also making sure to buy local produce whenever possible, which is not only making the trip more sustainable but also saving us some money. That's a good approach. We've decided not to indulge too much in the occasional tourist trap, preferring instead to experience the real Poland. Perhaps we'll even pick up a bottle of that before we leave. Now that's a taste of Polish culture. You know, I sometimes think while on this job, teaching English to foreigners, that the most substantial cultural exchange we do is the food we share. It's a bit like language, though – you never really know the depth until you dive deeper. Absolutely! Food, as you said, is a key part of understanding any culture. I remember when we were working over in Spain together, the food was such a significant part of it. It wasn't the giant plates of seafood or tapas; it was the understanding that meals were time for people to come together. Definitely. I just tried to explain that to my students. They were all excited about Spanish food, but when I told them that it's often about the social aspect, they were intrigued. It's funny how often people focus on the food itself rather than the cultural significance. I know what you mean. It's like saying 'let’s have a meal' when what they mean is 'let’s spend some time together’. This trip is also about clearing the clutter, right? Being in nature and minimalism. Yeah, definitely. It’s like hitting a reset button. We’ve taken out only what’s essential and left a lot of the things we don’t need. Surprisingly, it’s made the trip feel more free.

I've got no idea if we can make it to Preston before today's train strikes are over, unless we drive and hope the roads don't get too congested. You know, we could time our trip to just beat the morning rush. If we leave before 9 am, we should avoid the worst of it. But did you check the traffic updates? Sometimes the traffic right outside St Anne's can build up really quickly. Actually, that's a good point. I just checked - it says there's a minor delay but it's manageable. And if we are stuck, hey - it's not so bad to be stuck in a car with family. Everyone gets to relax and share a good story or two. Speaking of stories, have you two heard much about the Hay festival? It's this literary festival in Wales, everyone reads and discusses books. I heard it's really inspiring. Yeah, I heard about that. My cousin went once and said he was really moved by the authors and the discussions on politics and culture. That sounds like fun. Maybe we can plan for a family outing there next year if St Anne's is too far to travel to, right? Absolutely! But first, we need to figure out where to go for lunch. Ah, never a problem when we have a map and know our way 'round. Plus, I saw on the news they're showing that Preston is getting a redesign of the city centre. Maybe we can check it out. Really? That sounds interesting. But what about the commerce there? How are the shops and supermarkets? I've heard they're still quite solid. There's even a new one that just opened recently and it got good reviews. But I guess changing the city centre might affect some things. Well, let's try for that new supermarket after we handle our shopping and head back home. We need to check if we need anything from the list for tonight or the rest of the week. Or perhaps you can go through the list and just send the shopping to the nearest store. With the train strikes and potential traffic, why bother ourselves? You're right. That's a genius idea. I'll do that. And with any luck, we'll all be back home before you've sent the order, if the traffic cooperates.

Oh, golly! Look who's banging on the door today. Our surprise guest, Grandma Dot! Welcome back! I've been meaning to clear out the attic and downsize for ages. Want to lend a hand? That's grandma coming back to the nest! It's been ages since she's visited. I wish I could get her to clear out her own attic. The last time I saw her it was so cluttered... Wow, really? She's here? That's epic! Has she got any cool new tech I can have a look at? I bet she's got tales upon tales of when 'tech' meant the TV making noise. Yes, but I'd love to hear them, as much as she loves your games. And you know, these stories are just as valuable. They help us understand the world through their eyes. For sure! We could even record them and make a video archive or something. That would be so cool! Good idea, grandson! But let's not overload grandmother today. Dot, dear, come in, come in! Meanwhile, I've got her favorite tea all ready for her. Grandma, will you tell us about the old days? Or show me that old Nokia you always keep saying you still use? Oh, if only I had that Nokia here. You know, it's got more features than your games. You're right, grandma. It does! But can you play games on it? I think what's more important than that is sharing our time together. Like when we cleared out her old room – it brought us some lovely photos and stories. Exactly. And it's surprising how much we find emotional value in objects that seem worthless to others. This trip might be about more than just clearing stuff... Clearly more than clearing out junk, huh? Actually, it could be a good chance to talk about mental well-being. We all could use some help with finding emotional balance. Indeed. I've felt the weight of staying still, not really doing much. Not moving forward feels like… drifting. How about you, Dot? Do you ever feel like that? Is grandma drifting? I never thought about that... We all face it in different ways, dear. It's a part of life, especially during retirement. It's hard to stay motivated when everything feels so still. The world goes on and you feel like you're just on the sidelines.

Yo, mate, check this out. I just got this new laptop. It's got a solid-state drive and 16GB of RAM. Speeds are insane. Oh wow, that's pretty good. Is it better than the one that just died on you, though? Aha, no contest. This thing is a beast. That's a great laptop, but I've heard you can ruin SSDs by fracturing them if you drop the laptop. Does it have shock protection? Yeah, actually it does. This thing has multiple shock-absorbing points. That's good. I've heard stories of laptops getting messed up from just being dropped accidentally once. Tell me about it. I've seen it happen to my sister's old laptop. Anyway, what software have you got on here? Well, it's pretty standard. Windows 10, Microsoft Office, Adobe creative suite… and I've installed some good photo and video editing software because of my job as an artworker. That's wise. As an English language instructor, I use quite a bit of Microsoft Office, but software for video is always handy. I just use it for surfing the web and watching YouTube. Especially if I'm looking up video guides on gardening. Fair enough. YouTube can be helpful for all sorts of stuff. Speaking of which, have you tried ASMR videos? They really help with relaxation sometimes. Yeah, they're alright. I prefer watching videos on fixing old computers, though. There's something satisfying about bringing back an old machine to life. There's also some good tutorials on fixing or improving your computer hardware on YouTube. Seems like the Morecambe twins are making a comeback with their YouTube vlogs. I noticed a lot of their content centers around retro tech. Yes! I watched one of their videos and it really took me back. I actually grew up playing Sonic on my old Sega Mega Drive. Retro tech is cool for nostalgia, sure. But for me, I prefer newer tech because it's just more efficient. Though, I do have an old Panasonic TV which still works fine. I could use a new TV myself. Mine's been playing up for weeks and I've had to manually adjust the channels. I might look into that topic for next week's lesson plan. Could make for an interesting English conversation topic – current vs. outdated technology. True that. You could also talk about this in the context of hobbies or interests.

Oh, I'm so glad we decided to have a catch-up over coffee here. This bistro looks wonderful and the atmosphere is so cozy. It's been quite a while since we last met and talked without distractions. I'm glad we could find some time despite our busy lives. Absolutely. It feels like ages since our last proper chat, actually. Now, shall we start with this? This bistro is fantastic, isn’t it? I've never been to Tarnow before, so this is a pleasant surprise. It really is. The interior is so warm and inviting, not to mention the food looks amazing. I read online that the chef is Polish but has worked in various places abroad, so that might explain the modern yet traditional mix here. That sounds like a creative fusion. While we're at it, let's admit it's been a while since we both felt truly settled, or whatever settled looks like right now, or even if it's something we still want. Settled... that's a word we often use when we’re trying to reassure ourselves things are fine. But don't we all crave a little bit more definition or at least stability, given our varying circumstances? Honestly, yes. Speaking of which, how have things been in your job as an English teacher? It seems like you're doing great, but I know that 'fine' can also hide a thousand unspoken struggles. Exactly. The 'fine' facade, we've both worn that at one point or another. As for my job, it's been rewarding but exhausting, a bit like the blurred boundaries between work and personal life. Especially since the pandemic ended, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. I know exactly what you mean. Being an English teacher, especially online, must mean dealing with a lot of people struggling – emotionally, personally, academically. That can't be easy. On a different note, what about your fitness journey? I remember you were into yoga a year ago. Ah, yes. Yoga. It's been a bit sporadic this year, to be honest. I've had to deal with some health stuff and personal issues which have thrown me off balance. But I've started doing Pilates more regularly. It gives me a sense of control and keeps me grounded. That's great... control and grounding are exactly what we need in life sometimes.

Yo, anyone hear about that weekend Dorset Steam Fair?? Seems like it's going to be super fun, especially for us who love all things old and steamy! I talked to someone who said there are loads of restored steam trains and tractors, really cool vintage stalls and even live music! Ah yes, I've seen the advert for that one. But do we need to buy tickets or can we just show up? I'm not sure I'm up for dealing with the hassle if we can avoid it. Well, according to the website, they recommend buying tickets in advance, especially if you want to try any of the rides. They say it gets pretty busy at the weekends, so it's probably best to get them online early. That makes sense. Do you remember last year when we tried to get tickets for the ferris wheel on the morning and ended up waiting in line for ages? Let's not repeat that again. Ron, you know how it is, the youngsters love these things. But honestly, I couldn't care less about it. Just make sure there's enough seating and accessible loos for me. Yeah, and they should have some accessible activities, right? I noticed when we looked at the website that they mentioned something about activities for disabled visitors. Indeed, the details show that there is a special wristband for visitors with disabilities, which gives them access to priority queues and specific areas for wheelchair users. Plus, some of the stalls seem to have large canopies or indoor venues for those who can't stand for long periods. We might want to check and make sure these are easily accessible from the car park too. Good, good. I'm more concerned about my poor joints than anything else. And let's consider the property prices side of things, hasn't property in Bournemouth, and the wider area, gone up a lot since we first moved here? Oh, absolutely. It's shocking, really. There was a report in the local paper last week saying that house prices are nearing record highs. Makes me glad we got our place when we did. Well, I suppose it's good news for us as homeowners, but it's not helping for anyone trying to get on the property ladder. True. It's pretty concerning for young people like me, just starting out and maybe thinking of getting my own place soon.

Ah, marvellous to see you all again! I've missed you dearly. How have these past months been treating you all? Everything's been very well, thank you for asking. We've been quite busy with our little ones at school, and the weather's been kind – no major questions there! Yeah, it's been okay, but the weather hasn't been so good lately. It's always raining! I know, I know. That rain can be rather relentless at times, can't it? Especially in this town. You'll tell me if I'm saying something wrong, but don't you think our part of the country gets more than its fair share of rain? Haha, you're absolutely right about that. But we Northern souls have grown quite accustomed to it. And speaking of rain, has anyone ventured out to see the latest performance at the local theatre? Oh, didn't know you were interested in the local theatre? That's actually something we plan to do this evening. We heard it's a bit of a quirky play, but it's got some great reviews. Really? I've not heard much about that. I prefer the classics myself but I'll definitely keep an eye on it for the next time they host something more my style. Speaking of which, I saw there's an upcoming performance at the church – quite the technology involved for a piece on the origins of theatre, if I understood correctly. Oh, yes! They're trying really hard to keep things fresh and modern. It’s all about reaching out to the younger audience these days, don't you find? But it's nice to see the church stepping into the 21st century, even if it's just a bit. And let's not forget about Twitter – the young man here seems to be a bit of a fan of the local Twittersphere. I'm always getting caught up on what's happening in town before I find out from anywhere else! Yeah! I follow all my favourite football players and some local gossip accounts. It’s really cool to see what people are talking about. Fascinating, really. It’s wonderful how technology has connected so many of us. Though one does wish that social etiquette hadn't got a bit lost in the process – it seems some don't know when to turn it off or when to mind their words.

Oh, did I ever tell you about's Dad's story when he took ANON to the dentist? It was hilarious! He was so nervous, insisting that his teeth were all fine. Oh, yes, please share! We're on questions today! Yeah, and Ashaad's friend was telling me about a hearing test he had to take. I didn't know such tests even existed! Well, both of those keeps coming up due to Easter. You see, both ANON and his closest friends, like Ashaad, have birthdays around Easter. ANON just had his and I was wondering if you've heard Easter chocolates are just like maths: you can't consume them all at once! No, I hadn't thought about that. But what about Monets? My teacher did project with us on Monets before the school break. Oh, that's interesting! ANON brought back a painting from his school trip, it's quite adorable. They went to the National Gallery. I love art. Have you ever been to Norwich to the gallery? There's a beautiful Monet exhibit there. No, but I'd like to. Speaking of which, I also took ANON on a school trip recently. Well, actually, it was to a farm to learn about radishes. I know it sounds strange but it was actually really fun! They even let us plant some. That sounds awesome! I would love to learn about radishes. It was fun. We even learned that some radishes can be used in art, not just food. I didn't know that. But do you think it would be good to take them for another trip now that we’ve had birthdays? That's a great question! While ANON's birthday was just before Easter, I think he'd really enjoy another school trip. What if we asked the school for another one soon? Like just before the summer break. That’s an idea worth exploring. But first, let's figure out the math: Is it even possible given the schedule and availability? And what about ANON and I, should we have a joint birthday celebration now that we share the same day? That would be fun. Maybe a joint birthday party that involves radishes or this year, some Easter chocolate-making? That sounds like a recipe for disaster! I mean a recipe that sounds delicious! I love that idea! Alright, so it seems we have our summer plans sorted out.

Oh, God, Rachel! You should've seen how Grace reacted today when she found out we were having fish and chips for dinner. Literally, talked about it for the whole morning! Aww, yeah, Grace, she’s got a massive love for food! But honestly, don’t you sometimes wish we could plan and cook meals together? It feels like a chore sometimes, especially after a long day at work. Oh, absolutely. It would be so nice to have that extra set of hands in the kitchen. You know, it's funny, during uni we had such lazy schedules – always had time to try out new recipes and cook together. Yes, those were the days when our cooking was more about having fun than actually cooking something edible. Like the time we decided to make sushi and used pre-made sushi rice because we thought we were too lazy to make our own? Oh, God, or the time we tried to make a cake and forgot to add sugar and it was so bitter it made our friends' faces twist in disgust. Good times, good times! Yeah, those stories always bring back some good memories. Speaking of things we love, isn't it time we start really putting some effort into planning Grace's birthday? I mean, she's becoming such a big girl. Absolutely. We can plan something fun, maybe a picnic at our favorite park? Yeah, that sounds lovely. More food festivities! On that note, did your mum say anything about coming over for dinner before she leaves for her holiday? She did. She'll be bringing her famous apple pie this weekend. Oh, perfect! I've missed her pies so much. Yeah, and we'll actually get some domestic help for a change. That's almost too much to ask for in one weekend. Speaking of domestic help, we really need to discuss our finances more. I mean, it’s not just about our immediate expenses but also for the future. We've been pushing it off for a while now. I've been thinking, maybe we should start setting a budget that really considers our long-term goals. Like saving for a house, preparing for future health expenses, and maybe even planning for children. Absolutely. Both of your parents retiring soon too, so we might need to start planning how to support them, financially or otherwise. Yeah, family support is a big part of our future plans.

Ah, marvellous weekend. I remember when I was a lass, I'd often take long cycle rides around Almondsbury and the surrounding countryside. Times were much simpler then, don't you think? Indeed, indeed. I've just thought of something, though. You know, when I was working as a teacher at St Peter's School in Ramsgate, we had access to a few ‘perks’ that now sound almost scandalous, right?  laughs  Oh, I've got one. You know, alongside all the usual benefits, dentists in the NHS used to be treated to 'lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon.'  chuckles  Yes, that's just like the time I spent as a dental surgeon. The NHS used to have this odd little initiative where they would send us on guided cruises to attend lectures and seminars while at sea. Quite a perk, really.  laughs  It's unbelievable now, isn't it? Off we'd go, floating lectures. Someone should make a comedy about it. For sure! We could call it 'Teeth and the Sea'. Anyway, speaking of different times, the affordable bargain trips we took back then—how I wish they existed now.  nodding  I hear Prague's on sale. A few weeks in Prague for what we'd spend on a couple of meals out now... A walk in the park, so to speak. Indeed. And getting into those fully booked theatres, exhibitions—they never said no thanks to a retired teacher or dentist.  smiling  I remember how we could always seem to 'persuade' the box office to find us one more ticket. "Just a retired dental surgeon who just loves the arts..."  chuckles  I'd add "who just happens to have skills valuable to mankind". It was usually enough. While you're planning your next trip to Prague, we've also been discussing our local town. Yes, it's been such a shame to see what used to be such a quaint, bustling town fall into disrepair. The old architecture, the local shops... And yet, I still see the potential. There's something almost romantic about bringing it all back to life. We could start with those old buildings. If we just rethink their use. Turn that old grocery store into a local artisan collective, perhaps. But it won't be easy. Sure, there was that application for a solar farm down... Oh yes, that latest decision just came in.

Alright mates, so while we're housesitting in Australia, spare time can be quite abundant, right? I was thinking, we could harness this time to brainstorm some ideas for a small business in the education sector. As we're both quite passionate about effective communication and learning, maybe there's a way to develop some kind of innovative learning materials? Absolutely, that sounds like a fantastic idea! I've been noticing a lot of the children I've come across, they're so innately comfortable with technology and even how to digest information digitally. Think about it - if we developed case studies or even animated, moving-image educational content, we could have a winner on our hands. Exactly! And let’s think broader than just traditional digital platforms. Everyone’s always on their phones but when it comes to education - especially making it fun and interactive - we could have a real competitive edge. I remember when I did project work at university, case studies were so effective in helping me understand complex concepts. But if we incorporate moving images and animations, we could make it even more engaging. That's true. I've noticed this trend in schools and it certainly helps keep students engaged. Now, if we can create visually appealing, contextual content that's applicable across the curriculum... that's gold. Kids in particular respond so well to stories and visuals to learn core concepts, like in language, history, or even technology. Absolutely, and it's not just children. I've seen it really work with adults too when we’re trying to get a message across. It’s about marrying the content with the right delivery doesn’t it? But where do we see this material being used? Schools? Organizations? Private tutoring? A great question. Schools could definitely be one market, but I also see potential for organizations looking to upskill their staff or for private tutoring services looking for unique value adds. Perhaps even for people looking to learn new languages in an immersive but engaging way. We could target online courses where learning material is especially essential. Fantastic. So we build our own content, own platform or partner with existing ones? That's a bit of both, I would think. We have the skills and expertise to create premium content. We could almost upskill ourselves in the process. Maybe use this time to develop a prototype and see if we can get some early adopters to test it out.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time we went to Brighton and nearly got lost in those old winding streets? It was bizarre, but utterly beautiful. You mean the one where we almost got into the Royal Pavilion by mistake? That was hilarious. I still can't believe we had to navigate through that town like it was a maze. Yes! Exactly! And you of all people should know how I love mazes. Well, I'm glad it worked out in the end. We had such a great time after all. Absolutely. And the sea wasn't just a beautiful backdrop - it was like another character in the story. Dramatic, but always present. Reminds me of old fishermen’s tales that I studied back in my folklore course. That's true. The sea has been both a source of comfort and conflict for humans throughout history, hasn’t it? It fills you with a sense of awe, but also a bit of fear, don't you think? Very much so. I remember this one story about a man from Cornwall who spoke of the sea as if it had a personality of its own. Always in conflict with the land, but at the same time, there's this deep connection. It's as if the sea knows secrets we don't, or maybe it just reminds us of secrets buried deep within ourselves. That is a fantastic way to put it. I never thought about it that way, but now I can see how it applies to so many things. The sea is the giant that guards our shores, but it's also the one that reveals all our mysteries when we dare to dive deep. Exactly! And I just thought, isn't that a metaphor for so many areas of our lives? If we're brave enough to face what's deep within, we might confront fears, and find treasures we never knew we had. You always do that, don't you? Turn a simple conversation into a deep philosophical discussion. I suppose that's one of the reasons I love talking with you. Well, I have to pick up where the scholars have left off, don't I? Even if it's just over coffee or a walk like this. And who knows, maybe one day we'll trade our lecturing roles for something a bit more adventurous.

Oh, did you see that?? Did Kim Kardashian just wear the same exact outfit to two different events within a week? I don't know, fashion choice or just running low on ideas? No, but seriously, though! That's quite something. I've seen her pull off some really classy looks but those definitely felt a bit... out of character. Maybe she's just out of inspiration. Seriously though, even if it is lack of inspiration, at least it's not a repeat error most of us could make. I've had lazy days where I just pull out the same dress I wore last week because I couldn't decide what else to wear. Agreed. But let's talk about something more constructive. Have any of you been keeping an eye on the biggest fashion trends of this year so far? I feel like I'm a bit out of the loop. Hmm, I've been hearing a lot about the rise of sustainable fashion. People are starting to make more conscious choices, which I think is really positive. But I suppose that's more of a lifestyle choice than a trend, per se. Exactly, which is actually kind of neat. It's nice that fashion can be so in line with the current climate issues and public sentiment. It really influences people's mindsets, doesn't it? Totally. I feel like it's also pushing designers to be more inventive with materials and production methods. It's fantastic for the environment and it might actually help with the "fast fashion" problem. Well, there's the elephant in the room. The issue of fast fashion has been really on the forefront of discussions lately. And let's not forget about those who are truly setting the trend in this category: the students. Yes, the students. They're the grassroots influencers nowadays. All those TikTok fashion challenges and youtuber collaborations are a game changing force. Yes, I mean, who needs professional advice when you can just follow someone's outfit of the day TikTok. But I mean, at the end of the day, real change in fashion would be if the leading brands took up this sustainable mantra. Agreed. But realistically, as consumers, I think we do have a lot of power. Our choices and what we support do make a difference. I agree. But it's also important for us to be informed consumers.

Mum, I've been meaning to show you this. I took these photos during my photography club. I really enjoy it, even if it's just practising after school. Oh wow, they're really good! You really have a good eye for composition, haven't you? Which one do you think is your favourite? I reckon the one of the beach at sunset. The colours were really dramatic that day. I'm glad I managed to capture that. Well done. It's nice to see you get out and about with something you enjoy, even if it's just for a couple of hours after school. Yeah, it's a really good break from studying. Though, to be honest, there is this one thing that's really stressing me out at the moment. University applications are coming up and I'm really anxious about them. Ah, I remember those times all too well. It can be really daunting, thinking about the future like that. What's your fear? Is it just about whether you'll get into the college you want, or something else? For me, it's a bit of both, but also what if I don't know what I want to do? I know everyone says you don't have to have it all figured out yet, but it’s still quite scary. Yeah, it is scary. But remember, most people change their minds even after they start college. Some people still change their minds even through university and into their careers. It's okay to not be certain, and it’s never too late to make changes. I wish that made it feel less scary. It's scary but it's also exhilarating. The future is full of possibilities. And who knows, you may do something completely unexpected and love it. Okay, that's a nice way to look at it. Thanks, Mum. Always. You know, you might want to talk to some of the older kids in your photography club. They might have some good advice since they've already gone through the university application process. Yeah, that's a good idea. And speaking of universities, are you finally going to take up that photography course you've been mentioning for ages? I might just have to this year. It's been on my mind for a while, and we've managed to save up a bit.

Ah, marvellous to see you both! Just got back from taking a walk. It's a beautiful day, isn't it? The sun's shining, and the birds are singing. Got some of them young ones flying out of their nests today. Morning, dear! That sounds lovely. I'm glad the days are starting to get a bit longer. Speaking of birds, have you heard about them cockerels that have been invading our street? Irritable little buggers, I'd say! Oh, yes! We've got one at the bottom of our road. Keeps me up most mornings, doesn't it? Even with my old bones, I could've done with a bit more shut-eye. Can't seem to sleep properly any more, you know? Tell me about it, dad. I've been reading up on 3D printing and might get started on some of those sleep gizmos people are using now. 3D printing? That seems complicated, doesn't it? I'm not sure if I could get my head around it. Though it's interesting, I suppose. I remember when I was younger, the only thing we had to print on was the paper.
