It was quite a challenge but it's usually the ones that are a bit tricky that prove to be the most rewarding. Sounds similar to managing a project in operations, just with different variables. I had to work closely with our design team earlier this year to overhaul our project management system. Lots of detail to handle but it paid off in the end. Absolutely. And looking forward, I'm thinking of trying out some new software for the freelance work. But first I need to tackle this wine tasting trip for the weekend. Speaker_2 : Wine tasting trip! Is that with dad? It is. He's the wine enthusiast of the family and this weekend we're heading to the vineyards of France. It’s a bit of a treat for us, really. Speaker_3 : Ah, so a couple of old friends are combining our passions. I've been meaning to get more into wine myself, actually. You're going wine tasting? That sounds incredible! I wish I could join you! Well, maybe next time, kiddo. But tell me, what’s your favorite wine? We could look into that for future family festivities. I don't really know. I've only had a few sips of juice or something when we had cake at parties. Speaker_2 : Because, of course, juice and wine are basically the same thing. Speaker_1 Ah, but I'm sure you'll develop a taste soon enough. Actually, what about skiing? Did we ever settle on a plan for the winter break? Yeah, I was thinking about the slopes of Austria. Got any preferences? I've never been skiing! Is it fun? I heard it's quite difficult. It is challenging, but also very rewarding and a lot of fun. I've been learning for a couple of years now and it's great to hear the laughter and see the excitement on the slopes.

Ah, look at this one. We were in Japan; these are some of my favorite photos from that trip. Do you remember the little coffee shop we stumbled upon down by the river? Oh, absolutely! That was such an interesting place. And isn't that one of the most beautiful photos I've ever seen? This one, I took it at sunrise. The colors were incredible. I've always been fascinated by how different cultures experience and appreciate nature. That's interesting. Do you think having a more nature-oriented perspective in your life would make you like the badgers here more? Perhaps. But I have to say, even with that perspective, I still find it hard to warm up to the badgers. I know what you mean. But it's fascinating to learn about them. Did you know they've got an amazing sense of smell? They can identify or even remember scents years later? That's comforting. So they can "remember" all the times they've dug through the garden? Exactly! Do you remember when we first moved in and they started visiting our garden? Oh God, yes. It was like an old sitcom. The badgers were like our new housemates we'd rather not have. I was thinking of showing that video to the kids next time we're talking about different animals. Oh, do let the kids see. They should know what's waiting for them when they grow up, digging holes in the garden. Alright, alright. But they are cute in their own way, right? You'd think after all these years I'd be a bit more appreciative. But I'm still more for foxes. And I thought only me and the dogs favored foxes! Nope. It's a British thing. Definitely. You know, our trip to Japan really taught me a lot about slowing down and appreciating small details. Even finding that coffee shop was about being observant and open to any adventure the day might bring. That's such a good thing to keep in mind. Maybe next time the badgers visit we'll make it a point to sit outside and appreciate the little things. That's the spirit! Maybe we'll even do some photography, badgers and all. Yes, but keep it at a safe distance this time! Of course. No more taking close-up photos of badger's faces. Speaking of photography, should we make more of an effort to take time for photos with the kids?

Yo, mate, did you hear about James' latest trip to Ireland? He was telling me about the craic he had. Whole bunch of new experiences, from skinny dipping at the cliffs to trying garlic cheese fries. Ha! Sounds like he found his own little piece of paradise. I'm not sure I'd have the guts to go skinny dipping, but the garlic cheese fries sound like a brilliant idea! Oh, I'd love to go to Ireland. I've always been fascinated by how it's so different from England, yet still so similar. Yeah, I've been to Ireland a few times for surfing. It's stunning, really. But did you hear that the water is surprisingly warmer than you'd expect for the location? Definitely needs a little taste test though! And what about you, Sarah? How's the café going? Ah, it's fine, thanks for asking. Working long hours, but it's good. Did I tell you about this new Jewish recipe book by Claudia Roden I've been devouring? The falafel recipe is a game changer. Oh, I’ve tried a few of her recipes. The Sephardic ones are the best. Ever tried her recipe for sambousek? It’s like a mixture of a spinach and cheese pastry. No, I haven’t. But I'd love to try it. Speaking of Jewish food, have any of you heard any good Jewish jokes recently? Oh, they're always a treat. Let me tell you one: "Why do Jewish people have such big noses? Because the air is free." And let me add one. "What's the difference between a Jewish mother and a Rottweiler? Eventually a Rottweiler lets go." Those are good. My aunt, she always loved those jokes but never let us forget to add the disclaimer that it's all in good fun. Definitely. Always good for a laugh. You know, it reminds me, I saw this new photo app on my phone that uses AI to convert your 2D photos into 3D. You could essentially walk around the picture almost. That sounds amazing! I love advancements in tech, especially when they're about photography. Totally makes sense thinking about how it will be used. But it also brings up questions about privacy and data use, doesn’t it? Yeah, privacy is a major concern. But the idea itself, it's a really cool concept.

Alright mates, so who was your first ever crush from theme parks? Oh, for me it was definitely the 'Ride of the Dragon' at Alton Towers. It was so thrilling and scary at the same time, and I was about 13 at the time. Wow, I knew Alton was popular but never knew "Ride of the Dragon" was your first crush! But actually, I've always had a thing for the 'Reverse Bungee' ride even though it is now replaced. I can't say I've ever been on a reverse bungee, but your choice is just as valid! You didn't miss out on much, did you? And now you can't even visit them because of this blasted pandemic. It's been a real struggle this past year. I mean, I've been trying to distract myself with computer games but they just aren't the same as the real deal. Completely understand. I'm currently relying on games more than ever right now, but I do miss the graphics of the older ones compared to the newer, more realistic ones. Ah, the old games had charm, didn't they? But they also had their frustrating moments, couldn't unlock certain levels or characters without spending hours. Or the constant loading screens! I'm also getting into Game of Thrones books. There's something about that type of world-building that really captivates me. Speaking of captivating, did you ever read the Game of Thrones series? I couldn't pick up the books after the first one but the show just pulled me in, unlike anything else I've watched. Yeah! I got into the show after most of my friends started watching it. And then I almost immediately read the books just to see the real depth. The way George R.R. Martin writes is amazing! It's like he's painting a detailed picture rather than just telling a story. But now I'm more drawn to the Border Security series, it’s really given me a new perspective on the challenges our borders face.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my attempts to learn how to row? It sounds easy, but trust me, it's harder than it looks. I even managed to tip my boat over once! No, you haven't. That's hilarious! I'm not sure I've had any luck with kayaking either, but I suppose every adventure starts with a little disaster, doesn't it? Absolutely. But, talking about water sports, do you have any advice on how to dress for wet weather? I've been kayaking in the Cambridge lakes and, well, I've ended up quite soaked more than once. Oh, definitely! You need good quality waterproof gear. Sports shops here usually have a good selection. But even if you're just going to the lakes for a day out, it's worth dressing appropriately. Exactly! I've been going with just an ordinary waterproof jacket and it seems to work, but maybe it's time to invest in something more professional. Perfect. I've been recommending a brand called Kokatat to my students. They're quite affordable and certainly effective. Ah, I'll look into that. Also, I had the most wonderful time seeing my younger cousin rowing the university team. She's been doing it since she was a teenager. It was lovely meeting her at the university – I hadn't seen her since we were kids. That's lovely! It's always wonderful when family members pick up similar interests, even if they couldn't have been more different in their youth. Yes, exactly. It's moments like those that make me realize how much influence family and our upbringing have on our interests and passions. Absolutely, and it's also interesting when family connections create new events to look forward to. On that note, did you hear about my family? My brother had a bit of an episode with his health recently and it really took us all by surprise. Oh no, I hadn't heard. I hope he's okay? No news is usually bad news in these situations. Thank God, he's recovering. It's been a stressful few weeks though. They've ordered more tests, but so far, it looks good. That's a blessing. Family health scares can be so distressing. Indeed. It's also made me value our own health more. We're not getting any younger, after all.

Yo, Dad, did you hear about how strict they've become with texting these days? They nearly banned us from sending text messages during exam season! Oh, yes, well, that's just to minimize distraction, really. I remember when it was all about Morse code. If phones were banned, questions were asked if it was Morse code involved and if it was, then it was allowed. It's all about focus, dear. Morse code? Now that’s old school! And fun too! Exactly! Anyway, Dad, why don’t we make a day out of it and actually go see some antiques? Might inspire some game ideas.

I was reading in the newspaper this morning about how the local library is under threat of being demolished. It's such a shame. It's been a key part of the community for years. You two remember when they first started that children’s reading club? Oh, yes. It was just so quaint. The library was where my kids used to spend hours after school. And now it’s all about “innovative learning spaces” and the like. I don’t get why they can’t just keep up the good work they’re doing alongside new developments. Exactly. It’s not just about the books, is it? It’s a safe place for kids, a quiet space for people to study or work. And even for those among us who just read for leisure, places like that need to exist. They even talk about building new flats where the library is. It's tragic. But speaking of creative spaces, have you got any ideas about upholstery fabrics for the new sofa in the living room? We’re between these two beautiful options at the moment, but we can’t seem to decide. Sure, I've been looking at some online reviews. There's a pretty decent website called The Modist, I think? They have a wide variety. But honestly, I was intrigued by a picture of a fabric called Suede Lux by Robert Allen. It's very similar to one of the options you were considering, but I think it has a more luxurious feel. Oh really? That does sound nice. Alright, I'll have a look. You know, I also saw online that the community is getting together to protest the library demolition. I think it’s time we joined the cause. I completely agree. I was planning to look up more information about it later. More people need to make their voices heard. But tell me, do you think it would be possible to save the library without necessarily bringing it up to date? Well, it's a bit like trying to make an old building look modern without making it lose its character, isn't it? But honestly, that’s what I like about old buildings – the integrity of the structure, the facade. Have you seen the new apartments they’ve built on King’s Road? The first floor has got all the old facade still, and it’s beautiful.

Right, let's get this weekend sorted out then. What's on the agenda for music today? I grabbed some of those old vinyls from storage the other day, maybe we can play those. Got some of the Rolling Stones and Queen, you've both liked those before. That's brilliant! I love vinyl. Can't wait to hear some Queen. I've got a bunch of new music on my phone, though. Have you heard of Billie Eilish yet? Actually, I've set up my laptop here in the car and have loads of playlists prepared for our trip. I think it's a good idea to mix it up. I have some classical too, for when the conversation dies down or we need some background noise. Nice touch, Sarah. I wasn’t expecting the classical but that’s a great idea. As we're on the way to Hampshire for your sister's birthday, maybe you guys want to discuss presents? Ron, you know how it is. Presents for the little ones are always a bit of a challenge. But Sarah, how about you? Any ideas already? Well, I'm thinking this Harry Potter Lego set might be a hit. It includes the different buildings from the series. Plus, it'll fit all ages while still being relevant. I was actually thinking we could get the girls something more creative. A sketchbook with some good quality pencils or markers might be nice. It'd encourage their creativity as well, no? Sounds good, but remember they're 10 and 7. Something they can enjoy and play with is also important. Maybe we can combine your ideas, Sarah. Exactly. The Lego set would be fun for now, and if they're interested in drawing later, we can always get the sketchbook for another occasion. That's a good compromise. I'm also thinking of another present for Renae. Do either of you have ideas for Ann's other interests? Since she's a business analyst like Ron, maybe something related to her work or her hobbies out of work. Ron, any ideas? I know Ann's always talking about her favorite show so she might appreciate something related to that. It's called The Crown, if that helps. Ah, yes. I've heard it's very good. How about something like a book or a documentary about the royal family or something similar?

Right, now I know this topic might not sound very exciting, but it's important. When we're driving, we need protection in case anything goes wrong. Do you know much about car insurance? Well, I think it's like... um, you have to pay a bit, and then if you crash or something happens to the car, they give you money or fix the car, right? That's pretty much it, actually. Now, you might wonder, why isn't everyone just buying the most expensive policy they can afford? It's because insurance affects how much we pay in premiums, and that can be quite a significant sum over the year. Yeah, I've heard that. But how do they decide how much I have to pay? Is it just random? Not random, actually. There are a few factors they take into account. One of the main ones is your claims history. If you've had accidents or claims before, your premiums are likely to be higher. Another big factor is the type of car you drive. Some cars are more expensive to insure because they're powerful, or more likely to be targeted by thieves, or are more expensive to repair. So, if I have a fast car, I'll pay more? Exactly. They also consider the area where you live. If you're in an area with high crime or a lot of accidents, your premiums will probably be higher. That makes sense. What about age? Does that matter? Yes, it does matter. Young drivers are usually seen as higher risk because they're less experienced and more likely to have accidents. That's why premiums are often higher for younger drivers. How about older drivers like you? Do your premiums stay the same? No, premiums can change over time. At my age, they often go down because I've been driving for a long time and statistics show older drivers are less likely to have accidents. That's nice to know! But I read somewhere online that insurance premiums are getting more expensive. Is that true? It is. The cost of repairing cars these days, particularly with lots of electronics, can be very high. Plus, there's an increase in insurance fraud, which drives up the cost for everyone. But it's definitely worth shopping around. Some insurers offer better deals than others, and you might be able to get a cheaper deal if you complete an online driving course or if you agree to have a black box fitted in your car to monitor your driving.

Alright lads, so first things first. Irish Pub or Takeaway for dinner? Decisions decisions. Ooo, takeaway! We can watch Suicide Squad while we're eating, right? Oh, I don’t mind. But I think we should order from this new Chinese place near my sister's that makes the best chicken curry ever. And we could use an order of extra crispy. That stuff is like... game changers! What's so special about the curry at that place? Well, the chicken is always perfectly tender, but it's the crispy coating that's the real magic. And the spice levels are just right - you can feel it, but it's not going to blow your head off. Is that good or bad? Both. So, speaking of blowin' our heads off... What do we think about this idea of including kids younger than 18 at Irish Presents? Do we think it's fair? Ah, well, as an IT manager, I'd say it's an interesting idea. But there are definitely pros and cons to consider. For instance, are these kids emotionally and mentally ready for that level of participation? I mean, doesn't come without its stresses and pressures... Stress, that's on all our minds lately. Seems to be a common thread in our conversations. What kind of tests do they do at work to measure stress levels? Well, it's usually a combination of things. You've got your self-assessments where you rank your own stress levels, and sometimes more formal physiological tests for cortisol levels in people who are really suffering. And what do they do if the levels are off the charts? Well, that usually means... ...you've got a real problem. There's support, counselors, stuff like that. So, how does that work during the company's quality review processes? I mean, can you actually speak up about those levels? Absolutely. It's all about creating a safe space where you can share if things are getting too much. But not every workplace fosters that kind of openness. Which brings me to another thought... We've finally had some time to sit back and talk about non-work stuff. Like, what about that Equality Vote in Ireland a few years ago? That was a divisive topic but what did we all think when it passed? It was a big moment. A step towards equality and fairness that had been a long time coming.

Alright mates, so who was the first person to fly? Was it the Wright brothers or was it someone else? Well, technically speaking, the Wright brothers made the first controlled powered airplane flight on December 17, 1903. That's a fact! Really? I thought it was someone else. I remember learning about someone called Louis Bleriot in our history class. Ah, Louis Bleriot, yes. He was indeed a pioneering aviator but he wasn't the first to fly. He was the first to fly across the English Channel in 1909. That's correct. And if we're talking about pioneers in aviation, we can't forget about the Montgolfier brothers from France. They made the first flight in a hot air balloon way back in 1783. That's right! So there we have it. Several individuals made major contributions to the development of flight. It's a bit like the development of modern aircraft and how different it is from the planes we have today! You know, it's amazing how quickly everything progressed. I mean, in a relatively short time we went from hot air balloons to space travel. It's crazy when you think about it! Totally! And speaking of aviation, have you seen the new Airbus factory near Bristol? They're building some of the most advanced commercial airliners in the world. Really? I didn't know that! That's the progress we're making. Just last weekend, we were driving through a bit of countryside and I saw a plane flying really low. Seems like the weather was perfect for that kind of adventure! Oh wow, low flying planes are so cool! But can they see everything that's on the ground from up there? Well, sure, especially if they're using spotters or drones to check out the landscape. But for general observation, probably not. Unless they want to run into trouble! There was this one time when a plane got too close to a nudist beach. You could imagine the uproar... Clearly planes are not immune to unexpected situations! Can you imagine? Well, I'm not sure if I would want to be the pilot in that situation... It's situations like those that remind us, the law isn't always prepared for the unexpected, isn't it? Exactly, which brings us to the topic of law conversion courses. Speaking of which, I know quite a few people who are doing that to change their careers.

I've decided I'm going to become a vegetarian. I just can't justify eating meat anymore after watching that documentary about animal cruelty. I understand where you're coming from. I've drastically reduced my meat intake, but I still indulge every now and then. I've never been a huge meat eater, but I do think that the idea of synthetic meat, right? Shmeat... I'm not sure how I feel about it. Yeah, it's a bit sci-fi for my liking. But I guess, if it reduces animal suffering, it’s worth considering. You two are just looking for excuses not to give up your Sunday roasts. No, no - I'm just genuinely curious. And to be honest, it could be a game-changer for the environment. True, the environmental impact of meat production is huge. But synthetic meat? Sounds like we're just replacing one problem with another. I think it's too early to say, honestly. I don’t know enough about it yet, but if it can reduce cruelty and is good for the environment, then maybe it's worth the effort? It’s definitely worth exploring, certainly. I also wonder, though, about the health implications. Would it actually be better for us? That’s an interesting point. There’s so much talk about deficiencies in vegetarian diets - B12, iron, the lot. We might need to supplement it anyway, synthetic meat or not. Just what the world needed, more vitamin tablets! We can just stick to things the body actually needs. I mean, look at those vitamin tablets. They’re more chemicals than nutrients, really. If only we could get all we need from our diet. But it's hard, especially when you're busy caring for others and changing the world byte by byte with our art. Care for others, sure. But for me, I have a rough day at the pharmacy, and the thought of cooking doesn't exactly thrill me. I have a bit of a hobby. I've been trying to perfect my vegetarian recipes. Want to guess the last thing I made? Sure, what is it? Vegan 'fish and chips'. Vegan 'fish'? That's a... bold move. Fire away with the details, then! Well, it was a lot of work, let me tell you. Tofu marinated in a mixture of things to make it taste like fish. Then I tried to create the fried batter without using eggs.

Yo, anyone seen that new horror film that came out last month? I was thinking of getting it for a Netflix binge. Yeah, talked about that with the mates at the pub last week. It's got quite a mixed bag of reviews but they all agree the suspense is pretty good. So you reckon it's worth watching then? Yeah, I've heard it has this one scene that's quite tense. I'd be up for giving it a go if we're gonna watch it together. Good, I was hoping we could all settle in for a film night. We can get some snacks and just chill. Sounds good. Though let me remind you, we’ve got to be quiet if we're watching in the lounge. There’s the others making Christmas plans, and they’re all pretty focused. Fair enough. We can go with headphones if we need to. And guys, did you see the deals on Amazon this black Friday? Someone should probably check that out next. I’m running low on decent games. I saw some good bargains but didn’t buy anything as busy student life doesn’t really allow for too much shopping while the uni’s open. Speaking of shopping, hasn’t the local high street seen better days? All the shops seem to keep closing down. Aye, it's a shame. It breaks the vibe of the town really. But you can't blame the shops, I mean, they're losing business to online shopping. True that. I find myself buying things more and more online. The only issue is delivery times, but I guess that’s the trade-off. Can't win, can you? More convenient, but the town loses a bit of its character. It's all about balance, innit? Definitely. Anyway, moving on to lighter topics. Any plans for Christmas? You both might be around for the big dinner. I don't know for sure yet. If I find work by then, maybe. But probably just for lunch on Christmas day if that happens. Hope you’ll still come and have lunch. We can catch up and spend some time together. Of course, I’d like that. I’ll make sure to be available. Thanks, mate. That means a lot. No worries. I know it can be tough when you’re not working. How’s the job search going?

Oh, did I ever tell you about my Dad's epic decision to surprise the family with a holiday in New Zealand last year? He's always been talked about visiting his sister there and well, he just decided to bring us all along for the ride. That sounds quite the adventure. Going from Buckinghamshire to New Zealand sounds like a pretty drastic change of pace, but I bet it was brilliant. It was amazing! The stunning landscapes, the very friendly people... And we even got to visit some of the set locations from Lord of the Rings. Oh, did your parents try out the middle earth magic with that? Well, my mum was keen on trying some of the local 'magical' honey. And my Dad, bless him, started acting out parts of the movies when he thought no one was watching. It was quite fun though. Your family must have had a good time. I've always wanted to visit New Zealand - the landscapes look breathtaking in photos. Oh it was, it really was. Although, it was funny trying to understand the local accents. You know, you get used to the 'R's in South Eastern English and then you arrive in the South Island and everyone is really rolling their 'R's. Yeah, I had that experience in Ireland, trying to understand the Dublin accent. It was a bit of an adjustment at first but then you get used to it and start picking up the rhythm and quirks of the local speech. Well, it's the same with New Zealand. The 'R's, the 'Y' sounds, everything's just a bit different. We spent ages trying to understand what was being said in some of these real, blurred out, local pubs. Oh, I can imagine. It's always great to immerse oneself in another culture's dialect, even changing the way you pronounce everyday things is an experience. Definitely. And it's funny, in these situations, you often start using local expressions. We were all saying 'bloke' and 'mate' within a few days! That's the best part about travel, isn't it? Adopting little bits of local culture into your own. I did that when I came back from the USA, started saying 'awesome' all the time. Yeah, I know the feeling. I started calling everyone 'darling' because we heard that so much in New Zealand. That sounds like you might have had too much of that 'magical honey'.

Yo, mate, did you finish reading that massages module from last week? I'm really struggling; these muscles and whatnot are all a bit confusing. Yeah, I did. To be honest, I still can't quite grasp the difference between trigger points and knotty muscles, but I suppose that's what questions are for, innit? Haha, yeah, good thing I asked then! Seriously though, I've got this essay due soon and I'm a bit worried about getting it right. Plus, my tutor always says how important it is to relate it to real-life experience. You get any good tips from your postgrad? True, your tutor's right, experience makes all the difference. For essays in your field, try to highlight case studies or real-life examples. Also, read a few journal articles from your field to get a better understanding. That sounds like a good plan, thanks mate. I'll do that. You're welcome. Also, if you're struggling, don't be afraid to ask for help. You uni has resources and tutors who are there to help you. I know, but sometimes it feels like no one else is as confused as I am. I just feel like everyone else has this under control. That's absolutely not true. We all struggle sometimes. I mean, even in my postgrad, there were times when I felt utterly lost. But the key is to not be afraid to ask for help, to read more, to talk to your tutors about it. Yeah, I know. It’s just that sometimes when I don't understand something, I feel like I’m the only one and the tutors just kind of expect you to already know. But here’s the thing, the fact that you're struggling and asking for help shows that you're actually paying attention and want to do well. That's a good sign. That's a good way of looking at it. Thanks for the advice, it's really helped. No problem, glad I can help. Speaking of help, did you go to that yoga class last week? Seemed like everyone was raving about it. Oh, yeah, I did. It was actually really nice. I was thinking about signing up for more stuff like that. Even just to take my mind off uni stuff. You fancy doing something like that together? Actually, that sounds like a fab idea.

Right, let's get this weekend sorted out then. How about we cook up a big family lunch; it's been ages since we've all sat down together to eat. That sounds lovely, I need to plan out my lessons for next week but now I think I can spare a few hours for something like that. Yeah, let's definitely do that. Cooking together can be fun. Have you thought of a menu yet, or should we each suggest something? Well, I was thinking how about we get a big roast beef in. You can't go wrong with that, plus it'll give us enough leftovers for sandwiches for the next day. I can pick one up from the butcher's near by on Saturday. A roast sounds good, but maybe we could also consider some vegetarian options? What with all this news about the climate and migrant crisis in Calais, it feels slightly indulgent to be planning a big roast feast. That's a good point. And we can always have some vegetarian sides. Pasties or maybe a few vegetable curries? Sure, that works. I can do a big vegetable curry, plenty of leftovers that way as well. And pasties are a good idea, we can bake those in the morning. Speaking of climate and the news, did anyone catch that program on Channel 4 last night about Calais? It really puts things into perspective, doesn't it? Yeah, I saw that. Can't believe they're still in such a bad situation all these years later. It really doesn't feel right that we're sitting here planning a big lunch when there are people living in such appalling conditions just across the channel. Exactly. Maybe instead of just planning this lunch, we could also see if we can make a contribution. Do any of our local charities support those affected in Calais? Good idea. I've heard some organizations are doing collection drives for supplies. We could also donate some food to the local food bank, seeing as it's a bit more immediate. And also talk to our children, make sure they understand what's happening. It's important for them to see the real world and not just what's show on TV. Agreed. Making them aware is a good start. Maybe we could even set up a small donation fund and if we all contribute a bit, it could make a difference.

Ah, good morning, Peter. How was your weekend? We've been swamped with deadlines these past few weeks. Oh, it was alright, thank you for asking. You know how it is. I spent most of my Saturday researching and Sunday baking. Ah, baking! I don’t do much of that anymore, but I do have quite a passion for home decorating. I've been thinking of updating my study with some new furniture. Really? That sounds interesting. Are you planning on doing it yourself or hiring a tradesperson? Hah! Well, I would like to think I can, but honestly I’ve been relying on the expertise of local tradespeople to do the heavy lifting. I find that if you can afford it, it’s often best to let the professionals handle the bigger jobs. Absolutely, they have the right tools and experience. But be careful, I've had friends who’ve got scammed by freelancers who turned out to be quite incompetent. Ah, yes, I’ve heard horror stories. But I suppose that’s part of it. We should connect some of our colleagues with good trade contacts. I’m sure we’re not the only ones looking for reliable sources. A good idea! Do you also happen to have a bathroom project in mind? I’ve been thinking of installing a new bathroom for some time now, especially as I seem to spend half my day in there in quarantine. Ah yes, the bathroom, a great area for improvement. I would definitely look into modernizing it doesn’t come cheap but it’s worth the redesign and the functionality that comes with it. I completely agree. I’ve seen some lovely designs online. I just hope I can find someone decent to do the work. That can be tough. I once hired a young couple who were quite competent but were so eager for the job that they underpriced themselves. We ended up having to compensate them more to ensure the job was done to a proper standard. I suppose that's another experience. I know a plumber who’s always busy because so many people run into issues with drainage or plumbing leaks. Plumbing, yes, and electrical issues. Both can turn into nightmares if not handled properly. I've had a few lessons myself over the years. Indeed. Speaking of skilled workers, did you hear about Dave? I’ve been working with him on a project and he’s been incredibly helpful.

Ah, now I'm not one for educating anyone on the finer art of drinking but today's the occasion. Decided upon a celebration and celebration calls for a good pint, wouldn't you say? Yeah! Is it like a birthday or something? Did the toddler get a new book or something? Because if it's for me, I'm expecting something extraordinary, and I mean EXTRAORDINARY! Oh dear, no, it's not for you, Thomas. It's for your dad actually. As it happens, today marks a major milestone in his... knowledge of his own limits, shall we say? A lazy Sunday, with a decent amount of Guinness and a bit of pint talk. Oh, so what happened was he read this one really good horror story in a curry cookbook! Yeah, that might be a stretch but it's partly true. He's been reading this book that talks about biology, pain and superpowers... very appropriate, right? Well, yes, it's all very sophisticated. He read about how some people have a gene that makes them feel less pain. I mean, it's not a superpower, but if you told enough people with hangovers the next day, they might believe you. So he's planning on drinking so much he can't feel the pain tomorrow? Well, technology is certainly advancing at a breakneck pace, isn't it? Ah, that's really putting it charitably, isn't it? We might achieve humanity's first "drinking-induced superpower" today doesn't sound ideal but, it's a bit of the lads catching up. Indeed! Now on to more sobering topics. Last night, I had to use one of those night deposit boxes at the bank just because, well, the idea of a bank being closed on a Sunday is almost as funny as this conversation. What's a night deposit box? It’s a big slot in a wall where you can drop off your cash after hours. Like a genie's lamp but for banknotes. It’s usually for businesses but I was depositing a cheque for a work matter. So, like sending a message to Scrooge McDuck? Exactly! Clearly, I need to work on my examples. Speaking of unusual habits, I heard something fascinating. There’s this new trend called “eating metal”. Apparently there are people who actually eat metal like it’s a snack. That’s not possible, right?

Ah, marvellous weekend we've had haven't we? Halloween was a whirlwind; these youngsters and their tricks are getting more creative by the year! Certainly is! Made me feel old though, hearing the voice of time. Still, now that the candles are blown out, let's catch up on some news. How have you been holding up, sir? Ah, spinning cotton with the spool and reel, of course. Now, don't mind me, but your granddaughter Emma is doing so well with her horse-riding, isn't she? Yes, she really is! It started last year as a bit of fun, but she's taken to it like a fish to water. Might just encourage her to compete next year. Brilliant! Competitions are a great way for kids to learn discipline and teamwork. Much better than all these gizmos and gadgets they're glued to these days, if you ask me. Hmm, spot on, mate! But these modern times... Technology can be a blessing and a curse, innit? I never even had a calculator when I was a lass. True that. Now, speaking of technology, have you heard the news about the new high school curriculum? I'm curious to see how these kids are going to manage all that coding and whatnot. Well, I teach at a local school and honestly, it's a balancing act. We need to prepare them for the future, but we also have to acknowledge the importance of traditional subjects. Communication and interpersonal skills, for instance, are just as crucial in today’s world. Yeah, and I'm really into it. Last project we did in tech class was to create a digital storybook, and I made one about Halloween myths and legends. It was really fun. That's terrific! I remember when I was at school, we used to carve pumpkins and tell spooky stories around the campfire. Simpler times, perhaps, but still cherished moments. Ah, yes! Those were the days. No one can do a proper Jack o' Lantern make these days. I'm sure your granddaughter could give them a run for their money though, isn't that right? Absolutely! And it's not just about the show, it's about strengthening the family bonds. These kinds of traditions are priceless. You put it well! And speaking of places, I've been meaning to show these photos from my trip to Cambridge last year.

Oh, did you see that?? That's the third time we've been nearly cut off by some impatient driver today. This traffic is driving me up the wall. Right! And to think, we've only just left Kent, we won't get stuck in questions again! Speaking of getting stuck, have you noticed how often we see that elderly gentlemen from our street struggling to get into those tiny council houses? Oh, poor Mr. Harris. I can't imagine how difficult it must be for him to navigate his little flat, especially with the lack of disabled parking nearby. I used to work with a similar elderly client. It just shows how poorly considered our council housing can be. No thought goes into accessibility for those who actually need it. Exactly! And what about the newer developments they're building? They're all going up looking fancy and nice, but do you ever see any disabled parking spot? No, and it's not just for the elderly. I've seen many young people using scooters or with disabilities facing this same problem. It's as if no one thought it was important enough to include in the initial design. Where did they get their planning qualifications? Stampeding over people's lives hasn't ended with age, has it? It stems from a much bigger issue - a lack of prioritization for people who need it most. Instead, we get 'luxury' apartments in city centers, really for the young professionals who can afford it, and all the while, our elderly and disabled are struggling in underserved areas. It's not just about the parking though. Have you ever seen the queue for council housing? I've heard it can take years to secure a place, and then who knows what you get? No decent toilet, won't fit a wheel chair, no consideration for its inhabitants at all. Oh absolutely. It's as if they're just handed keys and told to live in whatever they provided. It's so neglectful. We forget that these are people's homes, not just dwellings. I remember in my day, public housing was a bit more thought out, but still...blame Thatcherism, or perhaps the general apathy towards public policy? It's about money and politics more than anything else. The focus just hasn't been there. I swear, if I were in charge, I'd make sure that every new development has provisions for disabled parking.

So, I've been meaning to approach you both about possibly starting an allotment project. You know how I've always wanted to grow my own veggies and what not? That's right! You've mentioned that before. I think it's a great idea, though I'm not entirely sure where we can find one available around here. Yeah, that's the thing, isn't it? I've been searching online and there's actually quite a few options around Torquay. Our local council offers allotments and there's also a community garden a bit outside town. Oh, that's actually really convenient. I hadn't considered our local council, just the community garden I used to visit back in London. Is that a good choice? The community garden is lovely, but it can get a bit busy - which can be nice, but might not be your cup of tea. The council allotments, on the other hand, are very popular and you get a good sized spot. Size is good. I'd want room to move. Also, would there be any rules or regulations or a waiting list? Absolutely. You have to join a waiting list but it's generally not as busy as expected. There are rules on what you can grow and of course, you have to maintain your space regularly. I suppose that makes sense. It's a shared responsibility then. Exactly! A bit like shared property, but with veggies instead of walls. Haha, that’s a good way to put it. So, what’s the first step? Should we check out the council's website and see the available spots? That'd be a good start, yes. I can also give you the contact details. Sometimes it helps to get in touch with them directly to see the condition of the land and what it offers. That sounds like a solid plan. And who knows, next summer we could be harvesting our own tomatoes! Exactly! It'll be so rewarding, not to mention healthy and maybe even a bit of a cost saver if we can grow enough for ourselves and share. Absolutely. And we can learn from each other, maybe have a bit of a community aspect to it. I could even bring some of my TEFL skills into play and maybe introduce the kids to the joys of gardening. I believe it's a great way to teach them about responsibility and nature.

Yo, mate, fancy grabbing a brew at The Old Friends's place? I've got so much uni work to do and I could do with a proper chinwag to clear my head. Yeah, love! That sounds fab. I've just got through this massively long essay for English Literature and I need a tiny bit of me time before I start on my next one. Say about 7pm? 7pm, right. Might be able to squeeze in a bit of revision before then. But I'll definitely be there. Are you still with Olive and Gabby? Yeah, they're in. Ah, I hear that house prices in northern England haven't kept pace with the south. Is that still the case? Yes, it's true. It's always been the case really. But what about the quality of life? How does the north compare to the south in terms of amenities and services? Well, that's a good point. Different areas offer different advantages. Yes, people are seeking a better work-life balance, and places like Cumbria certainly offer that. However, for the prices to realign completely, significant changes in the job market and infrastructure would be needed. The north tends to lag in this sense, but there's certainly movement in the right direction with regional development plans aimed at attracting business and improving connectivity.

"I wanted to talk to you about some things today. I think it's important that we discuss and understand the hard things in life, like slavery and war." "Slavery and war? Like the war movies we watch with mum?" "What does slavery even mean? Like the story where Tom was a slave?" "Well, it's when one person keeps another as their property, like a toy. But it's not fun like a toy, it's really not. They have to work all day for little food, and live in very bad conditions. It wasn't just toys, like dolls or trucks. It was human beings, just like us but from different parts of the world. And yes, it's like the Tom you're thinking of. Tom's story is a true one, from history." "That sounds really bad. Why would people do that to others?" "It's a hard question, isn't it? Human beings can be cruel, selfish and they see others as different and sometimes less than them. But the important thing is to learn from these mistakes, to understand why it's wrong and to make sure it never happens again." "But we don't keep people as toys in Britain anymore, right?" "That's right. Slavery was stopped in the UK about 200 years ago, thanks to people like Wilberforce who fought to end it. But it still happens in other parts of the world. And that's why we learn about it, to know how to end it everywhere." "But it can't happen here, can it?" "Right now, it's illegal. Our laws protect everyone from being treated like a toy or a thing. But we must remember and educate ourselves about history to ensure no one tries it again, anywhere." "So is war also like when people fight over toys?" "Well, not exactly like fighting over toys, but it's when large groups of people, usually countries, fight each other over things like land, power, or resources. It's very dangerous and can affect many innocent lives. But again, we learn from this too, to avoid them and to recover from the harm they can cause. "That still sounds really scary." "It can be, but remember, we live in a time and place where we're lucky to have peace. And while some wars are over and slavery is banned, we need to always be mindful and respectful of each other so these things don't happen again."

Like, we keep just one, special gift each? That's a good idea. Plus, we can focus more on experiences rather than stuff. Last year's family trip to Italy was a great idea. It was. And who's up for next year? Let's say... New York City? It’s something different, isn't it? That sounds like a real adventure! Again, depends on the logistical and financial stuff... but it's definitely worth considering. I love how we're swinging towards more of a travel vs. gift conversation. It’s not always about the stuff. But it’s interesting how often we get stuck choosing between these two this time of year. Speaking of practicality, has anyone heard back about the DIY projector? No, but I'll make sure to check. Though we are talking about Christmas and travel, it's nice to also talk about our individual interests sometimes.

Alright, kids, who first can tell me about different types of metals and how they're used in Minecraft? This should be fun! I can, I can! In Minecraft there are like, 12 types of metal – gold, silver, iron, copper, lead, nickel and more! But most people use iron for tools and swords because it's sturdy and common. And we can use gold and diamond for decorating houses and making keepsakes right? But they're rare and hard to find. Yes, very good! You both have got the basic idea. Now, did you know that in real life, different metals have different properties as well? For example, copper is good for conducting electricity, iron is strong and used in construction, and gold is used in electronics and tooth fillings! Wow, gold for tooth fillings? That's interesting. Gold is also expensive for decorations and jewelry because it's rare. For sure! We use resources differently in the game than we do in real life. Okay, now while we're on the subject of resources in Minecraft, do you know what other things are valuable there, like fabrics? Oh, fabric? Like, perhaps wool? We can shear sheep to get wool for making beds in Minecraft. Yeah and leather from cows. It’s useful for making books and armors. Brilliant! So, different fabrics are useful for different reasons, just like different metals. We use wool in real life for keeping warm and textiles, just like in Minecraft! Now, let's invent our own legend! If you think about it, Minecraft is like a legend itself, full of different lands and adventures. Oh, we did one at school! Like, there was a giant that protected a treasure chest in the Nether. Or maybe there's a story about a village that uses real world objects to unlock magical powers. That's almost as mythical as the real world uses of these metals and fabrics! Speaking of the real world, have either of you thinking about taking your vitamins? It's important for growing children and for staying healthy. I don't like taking them. They taste bad. Yeah, and they're so big and hard to swallow! You know, maybe there’s a legend about how if you take vitamins, you get special Minecraft powers? That would be cool! Like, if you take vitamin C, you can sprint forever or something! Or if you take a B vitamin, you could craft things faster!

Yo, mate, did you hear about that strict new law regarding social media? I'm really worried; these politicians seem more concerned with pretending to protect us than actually doing something about paedophiles, you know? Right, really? I saw the headlines and thought the same, but honestly, I'm more questions than answers. I mean, people say it's about making "the internet a safer place," but where's the real action? They're just moving goalposts, aren't they? They're so frightened of being seen as "soft on crime" or something that they'd rather chase after internet regulations than, you know, properly deal with the issue. Definitely makes you wonder where their priorities are. Exactly! So what about you, planning anything good for the holidays? Actually, been thinking about learning guitar again. I used to play, but it's fallen by the wayside with all the studying and such. You still play, right? What are you working on at the moment? Yeah, still pick up the guitar now and then. So, I'm actually in a band! We're a cover band and we play everything from The Arctic Monkeys to Arctic Monkeys's early stuff. It's fun and keeps me sane. That sounds good! I'm thinking maybe I could learn to jam with you guys? Though I'm probably a bit rusty. Like, you'd be perfect for it, mate. It'd be a laugh and a good way for us to hangout, actually. Seriously? That'd be awesome! I was thinking I needed something else to do apart from Netflix and studying 24/7... Exactly, and if you're rusty, the more the merrier! It's not about being the best, just enjoying the process of playing and creating. If you think I'll fit in, I'm in. Plus, it's always nice to have another Yorkshireman in the band, right? Definitely, and you don't need a try-out. Just come for a session or two and see how you like it. Thanks, mate. I might take you up on that. No probs. You could even bring your own stuff if you're keen enough to pick up the basics again. Yeah, sounds like a plan. Right, so we're thinking a week from Saturday? For a session at the band practice room? Sounds good to me... Great! Just text or call me if you can't make it, but definitely bring that old guitar of yours.

Yo, lads and lasses. What d'you lot's been up to since school's been out? Any super cool plans for this break? Ah, man. Got some stuff going on but I need to work on that EPQ. It's like, the most important project I've ever had to do. It's all about extended research and making a project out of what you're passionate about. I know, right? But actually, I've been thinking of trying to get involved in some volunteer work. There's so much poverty around here and it really affects our town. You guys ever thought about doing that? Well, yeah, I have thought about it. But I've been really caught up in thinking about that Montenegro trip I want to go on next year. My mate's parents actually own a little village over there and they said we could stay with them. Montenegro? That sounds amazing, but expensive, right? Yeah, it can be. But maybe we could fundraise or something. And it's not just about the travel for me - I want to learn about the culture, try the food, and so on. Food! That brings me to something I’ve been thinking about. You know, I started looking into the 'foodie culture' of the UK. Did you know that even within England, the food we eat varies by region? Yeah, like, in the North, they eat more fish and chips, whereas here in Slough, we've got more of an Indian influence because of the population here, I guess. Exactly. I've been experimenting with cooking myself because my mum works a lot and I'm usually the one doing dinner. That’s cool! I just started experimenting with vegetarian recipes. My mum's vegetarian, and it's pushed me to try new, less popular meat-free options. She said it’s better for the environment and animals too. Yeah, I get that. But it’s really hard to get used to sometimes. You know, after all the stuff we learn in school – about sustainability, social justice, and global issues – it’s like, it just makes sense to think about our impact on the world. Exactly. But it’s one thing to think about stuff and another thing to actually do something. I mean, I’m trying to work on my EPQ, which inherently is about making a difference in your chosen field.

Oh, did I ever tell you lot about my stupid landlord? He still hasn't fixed that leaky faucet! I've been living with this for weeks now, and every time I try to wash my hands, it's like a mini shower just comes on! Oh, isn't that just typical! At least his incompetence gives us a bit of entertainment, doesn't it? Seriously though, even if it is annoying, it's nothing compared to my mum's constant calls about my future, you know? Like, I barely have time to think about passing my exams, and she's already questioning if I'm thinking about my career choices and stuff. You're telling me? My mum's the same. Just the other day she gave a lecture about how I should already be thinking about a master's degree and finding a job before uni even ends. Right? And my dad's on his "when I was young" track, blabbing about how easy it was to get a job back then and how hard it is now. Oh, I know the feeling. My mum's always on about how I should 'manage my finances better'. Like, I know I should but she's always giving me long, detailed sermons about it. Ah, the money talk. Speaking of, did you all see the canteen menu today? I mean, £6 for a sandwich? It’s a rip-off. I know, right? But it's either that or the awful "quick" meal from Sainsbury's. Guys, I hate to bring the mood down, but did you guys see this in the uni paper? Apparently, they're planning to increase the halls fees next year again. No way! How much more? It's like they're taking advantage of us, you know? We're already paying so much for these rooms. At least it's better than my sister's room at Manchester. I mean, if you're going to pay that much, at least have a decent bathroom. Yeah, and the uni job I applied for? I realised yesterday I was way underpaid compared to the industry standard. Tell me about it. But at least we're all in this together, right? It makes dealing with all this... a bit better. Definitely, if it wasn't for each other, I'm not sure how we'd keep our sanity. Exactly.

Oh, so many topics we've got to cover. Let's start with the basics. How was your weekend, and how are you managing with work? Freelance life can't be easy. It's been a nice weekend. Had a lovely walk around the Millbrook – always something about the English countryside that soothes the soul. As for work, it's going quite well, but of course, it's always a balance. I've actually got a meeting with a new client this week, very excited about it. But even with keeps changing, I still get to see different landscapes and meet new people, which I love. That's great. I can see how you'd love that aspect of your job. It must be quite different from our routine. It really is. But now that I've got a bit of time to reflect, I have to say Torquay's been quite mild this winter. Still, it's looking like a nice Christmas ahead. Yes, I've been thinking about Christmas a lot lately. We've got the big family Christmas at my mum's this year. So much planning involved! I'm hoping it all goes smoothly. Family Christmases are always a challenge. You need a map and a survival kit! Well, at least there's always good food to look forward to. Do you know what you're doing for Christmas this year? I'll likely be spending it quietly with John, my partner. We usually do a quiet evening and maybe catch some family through Zoom if we can. Well, that's the upside to technology. We're planning to do a family quiz this year, which should be fun. And let the kids run wild. Ah, the joys of family. Speaking of which, did your family say anything about Rena and Alex's engagement? It's quite exciting, really. Oh, yes! They are getting married next summer. I'm a bit of a grandmother already, I think. I'm sure we'll have our fair share of input in the planning stages, but truly, we are just happy they're happy. It'll be lovely to celebrate with them. It's lovely to see. And they're so in love, just glowing. I can tell they're going to make a wonderful couple. Yes, and who would've thought they'd find love during our family get-togethers.

Yo, Dad, it's good to finally see you! Two years is a long time. How've you been? Ah, well young one, two years may seem long, but it feels like just yesterday you rode off with your mum to university. I've been fine, just another year of tickets being sold and grumpy customers being placated. Sounds like the usual rollercoaster of customer service. Any big changes in Kent since I've been away? Actually, yes. Lots of new speed cameras keeps coming up. You wouldn’t believe how many fines have been flying out to some unsuspecting drivers. They say it’s for safety but I think it's just revenue. I've heard that before, but to be fair, I think they’re genuinely trying to reduce accidents. Still, it can be a bit annoying if you're not aware. Exactly! But it did get me thinking about our licenses. Have you made sure you’ve got both of ours sorted since the last big renewals? Can't travel on those trips to Brighton without those! Actually, Dad, I'm planning to move there soon. I've lined up a view teaching job and it's all sorted out. I’ve been diligently working on my plans and I'm pretty sure everything will fall into place in good time. Brighton, eh? That’s a big change, son. Well, at least you're not moving to Tanzania for a while, I presume? Haha, no, Tanzania remains as a plan for a future trip, not a permanent move. But speaking of future trips, maybe you could come with me next time? Or would that be a no-go due to the work? Well, that depends on my schedule, doesn’t it? But I'd definitely consider it. Seems like the world's opened up again after a few nasty years. Yeah, it feels like things are slowly getting back to normal. Speaking of which, how's your health been? Last time I saw you, you were a bit under the weather. You sure you're feeling better? Oh, a bit more grumpy some days, sure. But for the most part, I just need to keep moving, you know? And I’ve added a bit of weight over these two years, so that's been a bit of a health focus. Yeah, I noticed. No worries though, Dad. As long as we keep things in moderation and you enjoy life, that's all that matters.

Ah, I can't believe how hectic today has been. We've been running around today like headless chickens. Well, it sounds like you've had quite the experience! I've had a long day too, although perhaps not as chaotic. Really? What's been so busy for you then? I'd been brainstorming about a new lecture series on public relations. I've been trying to include some very interesting case studies. Oh wow, that sounds intriguing! You know, alongside this whole teaching gig, I'm thinking of taking up some part-time work. That's interesting. Do tell. I'm all ears. It just seems like a bit of retail therapy is exactly what we need after all this. Perhaps a little pre-Christmas shopping session? Shopping? That could be fun. Where were you thinking? Well, I thought we could maybe check out the new spot in town that opened last month. It's got this great little record store too, if that interests you at all. For me, shopping this time of year is mostly about music, to be honest. The different artists release their albums just before the holidays, and I still love the physical experience of buying and listening to new music. Oh right, the music. I hadn't even thought about that. We should definitely hit the music section then. Although, I must say, I still can't get over how in-your-face the current trends are. It seems we’re always being sold a message, no matter what we're doing. Absolutely, it's like public relations has become such a big part of everyday life. Except, we often overlook the design or the planning behind things. Exactly, and it’s so clever! The way they relate to human behaviour. I'm actually incorporating a bit of that into my lectures this term. That's brilliant and will really help your students understand the practical applications. You know, it's interesting to see how often these theories play out in our everyday lives, especially when it comes to habits or preferences. True, when you think about it, shopping is one big publicity stunt for product consumption. And it's funny how even the biggest ad campaigns can fail if they don't understand their audience. Definitely. So, are we doing this shopping trip or what? And more importantly, are we listening to new music while we do it?

I've decided I need a new project. I have enough time today to start knitting a bean bag for the living room. Thoughts? You love your knitting. Is it going to be the usual solid colors or are you branching out into stripes or something? Probably the former. It's easier and quicker. But this bean bag, I'll make it a bit bigger than usual. Perhaps it can double as a footstool too. That's a good idea. We could use something like that to put our feet up. Speaking of sitting in our living room, have you noticed how bland our bathroom looks? Yeah, it does need a bit of a facelift. Exactly! Maybe a new shower curtain and some new towels. Or even just a spot of paint. We could add a bit of color. It's not major work and can really make a difference. Now that you mention it, our kitchen could use a bit of a revamp too. I thought you hated kitchen DIY projects. I do, but I think it's also because we can't decide on what design to choose. Well, I'd take that as an opportunity to choose something together. Maybe a new theme, or just really good accessories that suit your cooking style. But it's not just about the kitchen now, is it? It's about making the whole house feel more... us. We've lived here for a while now. It's about time we left our mark on it. Yes! And next time we have guests over, you can show off your new kitchen changing the world views about British cuisine . Definitely. I've had enough of phantom coffee for breakfast. I want a proper American-style coffee maker. Right, so we're not just renovating the bathroom and the kitchen. We could even get into more drastic... changes. As drastic as we want to go, I suppose. Although, I still think we should start small. You're right. Shower curtain and towels for now. Cooking the meal seems to have given me a... decorative vision for the house. Me too, actually. Let's start with the bathroom and work our way out. Good. And as a bonus, our cooking will come out perfect tonight because we're very focused. So, bean bag, bathroom decor and possibly kitchen revamp. Sounds like a party. Precisely! Shall we discuss plans over dessert?

Right, so I was going over some of these old family photos the other day. Got me thinking; these are moments we'll never get back. You've always been a sentimental one, George. That’s one of the reasons we all love you, George. You always manage to make the most mundane things seem quite special, don’t you? Ah, I suppose I do. Growing up in Costessey, life was simple, but those moments alongside family and friends were precious. You know, it's funny, those memories are all I have left of my childhood now. I can imagine. Even though I wasn’t born in Norfolk like you, George, Harrow had its own charm. And the places from my childhood... they’re changing so quickly. It feels like the London I knew is slipping away. The city has its own rhythm, doesn’t it? I’ve seen both Harrow and Middlesex change over the years, but there’s still something timeless about growing up in England, something about the familiarity of the place, the people. Yes. And it's these little details, these small daily routines, that make a place home. I remember the way the light fell on the church in St. Peter’s, the taste of the sea air, the Inns by the riverside. I remember the Harrow pubs, the parks where the kids in my childminding group used to play cricket, the smell of the bakery on Church Lane early in the morning... But it's not just about the physical place, is it? It's the people, the stories, the experiences you share. Whether it’s the Morris dancing in Harrow or the village festivities in Costessey, these shared events make a place a community. Oh absolutely. It’s about the connections, the relationships, and the shared moments of life. We're changing, the world's changing, but that sense of community, that's something that remains. I suppose that's why revisiting these old memories feels both bittersweet and comforting. It reminds us of where we've been, who we are, and who we are becoming. And George almost makes us sound like philosophers over here! I’ll take that! Perhaps it’s the joys of retirement then; we can afford to muse and reminisce. You could say that. But I suppose it’s not just that. It’s also the appreciation of the little things that life left behind.

Right, so I've been thinking. What if we all took a break during Christmas? Maybe head to a cottage or something. It could be lovely. Thoughts? Hmm, that sounds quite nice actually. We could all spend some quality time together. Especially now, after this year. Yeah, I've had enough of London and lockdowns. Fresh air, good food, and real company would be a brilliant change of pace. I'm all for it. But we should set a budget. We don't want to break the bank with something too fancy. Absolutely, Thanksgiving. We've had our fair share of rough patches financially, so need to keep things real. Might just need to dig out those old brochures Sue brought back from her last vacation. Try to find something within our budget. And have you thought about what we want to do? We could make it more than just relaxing. Maybe some outings or games? Like, visit some of these heritage sites? I've been reading up on old estates in Sussex. They say many are open year-round. Or maybe a Christmas market trip? Interesting idea! A balance between leisure and sightseeing would be perfect. And maybe some of our own games? Cards, Scrabble? As long as the food's good. Someone's got to cook or we can keep it simple like a potluck. Anything requiring fancy equipment or ingredients, no. I can contribute as a copywriter to ensure we find the right place and all plans are well-communicated. And since I'm still studying to become a nurse practitioner, I can use my knowledge of healthcare and local resources to make sure everyone stays safe if one of us has any issues. Brilliant, team effort! Now, shall we set a rough date? Next week or couple of weeks after? Just to make sure everyone's free and healthy. Let's set something like 2nd to 4th of December. Plenty of time to make arrangements and book if necessary. Yep, that gives us over a week. And it's not too close to Christmas Eve so we can handle anything that pops up. Agreed. And we should probably book something relatively soon in case the best options get taken up. Alright then. It's a plan. Dee, can you look into our options? I've been wanting to try a cottage bookings website I found. They offer discounts if you book a bit in advance.

Ah, marvellous weekend so far, haven't we? The weather here in Northern Cyprus is just perfect for people like us who crave the warmth after the winter back in England. Indeed, I couldn't agree more. I must say, it's quite the change from the British weather – always something to grumble about back home. Very true, very true. I've been here a couple of times before, but I'd love to hear your experiences. You're a bit of a local here now, aren't you? Local might be a bit of a stretch, but I've certainly been here for some time now. I got here a few years back when things were very different, just trying to find a bit of peace and quiet. Ah, I can understand that. What's been your experience here? Anything that's taken you by surprise or particularly impressed you? Well, it's a bit of an odd place, if I'm honest. The history here is quite deep and often complicated. You see old abandoned buildings, businesses left in disrepair, it's like the whole place is this... it's hard to explain. I understand the sentiment. There's a kind of quiet poignancy about it all. I've noticed the Turkish Cypriot and Greek Cypriot communities trying to make their presence felt, like the cultural centres and language classes they run. Yes, yes, that's right. They've been doing an excellent job of trying to keep the history and culture alive, considering all the... well, all the complexities. I'd say tourism has definitely helped too, it seems like there's more happening now. More restaurants, shops, places to visit. Yes, things are really picking up. Though the economic situation hasn't changed much for people like, well, me really. I've seen a lot of expats move in, bringing money and new businesses, but the locals are still figuring out how to benefit from it all. That's a really interesting perspective. It's often the case that while new economic growth does bring opportunities, some people can end up feeling left behind or priced out. Exactly. I've talked to some of the younger people here who are trying to make a go of their own businesses, but even they struggle. Getting loans, finding customers, all of that. It's a common problem really, not just here but in many parts of the world.

I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Grace's latest article? It's been doing quite well, and I'm proud of her. Oh yeah, I did. I actually sent her a message. It's fascinating, the way she's portraying the intersection of questions in her discipline. It's quite innovative and daring for her field, don't you think? Absolutely. Her work is always of high quality, but this one pushes the boundaries even more. Considering she's doing this during her keepsake time, alongside her full-time job, it's even more impressive. Right. I've been there, juggling work and side projects. It wasn't easy, but like you said, her quality of work never drops. Speaking of, how has your day been? It's been alright, but the pollution today was quite bad again. You could literally smell the difference when you walked outside. Yeah, I noticed that too. It's a recurring theme here in China, isn't it? I mean, it's astonishing how it can vary so much between different parts of the city. Exactly. And what's even more concerning is the impact over time, not just the immediate effects we can see and smell. Absolutely. I had a course this morning, and one of the students actually presented her study regarding the long-term effects of air pollution in the city, and it was harrowing. That likely doesn't come as a surprise to you, given your line of work. As lecturers, we end up seeing and understanding these issues more closely than many might. But the fact that less is being done about it... it's frustrating. Very. I mean, we're discussing these things in class, but it feels quite disconnected from the world outside sometimes. While teaching, I've also been trying to incorporate more on making change locally. Whether it's small actions or understanding how to talk about these issues with policymakers. It’s often hard to translate academic findings into policy changes, so I try to help my students see the bigger picture. That's a great approach and something I could perhaps adopt. We could almost make this a common thread in all our classes. You know, add those discussions into our lectures, even if it’s just occasionally. Absolutely. It gives them a sense of agency and shows that their education here is not just about theory, but also about making a difference in their community and the world at large.

Oh, did I just burn the bruschetta again? Ouch, Helen. It's not that bad. Just don't be too hard on yourself. That’s kind of you, Auntie Sarah. I knew I should've taken the easy route with lasagna. Or you could of actually followed that recipe you found. As if that ever happens with me in the kitchen. You know I always like to experiment, don't you? Definitely. I used that same recipe last week. Sent your mum a photo. You even asked for tips. Was it from Instagram or Facebook? Instagram. And no tips required, it turned out fine. Well, speaking of Instagram... how’s that new project going, little one? So, so. It's taking a bit of time to get on track, to be honest. Not enough likes or just not enough fun? A bit of both, I guess. I'm trying to make it more appealing but apparently, it's not as interesting as everyone's brunch. Hmm, maybe it's not the content, but the way it's presented. Have you shown the photos to a focus group, or something like that? No, but I've read that it's good to keep the content fresh. Maybe I need to work on that. Helen, the secret is less editing and more natural vibes. People want authenticity these days, not perfect photos. Good point. I’ll remember that. Now, while we're all gathered in the kitchen, shall we decide on a dinner plan for the weekend? I was thinking maybe we could outsource it. Order some Chinese tonight. Yum, that sounds perfect. Or perhaps we could all pitch in for some of that new Italian spot downtown. Or perhaps you both could do the cooking this weekend, just for once? Auntie Helen! Well, Helen. It’s not always about the cooking. But it could be a nice change. Alright, alright. No need to gang up on the old one already. We’d love that, though. Very well. So, it’s Chinese for tonight, Italian for the weekend, and we’ll keep Helen off the stove until further notice. That sounds like a plan to me. Hey, what about Netflix? And snacks, obviously. Ah, yes. After dinner. I have some new recommendations. Oh, yes. Do share. Me too! Me too! I saw this documentary called "Our Great National Parks". I think we'd all appreciate it.

Yo, I was browsing on the bus company's website last night. Did you hear they're proposing a new bus route from Silver Street to the university? Ah, yeah. I saw that on my commute yesterday. Right past the Cambridge University Press bookshop now, isn't it? That's actually quite convenient for students. Exactly! I think it'll be a good thing, especially for the students. Though I saw on the news, there's been quite a bit of protesting going on about budget cuts for transport. Yeah, I saw that too. You'd think it's a bit counterintuitive to cut transport while offering a new route, wouldn't you? I mean, they say the government needs to save money, but it's not like students can work remotely all the time. Absolutely. They're already paying through the nose to be here and then they're hit with transport problems? It's unfair. And speaking of unfair, did you see the protester video that got shared yesterday? The girl talking about how her degree fees have doubled in three years. Yeah, I saw it. It was quite a powerful moment. It really highlights the strain students are under. Exactly. I just feel for them. I assumed university would be this glorious time of life, but if they're already overburdened with financial stress... It's concerning indeed. It's like they're being expected to shoulder all the risk themselves. Speaking of which, did you see the new study Cambridge did about student debt? It was quite enlightening, I think. No, I didn't catch it. What did it say? Well, they were kind of holding a mirror up to the university about its role in contributing to this debt crisis. The study suggested that Cambridge should be doing more to reduce the financial burden on students, not just through discounted tuition, but through job placements and ease of skills recognition in the job market. That's really interesting and it makes sense. While I agree that changing the business model of a whole university is no easy feat, steps like that could make a real difference. Right. Universities like Cambridge are in a unique position, they're so connected with industry already, couldn't they do more to help students transition to professional life after studying? Again, it's about those institutions taking more ownership and responsibility.

Ah, I can't believe we're finally getting out without the children. It feels like ages since we've done anything together. That sounds familiar. It's not often we get some quality time. Indeed. Especially now, the kids are getting a bit older and need questions answered which they'd rather prefer me or yours stays for. True, my niece is always asking about where babies come from right now. I'm always at a loss for words! Oh, that keeps changing as they grow, doesn't it? Yes, but the questions about boyfriends and relationships seem to be the latest ones. Does anyone else have any advice from similar experiences? Well, I've been through that with my own children. It can be a bit surreal - they're growing up, and suddenly they're acting like young adults. It's all about trust, isn't it? And being honest. But it's also about setting boundaries, even if it feels uncomfortable. That's right. My nephew was terrified whenever I used the word "boyfriend" years ago. Now, it's all about when he's "meeting up" or "going on dates"! Ha! Their social lives are quite a juggling act. Especially if they're into the right age for driving. Absolutely. But while they're young, we need to be mindful of our language. It sets the tone for their understanding of relationships. It’s all about empathy and openness, right? Like when I asked my mom how babies come and she made it into a fairy tale laden with storks! Yes, it can be quite a creative process. Though the storks do seem to be understaffed. Okay, enough about babies. What about another pressing concern: lunch. What's everyone in the mood for? Oh, now you’re talking my language. I'm sure I could sit here all day talking about food. Let's make sure we're not too focused on carbs today, though. A balanced meal would be appreciated. Right, so some of that local Cumbrian specialties, perhaps. Or could even try some Cheshire cheeses and perhaps some fish if the place serves seafood well? Ah, sounds perfect! I'm always curious about local cuisine when travelling. Especially something unique. And while we're at it, has anyone taken care of reservations or any particular place in mind? No, I was thinking we could just drive around until we find a nice spot that looks appealing.

Oh, look at that! Another one's sprung up since I last walked along here. Well, it's not like London's particularly worried about historical accuracy, but I suppose that's part of its charm.
