Oh, it's so lovely to be all together like this again. Coffee tin's freshly opened, and I've got a sweet treat from the bakery this morning. Thanks, mum. It smells just like home. Wow, I knew it would be good but not this good. You really know how to spoil us. Just what I like to hear. Now, how was everyone's holiday? I heard it was a jolly good time in Burton? Well, it was quite an adventure. The shop got slammed with last-minute shoppers in the week leading up to Christmas. But we managed to get everything under control. And how's that new menu at your store? I saw a post on social media about it. Yeah, it's been... interesting. Some new dishes have been well-received, but we're still working out the kinks. The old favourites still sell best, though. For me, the highlight of the holiday was the trip to the theatre in Birmingham. The performance of "A Christmas Carol" was wonderful. Really? I didn't even know there was a theatre in Birmingham. I used to think it was all about shopping and the Bull Ring. Hey, there's more to Birmingham than that, really. But I agree, we’re always so busy with work and studies that it's hard to get out and explore. But it's good to unwind sometimes. I kind of went a bit overkill with my studies over the holidays, I think. How are your exams looking? You're not overdoing it on the studies now? It’s manageable, but I really need to find some balance. While I was on my holiday, I caught up with some mates we don’t see often and we planned to do a shopping trip in Manchester for our own little "after-exams' treat". That sounds so much fun. After exams, we should have a family day out somewhere. We haven’t planned anything since the health issues last year. Yes, definitely. Maybe we could even all meet up in Manchester. I haven’t seen that part of the country in ages. That would be awesome! I’ll start looking into places to go and for hotels if that works for everyone. And I'll look into our shop's schedule for that week. It might be a bit busy but I'm confident we can arrange something.

Yo, lads! What've you got for lunch?? I'm starving. Ah, just grabbed a tuna sandwich from Sainsbury's. Had the choice between that and chicken, but tuna was the healthier option for once. That's actually quite tasty if you haven't tried it. I sometimes get it when my mom's not looking. She's all about the chicken sandwiches. Tuna's never bad, eh? Besides, it's cheaper. But even so, it's never as tasty as when my mum makes it. She's got this secret recipe with onions and mayo. Speaker_2 [laughs]: Secret recipe, hey?! You're just talking about her standard tuna sandwich. No, seriously, it's way better than the usual. And yeah, well, cheaper versions don't always taste as good. I'd say it's a fair trade sometimes. Quality over cost, right? Exactly! Off topic now, but have you guys seen the latest Spider-Man movie? I was so hyped. Oh, for sure, mate. It was sick! Especially the fight scenes. Yeah, I thought the visuals were amazing. But the story was a bit over the top, if I'm being honest. They should have left some things unexplained. True, but it was pretty entertaining. Speaking of things being over the top, in school, the new prefects have gone a bit overboard, don't you think? For real. They're getting a bit too militaristic about things. Yesterday, they were treating us like we were in boot camp. And let's not start about racism. It's astonishing how some people still say stuff like, "You're just like a certain type of person because of your skin color or where you're from." It's just so ignorant. Totally agree. I've heard some of that crap on YouTube comments too. It's like, people out there on the internet think they're anonymous enough to say whatever they like and it just baffles me. Yeah, zero-filter memes are the worst. It's good that we can talk about stuff like this amongst friends, though. Wonder what our teachers would say if they heard we were discussing this. They'd probably be like, "Don't talk about politics, race, or war while you're in school." But I think it's important to speak up when we see something wrong. That's a bit hard when there are arguments at home too, between our families.

Yo, have you seen that new film "17 Again"? We've been planning to watch it; it sounds pretty cool. It's about a guy who goes back to his teenage years, don't you think that would be just insane? Yeah, it does sound pretty interesting, but I kind of regret watching it because it kind of makes me feel like school could be easier if we had another chance. It's kind of nostalgic but also makes me feel sad right now, as I'm struggling with school. Physics especially is getting tough for me. Yeah, it is a bit tough. You know, it's funny, our form tutor was talking about how tough it gets when we transition from primary to secondary school, and he was basically saying we were all in the same boat, even if we didn't think so at the time. He was big on telling us to "brace yourself" and that it's all part of growing up. That's really true. But man, sometimes it feels like we're in a film already, like someone just turned the plot on and it's all about surviving. Sometimes I wish we could all watch "17 Again" together and then suddenly, whoops, we're all 17 again and it's all easier. [laughs] Yeah, wouldn’t that be amazing? But in all seriousness, our physics teacher is trying to make it more fun. She’s always using real-life examples and competitions for us to engage more. But I guess it's always a struggle, especially if it's not your strong suit. Yeah, we should probably focus a bit more. But you know, sometimes when I’m doing my English reading lessons, it's a hell of a lot better because we get to discuss the books and our opinions, and it feels more relaxed. That's true. Our English teacher, Mrs. Brown, is a real favorite, isn't she? She’s so supportive and makes the lessons really engaging. It's so different compared to other subjects where it's just chalk and talk and then you're expected to soak up all the information. With reading, there's more freedom to express your thoughts. Exactly! And in people at school, I really like Emily from our form, isn't she brilliant? She's always coming up with ideas for our projects and such.

Yo, mate, did you hear about James' latest trip plans? He's planning to backpack across Transylvania this summer. Transylvania?! That sounds insane. I don't know if I've got the guts to do something that risky. I mean, creepy castles, Dracula’s supposed grave, and rumors of werewolves and sharks... and that's just Dracula and the internet. Oh, I've heard about it, actually. I've always been intrigued by Transylvania and its ancient history. But even if it is a bit risky, at least it's not Australia. Hahaha, there's always a risk in Australia with the spiders and snakes, right? But seriously though, that sounds thrilling. Does he know anyone over there? Yeah, he knows a local guide. And he’s well-prepared. Hence the laser eye surgery he just got, so he’ll be good even at night with his new spectacles! Ooh, laser eye? That's cool! Did it hurt? I've been considering it, but I'm still not sure. It sounds beneficial, especially for someone who's on the move all the time. I’ve heard mixed reviews. Some people say it's like the best decision ever, while others say it’s awkward for a week or so. Yeah, apparently the recovery can be quite peculiar. Right, like my mate Joe did it, and for a few days he was in tears walking into sunlight. But now? He reckons it’s the best thing he's ever done. That’s quite a story! But it proves the potential is there for improvement. Indeed! Anyway, all this talk about travel planning has got me thinking. Have you all made any plans for the weekend? I’m thinking of heading out to Brighton for a casual day at the beach. Brighton sounds great but I’m working this Saturday. But I'm free for a bit on Sunday if anyone's interested. I can do Sunday. I've got a Sunday off for sure. I've been meaning to explore more of Brighton too so that sounds like a plan! Can we maybe meet up for a beach walk or something after brunch? Excellent. That works for me. We can all catch up and maybe recover from all the late nights we've been having. Speaking of late nights, did you hear about our friend Emily? Apparently she finally landed that management position in her bakery.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that party we had last weekend? The playlist was epic, and we all danced the night away! I talked to someone who said she really enjoyed the Alice in Wonderland theme. It really set the mood for the night, don't you think? Oh, really? A party themed like Alice in Wonderland sounds so cool! Yeah! I've never been to a party like that. Can you tell us more about it? Well, we had a projector setup in the garden, showing scenes from the film. The guests were dressed up in all kinds of Wonderland attire, and we even had a few photo booths with props. It was like stepping into the looking glass! That sounds so fun! Did you take a lot of photos? We did! In fact, we're thinking of having a photoshoot with proper family photos too. What do you guys think? And maybe even grab some images from the party. Someone should be in charge of sorting through them or even making a little album. I'd love to see those photos! And maybe even help with the album? I'm pretty good with computers and stuff like that. Yeah! And can we make it into a really nice photo album? Maybe even get some prints for the living room? That'd be lovely! We could then display it here in the kitchen where we all hang out. And speaking of hanging out, we should also discuss the plans for this weekend. I've seen a fun photoshoot theme online involving an aerial hoop and a muddy obstacle course. Wow, that sounds like so much fun! I've never seen an aerial hoop photoshoot before. Can we really do it? We could look super cool in those photos! Yes, definitely! We just need to decide on a time and make arrangements. Perhaps we'll set up in the backyard on Sunday afternoon? Sunday afternoon sounds perfect. Plus, I can help you set up the hoop if we need something extra, or check if we need any props. That would be such a big help! And for the muddy obstacle course, maybe we could construct it in the garden or just use the field nearby if the weather permits. Can we really get muddy? As in, really really muddy? Absolutely! And why not? We're a family that enjoys a good mess every now and then.

Right, now I'm going to unwind a bit, watch some Match of the Day. You know how it is, love to see my Manchester United strut their stuff on the pitch. You love your football, don't you? I almost rooted for Spurs last season, but nope, still love the reds. You'd think you were still working out at the local fields with the lads, not settled into retirement. Heh, still got spirit for it! Speaking of keepsakes, I still got my old kit in the attic somewhere. Granddad, have you heard about the new Player of the Year's stats? They say he's almost on par with Sir Alex’s teams. No kidding, but can he handle the pressure? They say the weight of that team's expectations can crush even the strongest of wills. Well, speaking of handling pressure, both of you might be surprised to know that even teaching these days deals with its fair share. Past parents' evening, for example, I never knew I could talk that fast! I'm sure it's nothing compared to being grilled by Ferguson himself. You must have been one of the good kids, never had a harsh word from Mr. Ferguson, did you? Heh, well I'd take that over some of the questions parents can throw at a childminder any time. We have those moments too, "Why can't I have ice cream for breakfast?" Or "When will I be done with the homework that I kind of know how to do." That's right. Seems like the young ones try their best to keep us on our toes. On that note, did your professors let you off easy this semester? The last report I got for my niece had questions that made me sit back and think for a bit. Not really. Mr. Jenkins is tough but fair. He says these questions are about developing critical thinking, not about giving us a hard time. Same here. Mrs. Taylor said the exams are designed to challenge us. Yeah, well, in my day... We just had to show up and hand in our homework. Not stuff about "pressure points" or "tweeting photos." You mean we went back to basics and had actual book knowledge to recall, not this... this... whatever... social media stuff. I remember when "tweeting" meant birds using the garden's bird feeder. Speaking of feeding, I saw the most delicious chocolate roulade in the store at lunchtime today.

Ah, I can't believe we're playing Chinese chess again, Dad. It's been ages. It's been years since you last played, hasn't it? Are you still as clumsy at it as you claim? Well, let's just say I've had time to forget everything I knew. I wish I could play this, it actually looks quite interesting. I've never tried it. It's not as simple as it looks, trust me. This game requires knowledge and strategy, just like any other. I can see that, despite not understanding the rules. Is it any different from Western chess? Oh, big time. The pieces are even named differently, and they move in unique ways. It's a different world. I mean, we even have different ways of describing the same movements. For instance? Well, in Western chess, a pawn can attack diagonally on the front rank. But in Chinese chess, that's not possible for pawns. Their movements are very restricted, while the 'soldiers' move in a more straightforward line. Yes, and the 'chariots' equate to the rooks, but their movements are limited to certain 'roads', isn't that correct? Exactly, and the 'cannons' are interesting because they need a 'meat shield' to jump over and capture. Meat shield? That's a new one for me. He means that the cannon can only capture pieces that are just in front of another piece, like a bridge. If you think this is complicated, just wait for the 'elephants', or what we call the 'ministers'. Their movement is limited to diagonally two spaces on the same side of the board, but only within a bounded area. Sounds like there's a real structure to follow. I might need to try this out sometime. It's definitely challenging. You could even say it's like... a different language. I love that comparison, Dad! Language or not, thinking ahead is key here. Just like when discussing complex social issues like Scottish independence. Ah, yes, I recall that conversation we had about that. Quite a few pros and cons to weigh. Indeed. Another topic that can get quite heated, just like our little board here. Playing games with you always seems to end up in deep discussions. It's better than just talking about the weather or everyone's health. Hey, what's the forecast for today, by the way? Sunny but with a breeze.

Oh, I'm so glad we decided to have a catch-up. I've been meaning to vent to someone about my students. Do you know, this year has been so unreal? Most of them are still virtually coming to class, and I can't believe how the system still isn't adapted for online teaching after two years. Yeah, I've had a similar experience. It's like they're just winging it right now, isn't it? But, to be fair, it can't be easy setting up an entire system from scratch, especially in this timeframe. Exactly. But it's frustrating when the little things, like having to have perfect internet connection in your tiny flat, just to connect to class, become huge problems. Absolutely. I've had that too. And then there's the consent issue you need when recording the classes. Oh, the consent drama. Like, you can't even show a song without clearing it from all major record labels these days. Who thought we'd be living in a world that complex? Yeah, it's nuts. I mean, I'm all for intellectual property rights, but the way it affects our teaching... it's a bit over the top. Anyhow, speaking of over the top, have you heard about the proposed student loan changes over here? No, not really. I've been a bit isolated for a bit, between being unemployed and, well, not really being employed in a traditional sense. I don't really keep up with that stuff. Well, it looks like they're planning to do away with interest rates and instead, pay the interest directly. Seems like the government's finally doing something decent. Really? That's a step in the right direction. For once, they're actually making life a bit easier for young people instead of piling on more debt. Yes, though, of course, there’s the small print. The new system also requires that you're employed when you start paying it back, but given the current job market, that's going to cause its own set of issues. True, and that's just for the students. We're all trying to navigate work and life, and then they throw a wrench in things like the pension changes. Exactly. My pension is still nothing compared to what my parents' generation had. And with Brexit, any hope of better career prospects abroad...

Yo, mate, what are you thinking of studying at Uni? We've got to make some solid plans, innit? Honestly, I've been thinking about the sciences, maybe Human Sciences but I'm not sure. What about you? I was considering Maths – always been into it. But I've also been thinking about staying in London and maybe looking into the science or tech side of things. Have you thought about King's College, or UCL? Yeah, I know people who are going there. They seem to get a lot out of it. But have you ever thought about seeing the rugby side of things at university? Like, many uni's have top-notch teams. Yeah, actually. Might have to consider Sports Science or something. You could be good at it. You've got a mean spiral pass. And being part of a uni team is a great way to balance the studying with being social. You're thinking about playing then? Maybe grab a few sessions a week. Keep it casual, but it'll keep me fit and I'll be around people who like the same stuff. Makes sense. Sports is always a great way to make friends. You know, when I was at the 'Rugby World Cup' in 2015, I saw how passionate the crowd was, and I kind of caught the bug too. Ah nice! I'd love to experience something like that. Yeah, definitely. You should apply for a try-out. It couldn't hurt, and you never know where it could lead. Alright, alright. Gonna keep the possibilities open. You should. Plus, thinking about it, uni can be the first chance for serious side of alcohol, right? No more watered-down fruit juices at family parties. Yeah, totally. Of course, we should also know our limits and all that but, it's a rite of passage. You sure you're making the right choice studying Maths? No, not for sure. But people say it’s useful everywhere, even if I don’t end up as a mathematician. It’s supposed to be good for understanding the world, or something. True. Plus, you can always do almost anything post-university if you've got the right grades and skills. Yeah, plus, I've heard good things about lecture styles and stuff at King's. The professors are supposed to be seriously top-notch. I know!

Right, now I know this topic might seem a bit dry, but it's important we talk about these things. So, how do you think the current government's policies are affecting us? Well, from a teacher's perspective, I think the education policies have been quite concerning. There's been a lot of talk about underfunding and the stress and workload for teachers has definitely increased. But of course, I'm not just a teacher - I'm also a taxpayer, as I'm sure you are, so tax policies are also important. Absolutely. That's why I'm discussing this with you, sweetheart, because as you get older, you'll need to understand these things. Now, I used to be an accountant, so I have to say, to me, tax policy is very interesting. But in simple terms, do you know what the difference is between income tax and national insurance? I think so, dad. The income tax is the tax you pay on your income, and the national insurance, as I understand it, is similar but it goes towards things like pensions, healthcare, and unemployment benefits. That's exactly right. And the more you earn, the higher percentage bracket you're in, right? So as your income increases, so does your tax rate. And while the national insurance benefits everyone, the more you earn, the more you contribute to it. And do you think the current government's approach to tax is equitable or fair? Ah, now that's the tricky question. As an accountant, I'd say sometimes it is and sometimes it isn't. For example, the "progressive" part of the system doesn't always seem that progressive to me. On paper, it says if you're earning more, you pay more tax, and that's fair. But in reality, the really high earners often find ways to avoid those higher tax brackets through things like off-shore accounts or other loopholes. Just like the recent Paradise Papers scandal? It's quite frustrating, really, and it creates inequality. While the lower and middle income earners are sure to pay their fair share, these wealthy individuals can often find a way around it. Exactly. But it's not just the rich, sweetheart. Middle earners also get hit hard if the tax policies change in such a way that the threshold for higher rates falls. Or perhaps government proposes more indirect taxes, like increasing VAT.

So, I hear that your weekend was quite eventful last Saturday. What have you been up to? Oh, it was quite a weekend! I talked to my daughter the whole Saturday. She landed a new job at a secondary school as a part-time English and drama teacher. It's a big step for her after graduating this year. That's fantastic! A job in a secondary school, that must be brilliant. I'm sure she's chuffed about it. Oh, she is! We keeps coming over to discuss it. She's still pinching herself really. She's always been passionate about drama and English, so it's a dream job for her. She's also been sharing some stories about the new school, just trying to soak up as much as she can. That sounds lovely! I'm sure the transition from student to teacher won't be easy though. It's a whole new ball game, isn't it? Indeed. But she's got the knack of it, bless her. Offers advice to her students on how to keep their nerves in check, which I think stems from her own experience with exams. We've always encouraged her and her brother to be involved in extracurricular activities as much as they can. It seems to have paid off. That's the good part of being involved with so many things - the confidence you can't buy. It can certainly help in so many areas later in life, whether it's at work or simply as a social skill. Absolutely. Speaking of social skills, did you manage to catch up with anyone from uni this weekend? No, unfortunately not. My friends weren't back from their travels until Sunday, so we only managed to chat on Sunday evening. I've been busy with work as well. More dull project coordination, I bet! Yeah, getting things organised is my forte. But it's getting busier by the day. We're planning a big event soon so I've been trying to ensure everything is under control. It's a bit stressful but I'm enjoying the challenge. That sounds like a good project. Big events usually are. I always take pride in the results of ours at school, whether it's a school play or an awards ceremony. I could use some tips from you actually. I've managed to overplan things sometimes.

Right, so I've been reading about this strict recycling routine our local council have started. Seems like they want us to sort everything into separate plastic, paper, and glass. It sounds a bit over the top to me. Hi there! Yes, I've heard about the new recycling scheme too. It might seem like a hassle at first but isn't it a good thing? Sunderland's got this beautiful coastline, and the more we recycle the less ends up in the water. Ah, absolutely. Our coastline is a treasure. But even so, it's a big change. Back when I was working in the lab, I could see firsthand the impact of plastic on marine life. You two are talking about something I've been looking into lately, actually. I read that in some places, recycling isn't just environmentally friendly but can even lower costs. Exactly! So it's not just about saving the oceans, but also our community. Let's make sure we comply with the new rules. We could even start separating things now. It'll make it easier when the new bins arrive. That sounds like a plan. I don't mind helping with that. Now, have you heard from Sarah and Emily about dinner on Friday? I hope they can make it. Speaking of friends, let's also not forget the game night at Alex's. Friday or Saturday? Should we confirm? I'm pretty sure Alex has it set for Saturday. But can we talk about something really important? John, you know we've been going through some tough times with you working and me not finding a job yet doesn't it feel unfair that it's toughest on the folks that need it the most? Yeah, it does. Seems like the jobs are always in the hands of people who, shall we say, are a little more... confident than me at the moment. It's frustrating. But I'm trying my best to apply. I agree, changing the world takes time. We could sit together and go through your resume. I studied a bit of HR when I was at university. Maybe I can offer some suggestions. I reckon we should actually get some professional help. We can show you the best way to present yourself. It's more about strategy than luck. There's this local recruitment agency that I've heard good things about.

So, I hear you've just come back from a teaching conference. How was it? Yeah, it was really enlightening. There were loads of great presentations and workshops. I attended one session on technology in the classroom that I thought was particularly useful and I'll definitely be implementing some of those ideas in my next lesson plan. Oh, that sounds fantastic! As a TEFL teacher, I often struggle to get students to engage with language learning outside the classroom, especially once they leave. Any tips on how to make lessons more interactive and keeps students involved outside class? Well, there was one presenter who recommended using educational apps and online tools – things like vocabulary building apps or platforms where students can practice language skills through games. That is actually something I've been thinking of trying. But, from what I've observed, sometimes even the best technology isn't enough if you don't have a certain level of IT literacy among your students or support from the institution. Completely agree. It's often a bit of a chicken and egg problem. You need support and resources to engage with those technologies, but you also need to demonstrate their value to get that support. Exactly! And sometimes even if you have all the support and resources, logistics can still get in the way – like ensuring all students have the right devices or that the internet connection is stable enough, right? Absolutely. And technology can sometimes feel like a barrier to students without much previous exposure to it. Speaking of which, did you see that one study they presented about how technology can sometimes widen educational gaps rather than closing them? That was quite an eye-opener. No, I didn't catch that. That's the kind of thing we need to keep in mind, though. I mean, technology can be a great tool, but it's just that – a tool, not a solution in itself. I couldn't agree more. It's all about finding the right balance. For me, the conference was also great because it provided a chance to network with other teachers dealing with similar challenges. It reminded me that we aren't alone in struggling to use technology effectively. I'm sure it must have helped to talk and share ideas with people in similar positions. As much as I love the idea of all this exciting new tech in the classroom, it's so useful to have real-world advice from someone who's already tried and tested it.

Oh, did I mention we've got almost nothing left to snack today? Our fridge is almost as bare as my bank account! Well, at least the view keeps changing. That's the beauty of it though, isn't it? We're traveling, enjoying the sights, and just being. You've given up the nine-to-five grind, haven't you? I'm more like the never-five-something-to-do-grind. But yes, it's been a strange but wonderful time in my life. I've always thought there's more to life than just working, especially if work doesn't really make you happy. Though, let me tell you, even as a teacher, the work can be stressful sometimes but it's a job I love. Definitely, teaching is a rewarding job, and it must be particularly fulfilling to see your students progress. I also thought about trying some volunteering when I was freelancing as a TEFL teacher. There are often charities or organisations that would love English language assistance. For me, teaching this side of the pond is certainly giving me plenty of exposure to students different from anything I expected. Volunteering could be a great way to build up job opportunities while giving something back. Do you also follow a fitness routine? I used to have quite a routine when I was working full-time but since I've had time to myself, I've become rather sedentary. I try to keep fit, even here in the campervan. There are always small spaces to do some yoga or a few push-ups. But it's tough when you're on the road all the time. Yes, let the body crawl under the side of the bed for those exercises, I've tried that. Well, another approach is to incorporate small walks into our trip whenever possible. We've been driving for a while now, so a brisk walk would be good for both our bodies and our minds. True. I do find some of these cities in Poland have lovely walking trails and parks just outside. We should take advantage of that. You know, while I love freedom and all, I have to admit, I still miss having some sense of routine and structure. I get that. But at the same time, I think that's often what we hear when we're used to a certain kind of life and don't take the time to explore outside our comfort zone.

Ah, sure I'm delighted to have this conversation with you, brian. I've been meaning to delve deeper into gerontology and anti-aging after seeing how much of an impact the sciences are having on our life expectancy. It's fascinating, isn't it? I've been reading up on some research they're doing on telomeres and how they relate to the aging process. It's quite a deep subject but makes sense considering our cells and DNA. Ah, absolutely. Telomeres are like the caps on the ends of our chromosomes, they deteriorate over time and it's believed this contributes to the aging process. But there's also research about certain activities or diets that can help preserve them, or even lengthen them. Really? So what kind of activities or diets? Was it exercise or specific foods? It's usually a combination of healthy living and certain foods high in antioxidants. But there's also some buzz about looking into how our energy sources and how we use them might play a part in that anti-aging puzzle. For instance, the shift towards renewable energy could help reduce pollution, which in turn affects aging negatively. Now that's a bit more of a global and macro level than telomeres, but it's all connected in some way. That makes sense. I've also heard about how pollution and climate change can reduce life expectancy, not just directly but by causing more stress to our bodies and increasing certain diseases like cancer, or making them harder to fight off as we age. Exactly, global warming really is a key factor considering we’re talking about the kind of world humanity will face in years to come. I mean, doesn’t it strike anyone else as ironic that we're the first generation to have to deal with the impacts of global warming? I don't want to just be known as the generation that ruined the planet for future generations. It’s certainly sobering, but I also find it quite galvanizing. If we think about it, we can educate our children, they can confront climate change and maybe even find solutions. But first, changing the world starts with changing ourselves on a personal level. Definitely. Speaking of which, I've also been looking into what the Vikings might have done differently, or rather, what they could have done differently if they had the knowledge we do today to potentially affect their own aging processes and health.

Oh, did I mention my first year's exam results came out today? I got an A  in every subject but Maths. Literally, talked to my tutor the whole morning. That's great! You must be very proud! But let's face questions you've asked days ago. You remember that coffee machine we'd been talking about? Yes! I've been looking at those pricey ones at Curry's. But honestly, do we really need it when we have a keepsake maker at home? I guess not. But it’s nice to have a gadget like that for special occasions. You've been thinking about that a lot, right? Yeah, actually. There’s this voucher I found online. 200 quid off ANY coffee machine at Currys. But they said the deal expires today at 6 pm. Ooh, that sounds like big money! But honestly, we're not in the market for major expenses right now. I know. But it would be wasteful to let it go, right? You’re right about that, but the bigger news here is... the new baby chair has arrived. Really? Can I take a look? Sure, go ahead, but carefully. It’s a new one and we want it for the baby, not for the dogs, remember? Of course! I would never. As much as the dogs might want to try it on, huh? Wow, it’s huge! How are we going to keep this in the living room? It’s going in next to the sofa, and honestly, it’s perfect! We can use the space where that old armchair was before. Speaking of shopping, did you pick up something else you needed? Actually, yes, but I couldn’t find it at the usual places. It’s a new pair of sunglasses. Got almost all of my glasses at Specsavers. They're usually reasonable with prices and services. Yeah, but these ones... are from a particular brand that I just love. You can often find cheaper deals online. Have you checked online stores for any sales? I was about to check, yeah. Or wait, why don’t you check next time you’re in town? They might have some in the mall, and you could try them on before buying. Good idea. Mmm, that would be better. Speaking of shopping trips, have you sorted out the referendum vote, Emily? You know, I'm still on the fence a bit.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to deal with the Christmas tree situation at work? No, you didn't mention that. Is this one of your infamous nursing stories or something now? Both. It was just one of those years where everyone was so busy and the Christmas theme at the hospital was a disaster. I ended up spending most of my evening actually decorating the tree myself. As a nurse, decorating a Christmas tree probably wasn't in your job description, was it? Definitely not, dear. I just figured, hey, it needs doing. Might as well be me. But you know, looking back, it actually brought a little bit of joy to the place even if the decorations weren't perfect. It's funny how little things like that can sometimes make such a big difference. Like, I recently had to deal with similar situation at work. We were late with our Christmas ad campaign and I had to stay late to finalize it. Sure, I've been there too. The pressure can get high with deadlines. How did it all turn out for you? It was tough, but we managed. And the campaign itself turned out better than expected, so I'm happy. But I really had to push myself. Well, I'm proud of you for handling it. It’s all part of growing up and working, isn't it? Learning to juggle things and still get it done. Yeah, you're right. Speaking of work, I had a funny incident at work. Our office just got a new person, and I made the mistake of talking to him in a casual tone because I thought we were informal. But turns out, he's actually quite senior in the company. I had to quickly adjust but he was really cool about it. Oh, bless. You'll make that mistake once but I'm sure you've learned from it now. It’s all part of learning and growing, like I said. Definitely. But have you heard from our neighbours about those kids across the street? Their dog just had puppies and the kids are having a ball with them. Actually, I saw the puppies. They are adorable. I mean, it’s a bit of a noise but it’s nice seeing the kids so excited. I know! And don’t you just love the reactions when they finally pick a name for their new pet?

Yo, mate, welcome to our new pad in Sussex! I’ve been here since yesterday. It’s a decent size and has a lovely view. It’s really cute! I love the layout. Is this where you’re going to set up the office? Yeah, I thought about putting some kind of desk over there near the window. But first, we need to get everything sorted out. Like, our internet is supposed to be set up today, right? Yeah, according to the documents. But have you called to confirm? And when is our rubbish collection? Good point! Let me check that. Ah, it’s every Wednesday in our area. And just like you said, internet setup was scheduled for today. But we can double-check with the company. Great. And what about your cooking situation? Do we need to buy a new fridge or do you plan to use the existing one? I was thinking about that. But honestly, we probably need a new fridge. The old one in here might not be as good as it used to be. Plus, it could be a good investment for us. Totally makes sense. Shall we do a quick shopping trip for kitchen stuff then? Maybe grab some supplies and the fridge. Yep, that’s a plan. Also, remember how you mentioned smoking while working or studying? We need to check if this is allowed in the building. Oh, I almost forgot. Smoking isn’t really allowed indoors in most places nowadays… Right, so we’ll have to see about finding a spot outside. Let’s discuss that when we're planning our setup. Also, there’s a nursery next door! I was thinking of asking them for a few little plants since they probably have a green thumb or something. That’s a great idea! Nurseries tend to have a collection of seasonal plants. It would be nice to add some greenery here… maybe we can even exchange a few plants for them to teach in return for ours. Genius! That could be a fun project. What about food? Any local places we should try or are there plans already for tonight’s meal? I was thinking of just ordering something for tonight. You know how it can be. But if you have suggestions, definitely. How about we try our hand at cooking something? I heard about this new local market nearby for seasonal produce.

Oh, it's been ages! I almost didn't recognize you today. How have you been since graduation? I've been alright, just trying to find my footing. It's been quite challenging to get a placement but now I have this, so I'm grateful for that. You've been working for over a year now, right? Yep, been with the same company for a year and a half now as a project co-ordinator. It's been a rollercoaster ride but I'm learning so much. I can imagine, I've been surviving on a day-to-day basis with the graduate training program. But, honestly, I’m really enjoying the field. Though, let’s talk about something more fun. Have you eaten here at Bills in Peterborough before? Yeah, a few times. I love the atmosphere here and the food's great! They have this amazing Sunday roast with all the trimmings. Let's order that, then we can catch up properly. That sounds amazing! I've heard really good things about it. What's been the highlight so far this year for you, or what’s been keeping you busy? I just got involved in this big digital project at the company and it's been so interesting learning about the tech side of things. Elsewhere, I've been training for the half marathon in November, so that's been keeping me quite busy too. Wow, that sounds like a really good challenge. I've been thinking about taking up a new hobby but haven't found the time yet. I've been wanting to learn a language, maybe Spanish or something. That sounds like a good idea, learning new languages can be really stimulating. Maybe during your placement, you can use that as a reason to do some language courses? I haven’t thought of that. Could be a great opportunity. Oh, by the way, are your parents still living in the UK? And what about you, are you planning on moving elsewhere anytime soon? Yeah, my parents are still in the UK. Although I'm sure in a few years I'll be looking at my own place, but for now, they're quite supportive! And you know how family is, right? Absolutely! My parents are always asking when I'll move back to India or settle somewhere permanently. Yeah, I know the feeling. It's all fine, but sometimes thinking about the future can be a bit daunting.

Alright, I'm so glad we've finally made it out today. The sun is shinning and we've got a sweet pub to sit in, so that's the tea for me. You look excited though, got something on your mind? You know me, always excited for days like today. We don't often make it out together, so this is special. And, yeah, I do have something I'm itching to share. Hit it. Are you still working at that research place? You know, it's fascinating, but I never really understood what you did exactly. I used to find it hard to explain too. It just sounds like a bit of research, but the work we do actually impacts a lot of areas directly—health, tech, even urban planning. As a research manager, I essentially lead a team that develops, implements, and evaluates research projects looking for better paths forward. It's both highly challenging and rewarding when we make a tangible impact. Oh, right, I remember you mentioning something like that before. Sounds like you're firmly in the higher professional occupations now, working on quite high-level stuff. Higher professional occupations, indeed. I'm very lucky where I am. But the North East’s still my roots, so let's spin this around. What about the Midland life? Birmingham, nice city, but perhaps a bit too much of a bustle for my liking sometimes. I'm more of a peace and quiet type, which is why I'm loving my postgrad and working towards my PhD. But it's good for your studies, right? University of Birmingham's got some serious research libraries and facilities, if I recall. Oh, absolutely. The facilities are top-notch, but I also love the sense of community. I've met some fantastic people. Speaking of communities, have you noticed how much the North and the Midlands differ? While I was growing up in Sunderland, we had this unique culture, really rooted in the North East's identity. Yes! The accent, the food, the sense of resilience... The North truly has its own unique vibe. When I was over last year for your cousin's wedding, it took me by surprise how distinct those North East accents are compared to the Midlands. Yeah, and I'm pretty sure everyone came up with the joikle jokes then. It's something we still tease each other about.

Yo, nan, what's with all of these politics beans running around? I don't really get it. Oh, lad! Well, it's talked about a lot at school and down the TV, right? There's quite a bit to understand. Yeah, but do you have to understand it all to agree with someone? It seems like everyone and their dog has an opinion, but no one really says why they think a certain way. I see what you mean, lad. But politics is about making rules and laws that affect our daily lives. If you don't get involved or understand what's going on, you might not see the change you'd like to happen. So you're saying it affects us, just like the Sports Day happening next week. Everyone gets to decide on the events, right? Exactly, that's a good way of looking at it. On Sports Day, you get to decide on the events, but sometimes you also get to pick the teams. Politics is a little like that. But instead of picking teams for a sports day, you're choosing the people who'll make decisions or rules for the whole country. I'm still not sure I get it fully, but that makes a bit more sense. So how do they know who we want for 'teams' in politics? Like, how do they know what people want? Well, that's where elections come in. People over a certain age, like your parents or perhaps even you when you're older, get to vote for who they want to be in charge. It's a way of making sure everyone's voice is heard. Right, like the school council elections last year. Exactly, just on a bigger scale. You also have to consider what different groups of people want. Some might want less money spent on schools, while others want more. Some might want less money spent on healthcare, while others think we should spend more. Different politicians or political parties have different ideas on how to run things, and people choose who to support based on those ideas. That's interesting. It sounds like it's a lot of debating and convincing people. It definitely is, lad. And when it comes down to it, most of the time people want the same things – to live safely, have a good job, good healthcare. But the path to get there can be very different.

Ah, so I heard you've been babysitting Grace and James again. It sounds like they're getting quite a bit of attention from granny, wouldn't you say? Yeah, she's great. She reads us stories, and tonight we saw the blood moon together! That sounds lovely. A blood moon, how interesting! And very rare, dear. I hope you observed it and discussed it with your parents too. It is indeed a special sight. Well, seeing as you've been keeping such good track of our calendars, I just had to mention tonight's family meal. I did try to stick to dinner table manners, even with children. Try is the operative word here, isn't it? They were all over the table! It's important, though. Ronan, your IT background might help you with the technology, but good manners are still vital. Absolutely. I've been trying to teach them. But maybe that's just a lost cause with children and food! No, it's never a lost cause. And while the kids might not notice it now, good manners are a foundation for so much more later on in life. They become second nature. Ah, but Granny, did you ever see me or James using a knife in the right hand? We might achieve that with you, but James... I held the knife correctly the other night, kind of! Yes, one day in a thousand. Well, progress nonetheless. As for a family meal, I always loved sitting down together as a family when I was growing up. It was so important to us. That’s right. Family meals bond people. You can catch up on everything and share laughter and food. I suppose that's why we enjoy Sunday lunches together, isn't it? Absolutely, Sunday lunches are sacred in our family. Speaking of which, would anyone like to take a walk around Fitzgeralds Park once this is over? I love Fitzgeralds Park. Do you remember when we'd take you children there for picnics? Oh yes, and there was that time we took you all to hear the birds at the park’s aviary. Yeah! The birds, the animals, the park itself is so pretty now too. Maybe next time, we could take granny with us again? Absolutely, that's a great idea. Let's plan that for next time. And perhaps some dinner leftovers for a picnic lunch as well?

Ah, George, did you hear about that Scottish referendum last year? I have to say, it nearly kept me up at night thinking about what it might mean for our country. Yes, yes. It was quite the turmoil, wasn't it? I must admit, it made me question the whole concept of nationalism. But I suppose it's always a complex issue when one group wants independence. Absolutely. I think it opened up a lot of fractious debates among politicians and the public alike. However, I believe that in the end, it's a testament to our democracy. We can have those conversations, no matter how heated they get. Indeed, democracy isn't always smooth sailing. But in our case, the result was surprisingly close. Did you know that the 'remain' campaign won by just 55%? That’s right. It made me appreciate how much division there was, even within our own family. But you know, we’re British, we’re known for our stiff upper lip, right? It didn’t take long for everyone to get back to normal afterwards, at least. For sure. We’re a resilient bunch. Now, speaking of resilience, I just got through a rather grueling job interview for a job at a new educational institution. It’s a substantial change from what I’ve been doing, but I think the time is ripe for me to keep teaching but in a new environment. I’m hoping I could bring a bit of my experience from Brighton to a new school. Ah, fantastic news! It’s great to see you looking for new challenges at your age. That’s doesn’t come easy for everyone. Well, I’m sure you’d make a great influence wherever you end up. Thank you, George. But the interview itself was quite the eye-opener. The questions were a bit more contemporary than I expected, really. They asked about our approach to digital learning, for instance. It made me realize how much has changed in just a decade or so. That changing landscape is something we both deal with in our respective industries, eh? I had to overhaul my store when they started talking about moving more towards automation and online sales. It was a real wake-up call, let me tell you. Exactly! It's all about adapting, isn't it? I could use some advice from you in that regard.

Yo, Dad, did you hear about that new world record for the most uses of 'innit' in one minute? Jeez, I mean, I don't know who set that but congrats, mate. You should be proud of yourself! Oh, yes, Aaron! That's quite something, innit? I saw that, it was this guy from London, did you know that they're considering adding this to the dictionary? Now that's impressive, innit? Yeah, keeps changing, innit? Think about when I was at school, it was all about shorthand and now it's apps and 'innit'. Technology, innit? Yeah, crazy. And just like how my job changed from what we used to read in the newspapers to digital ads now. Speaking of jobs, Aaron, how's your artworking going? Any new project ideas brewing? Ah, yeah, plenty. Working on this campaign for a new café chain in town. They want this modern, vibrant vibe, innit? Using a lot of urban, street art feel. That sounds cool. I used to love art when I was in school. But never seriously considered it as a career. Speaking of school, how’s everything with the tuition fees increase, Ann? Ah, it's a bit stressful, innit? The thought of paying off university debt for, like, years is daunting. True, it's quite the burden. We might see more gap years or people opting for online courses. Well, there is the opportunity now to do online degrees or work while studying to offset some of the costs. That's smart. Seems like the flexibility is becoming more valued, innit? For sure. I'm also getting into skills courses online, like coding and digital marketing. That's great, it's a very changing industry. Yeah, reminds me of when I first started as an activity co-ordinator. It was more about face-to-face and now we're all about planning over Zoom. And now with people shopping more online due to the pandemic, most of my work is about those customer issues, innit? Wonder what the job market will look like in 10, 20 years. Will we still be talking about office work? Probably not so much. I've already seen a shift towards independent gig work and reduced office spaces since this pandemic. So the office might just become a place to, I don't know, have lunch or a work meeting? Exactly, innit? More flexible, less bureaucracy.

Alright mates, so who was the one who hitched our mammoth road trip up to those northern farms this weekend? Ah, you mean that indispensable time machine we've now pimped, our trusty automobile? That questions honours me, my dear. I say, have you two noticed the blossoming life around us? It's like spring has painted the whole countryside green! Oh, I've got to agree with granddad on this. It's like driving through a scene straight out of an idyllic pastoral painting. I've always loved tractor trails and the like, but I never tire of this sight. Indeed. Speaking of which, did either of you catch that big herd of cows we passed by just a mile ago? Oh, yes. It reminded me of the livelihood my father made from farming back in the days after the war. He used to tell stories about working from dawn till dusk, tending to those beasts, and what a feast it was when they brought a calf into this world. Granddad, did you ever want to be involved in farming yourself? I mean, with all the technical skills you might have had as a BT engineer, perhaps it could've been a different path for you? Aye, I did, but life is full of detours and deviations, isn't it? The life of a farmhand wasn't for me. But I always had a special appreciation for the land and its creatures. The way the sun glistens on the fields, the sound of the wind through the trees, or the gentle low of cows; it's hard not to be in awe. You know, I never really took the time before to appreciate that side of you, granddad. From technical manuals to pastoral musings, you've always lived life on your own unique terms. Absolutely. And in a way, I think that's just as valid a life as mine as a consultant engineer. I mean, we see animals on the side of the road often when we're working on projects, but those moments never really stick in my mind like this drive has. Maybe there's something to the old saying about living in the moment? Perhaps. But also, perhaps it's not so much living in each moment that sticks out as much as the moments you reflect back on. And those moments often hark back to simpler times—like when you took a drive to visit a relative on a farm.

Ah, marvellous to see you all again! I've missed these family dinners so much since I retired from teaching. The company is as good as the food, wouldn't you say? You're quite right about that. It's just lovely to sit around the table together – no rush, no need to be anywhere else. By the way, did anyone catch the recipe for that delicious garlic and herb roasted chicken you made last time? I've been looking for a new way to cook chicken. Ah, that was an old family recipe passed down. It's quite simple, really. You just season the chicken with a bit of garlic, thyme, rosemary, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Then you roast it in the oven. The trick is to get the oven to the right temperature so it cooks evenly. [nodding] Right, right. I'll make a note of it. I've been finding it a bit tricky sometimes to get the timing right. But, you know, it's all about practice, I suppose. That's very true, and I must admit, it was a bit of a learning curve for me too. But it's lovely to have these moments to cook together. Makes me think back to my mum's cooking, the way she used to bring us all in the kitchen, make us help, so we'd learn not just the technique, but the joy of it too. Ah, yes. I remember that sort of thing, especially during holidays. But isn't it remarkable how those meals somehow bond us? They're more than just food—they're love, and memories, and family time. Absolutely. Speaking of bonding over things we love, I've been thinking about finding some new fitness activities to do with family and friends. Maybe something not too strenuous but enjoyable. More along the lines of walks or light swimming, perhaps. Oh, that sounds lovely! If you're in the mood for walks, Cumbria's full of beautiful spots. And you could combine it with a picnic, make a day of it. As for swimming, there's a small pool in Carlisle that's open to the public for fairly reasonable rates. Actually, I've been looking at local choir groups. Might be a fun way to spend some time together as well. That's a great idea! I used to sing in the church choir back in Dublin.

Alright, let's discuss first things first. Our parent's evening. How did it go, everyone? It was pretty good, I think. My teacher said I'm doing well in English and Geography, but Maths and Science are a bit tricky for me. Yeah, me too. I'm finding those subjects hard. But she said I'm a great reader and I love discussing books. Ah, I'm not surprised. All three of you love immersing yourselves in stories. It's a bit like when we went to that circus last year, isn't it? Even though there were lots of loud noises and confusing stuff, you were all very excited. And we like dressing up for World Book Day as characters from our favourite books. It makes reading feel even more special! And going to the circus made everything seem like a story! It was really fun. It also shows how you both respond positively to creative, interactive activities. We could look for more things like this to help with those tricky subjects. So, like, maybe instead of just doing sums in our heads, maybe we could play some games that involve Maths? Or find Science experiments to do at home? Brilliant idea. Maths in the real world often makes more sense to people than the abstract stuff on a page. And hands-on Science? That's often the best way to learn. Can we, like, go to the Science Museum in Cambridge next time we have a weekend off? I'd love to see all those experiments and stuff. Yeah! And doesn't the Natural History Museum have free entry on certain days? That's true! Let me look into it. I'm sure there are plenty of great interactive museums and workshops around. Now, speaking of interactive, shall we discuss dinner? I'm making pasta tonight. Yes! Please add lots of cheese and tomato sauce! And can we have a salad too? And perhaps some garlic bread? Consider it done. What do you want to talk about for World Book Day this year? Any characters you're particularly fond of? Can we dress up as the BFG? We read the book in class and it was so funny. Yeah! And the Queen! We could all dress up as different characters from the same book. A whole family of characters. That would be funny and a great way to get more excited about books.

Alright lads, so first things first. Our little genius Oisin; he's been talking about working in a curtain shop. Do you think he's old enough for that? Oh, Aidan just told me this, but I kind of like the idea. It could be good for his development and it's something he seems interested in. 'Curtain shop! Curtain shop!' Ah, keeps coming backwards and forwards with 'curtain shop'. You'll need to check if that's okay with you two. Yeah, definitely need to check that out. But in the meantime, let's discuss Oisin's birthday party. Right, we can do a big house party here. We did well with Ava's party last year. That was a success. We could replicate that. Ronan, how about you help me with the invitations and decorations? And Colleen, can you start thinking about food and drinks? And don't forget games. Kids need games. Games! Games! Yeah, and we can include 'Pin the Tail on the Donkey,' 'Tug of War,' things like that. Perfect. And Oisin's very keen on his rugby, right? Ronan's been teaching him all about it. Can we get him a mini rugby set for his birthday? That's a great idea. How about we check that out as well? And then, we could plan to go to one of the Munster matches the next time they're playing in Cork. Oh, that would be a treat for him. 'Rugby! Rugby!' I'm sure he'll enjoy that. Alright, moving on. You know I'm the treasurer for the local garage for car cruises and things. I've been working out our finances for next year. You're such a great volunteer and leader with that. How's it going? It's going well. I just had to figure out some tax implications on some rented houses that are used as garage storage. That can get complicated. It is. But that's the kind of thing I enjoy dealing with... Speaking of tax implications, I just got a charity call today asking for a donation. I really want to give, but these days it's tough to make ends meet. Don't worry about that, love. We can discuss it later. It's important to give when we can. Absolutely. Charities do great work. Now, on another note, what do you both think about the step-relatives visiting for the party?

Yo, lads and lasses. What d'ye think about's this week's Word Games? I grabbed an old crossword from The Times. Fancy a go? Certainly, sounds good to me. Is this one quite challenging? I'll give it a shot. Let's see questions. Alright then. First clue: A river of Western England . Irwell? Doesn't quite sound right, but it's very similar. No, not quite. It's shorter. You'll need to think of another one. Ah, I've got it. Avon! Spot on! Well done, mate. Thanks. It was actually the first word that popped into my head. Hence your stellar performance as a research assistant, I see. Ha, nice one. Let's press on. Next clue: A big cat similar to a tiger but smaller . Well, that's quite simple. It has to be leopard. We've played it on the game show before. That's correct, but just a heads up, you assumed we only knew 'tiger'. True point, wasn't thinking about other big cats. Apologies for that. Well, then how about 'lion'? A bit too big, no? 'Tiger' was in there for size reference. True again. Then it's definitely 'leopard'. Yep, that it is. Good one, lads. You're warming up now, Speakers 2 and 3. Onwards then. The next one: A metal alloy that tends to corrode faster . That's a tough one. Is it... bronze? Not really, and it's only 5 letters. Think of something else. Well, I'm not sure. Perhaps iron? No, that's also not in line for corrosion. It's actually 'zinc'. And it's corrosive if you remember our chemistry lecturer's lecture on galvanization. Ah, you're right! Zinc. There you go again, brainy. Now, let's have one that might give us a bit more of a challenge. How about this one: An emperor of Rome during the 4th century ? Hmm... That's a hark back to any of my history lessons. Initially, the thought of Constantine comes to mind, but I'm not certain. Is it Theodosius? Nope, not Theodosius, although close, it's a bit later. Try thinking of someone who managed to solidify the empire, successful in his conquests. Ah, yes! That brings me to Valentinian! Spot on, but he's usually Valentinian I or II. Which one is it? It's Valentinian I. Good knowledge there, consulting's been good to you, hasn’t it?

Yo, mate, did you seen any of the latest Glasto's lineup? I'm seriously disappointed; they ditched some of my favorite acts. Yeah, I noticed that. They pulled a right surprise this year! But hey, at least it's still the best festival atmosphere in the UK, ain't it? Definitely! Glastonbury, Warrington, what can I say, our hometown's got a big spot right at the heart of British music. Speaker_1's Mum enters the pub, keeps coming backwards and forwards, putting a smile on both friends' faces before continuing her errands. Remember when we used to sneak into the kids' section at the museum in London? We pretended like we were proper nappers. LOL, oh god, oh god! [laughs] You still got that photo? It's on one of the old iPads at home, man. [chuckles] Yeah, I do! [laughs] Let me dig it out for you next time you're at mine or whenever. That would be hilarious, mate. Now come on, remind me why we ended up with silly names for our stereo system? [laughs] Alright, alright, so it was the summer we first got our own place. We named the speakers after our families, like, to make them less 'boring'. [laughs] Oh yeah! So John is your granddad, because he's always on about his 'fine musical tastes' even when he doesn't know who the singer is! Exactly! And 'Auntie Sue' because she keeps asking if it’s 'that new band from TV or something' whenever she's over. And the smallest one’s 'Little Lucy' because it's the bass one and it's small and low but packs a punch! Both friends burst into laughter as they recall their creative labeling. It was one of those immature things we thought was so genius at the time but now we can barely say it out loud without cracking up. And let's not forget the times we jammed to The Beatles or Oasis songs, imagining we were part of the Merseybeat scene all over again. Five minutes later, Speaker_1's mum walks in with a tray, swinging towards the bar. Speaker_1's Mum: [grinning] So, chatting about the music industry again? More like finding new ways to make fun of ourselves... Oh, always a pleasure to share our DIY troubles with Mum, isn’t it? They both chuckle, while Speaker_1's mum raises an eyebrow but shakes her head fondly, knowing that's just how cheeky and close these two are.

So, I've been going over the application for the council planning committee meeting. I'm really hoping we get a spot to discuss the upcoming community development project we've been working on. That's right. You've put in a lot of work researching and drafting the proposal, and I think it's fantastic. I've been looking over it myself and I'm confident. I'm a bit nervous though. I've never done anything of this scale before, and I know there'll be a lot of competition for spots. True. But let's not underestimate the value we could bring, okay? Your research has been thorough and engaging. Your point about the socio-economic impact of this project is really strong. Thanks, sweetie. You always make me feel more confident when I need it. Also, we need to discuss how we're going to structure the forum. It's not just about the project itself, but also how we present it. Absolutely. Knowing the audience and the environment is crucial. We'll need to highlight the potential benefits, sure, but also address or even preempt any concerns that might arise. I've been thinking of structuring it as an "Introduction, Relevance, Modality, Conclusion" approach. We can briefly introduce the project; explain why this matters and to whom; the specifics of the project and how it can be implemented or scaled; and then conclude with the impact and call to action. That sounds like a solid structure. We really need to keep it concise, though. It’s a community forum and we’ll only have a short time slot. Breaking it down in that manner should work well. Just to make sure we cover all our bases, what if one of the committee members brings up environmental concerns or side-effects? Those are valid questions. We've already addressed some of that research. If they do bring it up, we can reiterate that while we appreciate the concern, our project is designed to meet or exceed all current environmental standards. Also, we could prepare some examples of similar successful projects in other areas that meet those concerns. Right. I've been thinking of preparing some visual aids too. A chart or diagram showing the project phases or timelines might help clarify things for the audience. That's a great idea. Visual aids can be quite effective in communicating complex ideas.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that film we went to today? It was quite possibly the most boring film I've seen in ages! I talked so much through the whole thing, practically narrating every plot twist. That’s kind of you, questions are always encouraged! As if. It was so bad, I even considered leaving but we’d just got there, right? And how was work keeps coming backwards and forwards with how slow it is. You'll tell me to relax, but it's really stressing me out. I hear you. I've got a million and one things to coordinate for my upcoming project. It's like the less time I feel I have, the more time each task seems to take. Perhaps you need a break? We could order out, order a nice film, something relaxing. Yeah, that sounds nice. But what film? We recently rewatched For a Few Dollars More, that was quite good. Or maybe something funnier? How about the new 'Rae and Jasmine'? It’s gotten a lot of buzz lately. Oh, I’d love that! They’re always hilarious. A good laugh right now sounds amazing. Alright then. I’ll order some delivery and we’ll make a night of it. Perfect plan! Speaking of laughter... did you hear about the Johnson’s party last weekend? More was probably talked about it than actually happened, if you know what I mean. No, but I can imagine! Always something wrong with their parties, isn’t there? Like, who needs drama, though, right? No, what I meant was the food. Apparently, Mrs. Johnson’s new recipe for beef Wellington was so salty it could've startled a fish! Again? I swear, those kids can turn anything into a story. Always. Do you remember that time at school when... No, no more about old schoolmates for the night! I’m off to catch up on the news anyways. News? You really want to dive into that right now? Yo, mate, did you seen any of that program last night? "Quit your day job; sell your car and start a mobile phone business!" Thought it was mad, innit? Yeah, I saw it. I thought it was quite fascinating, the way they made a compelling argument for entrepreneurship. It kind of got me thinking about possible new opportunities. You're absolutely right. I have to say though, marketing is a crucial part of running any business. And in this digital age, selling online is a bit easier. But as you said, there’s still a lot of competition. Yeah, that's what I mean. One of my mates tried to sell phone accessories online and it wasn’t easy, man. He didn’t know how to market it properly. That’s a great example. Marketing is so important and often underestimated. I’ve been meaning to take some online courses in that area. Sure, I've taken a few NLP courses as well. They're pretty useful for personal development and communication skills. Really? That’s interesting. I didn’t know you were into NLP. It can be used in a lot of areas, right? Yeah, it’s pretty versatile. I learned it for developing my teaching skills in class, but I've also used it to help me quit smoking and all that. And you know, maybe I should consider using some of those techniques for marketing stuff. That makes perfect sense. The influence and persuasion aspect of NLP could be super useful for selling stuff online. More than useful, mate. I just wish more people knew about it. I've seen it make a huge difference for students with dyslexia or even for people trying to start new diets or careers. True, and changing habits generally. Speaking of dieting, we really need to sort out our dieting plans soon, don’t we? Yeah, I know. It’s something we always say we’ll do but never quite get around to. It’s like the ads for diets are designed to make you want it even more. Yeah, marketing genius at work there. Whether it’s dieting or new phones, if you know your stuff about marketing, you can sell anything.

Oh, mates, I haven't seen any of you since our mammoth road trip across Italy last year! How have you all been? You know us, always busy with one thing or another. Speaking of, how's your language class going? Still enjoying teaching students English? It's been a mixed bag lately. Some of the idioms and colloquialisms they're so used to can be quite tricky for them to grasp. But, it's very rewarding. Are you still using apps to support your classes? Though, sometimes I feel like we're all oversaturated with apps. There's an app for everything these days, right? It's a golden age and a nightmare, isn't it? I just got a freelance writing gig recently and I spend a lot of time on my phone for research and writing. Sometimes I feel like I'm losing my grip on reality! We really don't need that many distractions, do we? Indeed. I found myself while editing 'Ringing the Changes' in the peak of a commotion, several things buzzing on my wrist at once. It can be quite overwhelming at times! I know right, especially during peak management periods. I sometimes wish we could really disconnect more often, you know? Agreed. Like when I saw that ad for a new phone that's 20% faster than its predecessor. Who really needs 20% faster? I mean, what if one day it's just the speed we have and we just learn to use it better? Speaking of stress, have you checked out this meditation app that's doing the rounds? Apparently, it really helps with focus and stress management... You mean like Headspace? You'd think after all the coverage it's had over the years that I'd be more eager to try it. But I've never mustered the will, I guess. The irony's not lost on me: journalists and editors writing about digital wellness while struggling to turn it off ourselves. I complete agree with you, Libby. I just got a new freelance piece about sustainable tech practices. We're all talking the talk, but walking the walk... I suppose it's a matter of discipline... or perhaps better planning our digital hours.

Ah, marvellous to see all of you here tonight. We have so many shared experiences; it's been ages since we've sat down together like this. I talked to Speaker_4 recently and he reminded me of that time we all moved into this area. It was the 1960s, wasn't it? A real kind of crossroads for all of us. Indeed, indeed. It feels like only yesterday I was driving up from Ramsgate for my interview to be a dentist here. I remember it was a bit of a struggle finding accommodation at first, didn't it? Then my wife, bless her, she was so certain I should consider buying instead. It was a risk at the time, but turned out to be one of the best decisions we made. Ah, good old Birmingham couldn't compete with the housing prices of the time. I remember my first place was a bit... well, let's say it needed a bit of renovation. But it was a start. I think most of us had similar experiences, while the '60s were so formative. For me, coming up to England to teach EFL was a bit daunting. But it was an adventure, wasn't it? Absolutely, it was. And then there was the time we all really hit our stride, when we met our spouses. I must say, it's surprising how many of us met at community events or through colleagues.
