Listen, maybe he was on to something though. Our house is getting a bit full for us and the kids. A new floor would solve a lot of space issues. Well, I'm all for it if it means we can all sleep comfortably. But ANON, let’s start our planning from a real, waking standpoint, okay? Absolutely. But first, let's make sure he's fully awake and not still dreaming about building extensions from his... personal workshop. Oh, we'll definitely make sure he's not wearing pants to work on the plans then. I just hope our budget won't be as limited as his imagination right now. True, but don't underestimate the power of imagination, even if it happens in one's pants. Anyway, have any of you thought about what we want from this extension? For me, I'd like a proper dedicated office space. Right now I'm using the dining room which isn't functional at all.

Ah, good morning, Peter. How was your weekend? Did you manage to get your spare bedroom re-decorated? Morning, John! Actually, yes. Had the whole family down on Saturday, helping out. It was a bit chaotic, but it now looks lovely. You know, I've always been fascinated by this kind of home improvement. I know the feeling. I'm thinking of doing a bit of re-arranging myself, actually. Now that the kids are older, we could use the space for a home office or keepsakes storage. You'll need to think about storage, especially if you're lazy like me about throwing things away. But, it's been a very relaxing weekend. Indeed. Speaking of relaxation, did you hear about the new study project we discussed the other day? What's the latest news on the funding? Yes, the project's being looked at by the university. Ron, our department head, promised a discussion at the next meeting. We're still waiting for a reply from the possible sponsors, though. I hope it works out. The Forthcoming Research Grants Schemes are quite promising. We're planning to submit our proposal as soon as they announce the funds available. Absolutely. Good luck with the proposal; it's quite a challenging process. I also heard we can expect a few more students to join our department next year? Indeed, Ron mentioned that as well, especially after the feedback from the latest conference. Seems like our department is quite popular among students. That's great news. Now, how about a cup of coffee? I'm still brewing the new beans I got from that Italian market. You always have the best coffee beans here. Italian or otherwise, I'm sure it's always good. I just tried this new brand recently; it’s really strong and quite flavorful. Oh, by any chance, are they from the same producer as the one you found in Florence a few years ago? No, actually, but I found this out of curiosity after reading some reviews. It's quite popular. Funny how a country like Italy can produce such a variety of delicious coffee. You know, Italy does have a good reputation for coffee. And they almost invented modern coffee culture. Clearly. I love how they make it an art form. Even the water companies here don't make coffee as good as our Italian brews.

Oh, look at this! Another piece's ended up in the wrong box. It's like they've got legs and a mind of their own, jumping out at every opportunity. Yes, isn't it, Mum? It's like they have secret plans and are always trying to escape. But why do they do that? Do they feel lonely? You know, maybe they do a bit. But it's just fun to find them, isn't it? It's kind of like a treasure hunt every time we need to clean up. Oh, is that like what Harry Potter did in the Chamber of Secrets when he found the magic diary? Exactly like that! Except, I hope we don't find anything as scary as a Basilisk in our Lego boxes. No, we hope not, or we’d need Professor McGonagall to sort it out! Indeed, or Dumbledore. Now, where's the rest of the Hogwarts Express set while we're on the subject? It was over here, but now, now it's in the "Simpsons: Springfield" set, or so I think. Oh, good job, Bart Simpson! But you're right, we should probably get all the Lego sorted and organized over Easter. It's like a tradition now. True, and we can use the big storage box Uncle Fred bought us. He said, "This one’s big enough for the entire Lego collection!" Yes! And we can use little tray dividers. I saw them at the toy store. They have different colors, so we can sort by color or by set. That's a great idea. Like organizing a small Legoland. We can make it fun for you both. Let's say, whoever finds the most pieces from each set, gets to choose the next movie we watch over Easter break. Okay! But if Bart Simpson keeps hiding pieces, he's not allowed to choose! Deal! But remember, everyone works together. It's a team effort. I'll be the one who checks if everything has the right number of pieces from each set. And I'll build little prototypes of each set so we know what they are before we put them away! That's a brilliant plan! And when we've finished, we can make a little movie about our grand Lego sorting adventure, like what we might see in The Simpsons or Harry Potter. You mean, a Harry Potter Lego sorting adventure?

Oh, did I ever tell you about my Dad during the holidays? He nearly set off the fire alarm trying to roast the turkey again! No, that sounds hilarious! Was it the usual "just a bit too done"? Oh, absolutely. But don’t worry, it was safe and everyone was just having a laugh at the end. I can imagine. Speaking of holidays, did you try that new Italian place downtown during your break? Yeah, actually! The pasta was really good but I wasn't impressed with the service. Oh, dear. I’ve been wanting to check it out too. Might have to give it another try then. You might want to though. It’s the only place in the area that does this really good seafood pasta. That does sound worth a second chance. Did anything else happen while you were away? Well, we couldn’t go to Brighton like planned because the weather was so bad. But we still managed to have a nice quiet time at home. That's good at least. The rain can be quite...restless. How did you keep occupied while indoors? Stuck with Netflix and books mostly. I also finished a couple of projects at work. Ah, working from home can be both a blessing and a curse, right? Did you find it productive? Yeah, it was actually quite good. We have a good system going now and I get most of my work done efficiently. That’s great to hear! I kind of struggle with work-life balance, especially because my job means I'm always 'on'. More power to you, really. It’s so admirable that you keep going. Do you need anything to take your mind off things? Like a chilled night in or something? Actually, that sounds perfect! We could cook something together. You sure know how to cook. Thanks! I do love trying out new recipes. Maybe we could try that recipe for homemade pizza dough? I’d love that! It’s been a while since we’ve cooked together. Alright, agreed! When would you be free to do that? How about Saturday? I’ll make sure I’m done with all my shifts by then. Saturday works for me. I’ll start looking up that dough recipe and we can prep whatever else you like to go with it. Brilliant! And maybe you can also tell me about your DIY project?

Ah, marvellous to see you both again! You've had a safe journey today? The traffic sounds like it's been a bit of a nightmare from what I've been told. Yes, quite a squeeze on the A1 now and then! But we made it – no major questions on the exam just now. Aye, well, that's grand to hear. I've been wondering, how's the new job going? The maths exams, innit? Oh, it's still a bit of a task. You'll always find one or two surprises. But the students seemed quite keen today. Reminds me of the time I was taken to task for not knowing the correct side of the slide rule when I was at school. They even had an invitation to see the headmaster about it! Oh, Mr... was it Ron? Yes, we both remember that! Quite so. Now, how about you both help with the tea while I set this place up a bit? We need a nice quiet spot for our visitors. Sure thing, Grandma! The kettle, the biscuits, the tea pot... I think I'm all over it. Ah, careful now, lad! You wouldn't want to spill any tea on Aunty's favourite tea set. Remember, Yorkshire tea in the mug, English breakfast on the side. Oh, hush, now. We don't want him thinking that's a maths problem too complicated for him. Everyone laughs. Alright, if you're all set then, let's get this side of the room tidied up and a few treats on the table. The afternoon’s looking grand – warm sunlight and all. What do you think we should do later today? Well, I was hoping we could watch a film or something. Maybe something from the '60s? I heard you both have a lot of stories from that time. Ooh, yes, let’s so! And later, perhaps a game of cards or Scrabble? Aye, cards are almost as much fun as the time we spent playing dominoes in the back yard. I’ll fetch some if you like. Well, I think we can manage that. Films, cards, and maybe some cake later if there's still room for it. Brilliant! And maybe you can tell us some stories from when you were younger? I really enjoy hearing about olden times. Stories, you say? Well, I suppose I can tell you how life was when we were young.

Oh, did I ever tell you about when I was teaching my Grade 1 students about Peter Pan? It was such a sweet experience. Are you still here Alison? Did you tell them the whole story? Yeah, which one? The book, Peter and Wendy, or one of the films? Both! I showed them excerpts from the Disney film "Peter Pan" and we also read parts of the original book. But even better, we compared it with the 2003 live-action film "Peter Pan". Did you know it was made in the same studio where they made Harry Potter? Really? I didn't know that. Which film was your favorite? Ah, that's a hard choice. I think each version has its own charm. The Disney version is so classic, but the 2003 one is so visually creative and very close to the book in terms of storyline. I wonder, between the film versions, which one has the best Tinkerbell. Oh, Tinkerbell! I think both have her distinct character. In the Disney version, Tinkerbell is very sassy while the 2003 film makes her more emotional and substantial. Each has her own charm really. Have you seen the older 1953 film or the musical renditions? I love how they all recreate Neverland differently. I have seen some of them, actually. The 1953 film and "Hook" are quite different from the modern films but equally captivating. The musical "Peter and the Starcatcher" is also quite a unique take on the story. Can we watch one of those next? Perhaps "Hook"? Sure thing. We can spend a family movie night with either "Hook" or the 2003 live-action "Peter Pan". Both are great choices. Yay! I'm in for either one. I especially love how Hook is not just a villain. He has such a deep backstory. And Wendy's story! It's not just about the boys and Neverland. It's about her journey into womanhood, you know? Yes, absolutely. The real depth of the story lies in those themes. Wendy's character evolving from a child to a young woman who understands responsibility. And Peter's eternal childhood – it's a wonderfully complex theme that even children can grasp on some level. We could even maybe write a story or draw a picture about Wendy if we have time? That's a lovely idea. We could create a little project where we each imagine Wendy at different points in the story and draw her perspective.

"I never thought today would come, did you? Saying goodbye at the airport isn't exactly how I envisioned our last few days together. "I know, it feels surreal. Especially because this kind of life-event isn't something we've experienced before, right? "Absolutely. I mean, the last time we were all split up like this was probably for my work when I was managing in London. But this is different. This is...permanent, isn’t it? "Hey, we're just flying down to Bristol, then onto Florida. It's just a little vacation, right? We'll be back in time for Christmas and...the house-warming party! "Of course, that’s right. Just...temporarily. But the thought of being that far away from the rest of the family fills me with a sense of loss. "We'll make it work. We're a modern family, after all. Technology will keep us connected. The kids will still FaceTime with grandma. "I suppose you're right. I used to lecture on the technology revolution when I was in university. Never thought I'd be depending on it, though. "Well, it’s not all about you and your 'technology revolution'! I mean, doesn’t anyone think about the actual journey? How long the commute is?! The kids have been asking nonstop! "Ugh, the kids! Always worrying about the little things. But seriously, the commute. Do we know how long it's going to take to get to the airport? "We've got a bit of a journey ahead. With traffic, especially at this time of day, maybe two hours? But we should be fine. I’ve done this drive enough times before. "That's right! And we'll be back before you know it. Speaking of which, have we agreed on the plans for Christmas? "Not really. We've been so focused on getting everyone settled and prepared. We've rented a place in Taunton, remember? So, maybe we do it there? "That sounds perfect! And we can invite any extended family or friends that are left in Devon. "And we definitely need to guest list for the house-warming party. What about the date, though? Should we do it right after we get back, or wait till everyone’s settled? "I think we should wait until everyone’s had some time to settle in. I’d say, let’s plan it for mid-January?

On a day like today, what's more needed than a good Swedish massage, don't you think? Quite, quite! You know, I've always heard questions about Swedish massages and hospice care. It's something my wife used to say about making sure patients weren't just healthy but comfortable too. That's a wonderful point! There's an art to it, a touch that not only soothes but truly cares. Idle conversation is quite the luxury on a workday like this. So, what was your experience with art and dealing with such themes? Well, my background is in the arts, so the human aspect of all things - looking after, caring - these are very close to my heart. Nursery education, similar concept, I suppose. Giving the little ones a foundation isn't just about teaching them what or how, it's about how we make them feel. Invaluable, really. I'm sure. Where did you train, while on this track? Was it local colleges or St. Martin’s? A bit of both, but mostly self-taught over the years. The most important 'school,' as I call it, has always been the lives and stories people share with me. One never stops learning, especially when dealing with art and humanity. Life is like a painting sometimes, isn't it? Layer upon layer until you get the complete picture. Exactly! The brushes may change, but the hand that guides them always remains human. I've seen it in my dealings with customers over the years. There's a deep respect for the creation, the creator and the one who appreciates it. Respect, especially towards women. I've often thought about it. Equality – it's not just about roles or rights, but about respect. You see, my wife... Do go on. She was a strong woman in all the right ways. She always felt that we didn't formally use words like 'female equality' enough; we just lived it. But she'd say, use them, talk about them. Make it a subject of everyday conversation so that it doesn't become this... any more than a buzzword. Absolutely. I think using the right terminology, the language itself, can shape how we think and feel about certain issues. And when it comes to equality – absolutely, we should talk about it all day every day until it's what we consider successful. Precisely! We were quite involved in the local community, supported women's groups, helped organize events for equality and awareness.

Mum, I've been going over the plans for our holiday and I've hit a bit of a roadblock. Oh dear, what's the problem? You seem worried. It's about the resorts we're considering. We want the best, but also kind of budget-friendly, if that makes sense? And isn't too far for you to travel. Ah, that sounds like a challenge indeed. I'm right behind you in wanting a nice trip, but budget is key. Where were you thinking of going? Right now, we're torn between Devon and Cornwall, but possibly going to a beachside town – somewhere like Newquay or St Ives. Both are lovely. Might just depend on what you both prefer. Exactly! But I need to consider the travel time for you as well. Don't worry about that, I'd do anything for a family holiday. It's just... how far is it? Both are about a 3-4 hour journey for you, depending on traffic and what mode of transport we decide. Oh, that is quite a bit, but if it includes the train journey across the English countryside, I might even find that relaxing. Exactly! I think the train ride itself could be a great part of the holiday. And the sea views from both places are stunning. Cornwall is less touristy I think right, especially if we go further west? True, it is more off the beaten path. That said, it's still got a lot to offer: the scenery, the coastline, it's just incredible. The only issue could be that it might be a bit more secluded. Some people might appreciate that, less crowds, but for accessibility... Accessibility is a good point. On that note, maybe ease of access is key for this holiday. Rightly said. From your end, you need to think about the resorts' accessibility for my needs. True. I know there are some lovely resorts that cater to older couples and couples with family. Exactly, that's the kind we want. Can you look into inclusive ones, perhaps? Absolutely, mum. I'll make a list of them and maybe even get some recommendations from colleagues and friends who have stayed there. That would be very helpful. And also, are thinking of particular activities? Hmm, I know that you often like to go on walks and enjoy hikes and outdoor activities generally. Very much so.

Yo, mate, did you hear about Leicester City? Yeah, I did. What about them? They just got promoted to the Premier League! I mean, we've had a pretty shaky season, but this isn't the first time Leicester have surprised everyone. Remember when they won the league back in 2016? Yeah, that was quite a shock. And to think they were near relegation just a few years before that! Exactly! It just goes to show how unpredictable football is. And it's not just Leicester - look at Burnley and Bournemouth, they've been doing great despite being smaller clubs. And what's with this new manager at Manchester City? Sounds like they're planning to make some big changes. Oh, sure. Pep Guardiola. Yeah, Manchester City's hiring him. He's got a reputation for being one of the best managers in the world. I heard he's got a knack for big names and fancy tactics. But it'll be interesting to see how he manages the roster at City. I hope he doesn't start buying the whole team. True, but it's a whole different pressure when you've got the financial backing of City. Still, I'm curious to see how he'll deal with the more English style of football versus the more continental style he's used to. And then there's the squad he inherits. The likes of Aguero, Silva, Navas... it's one of the most talented teams in the league. He'll have to be clever to get the most out of them and deal with the egos. Absolutely, it's a big challenge for him. I kind of wish my university could hire a coach like that, lol. Lol, true enough! But in your case, just try to get through the semester without failing it. Ah, my grades will be fine, don't worry. I've just been dealing with a bit of stress lately. That's understandable. It's a challenging degree you're doing. Don't let the pressure get to you. Cheers, mate. Anyway, did you manage to make those transactions for your company this week? Yeah, we closed a good one. A pretty significant deal with a new client. It's all going well job-wise. As for your side, I heard you made a decent profit with that recent cryptocurrency investment. Yeah, that was a pretty good run.

Ah, lovely cup of tea, innit? Took me ages to figure out how to set up this skyping thing. Had to get help from our grandson. Got all confused with the cameras and whatnot. Just like when I tried to do face swap on my smartphone. I had no idea what I was doing and ended up making this hilarious "Pippi Longstocking ghost face" and posted it on Facebook by accident. Oh, that's brilliant! Technology is indeed a strange beast. Reminds me of my school project we had, making a video about our village history. After hours of struggling with the software, we ended up doing a live recording in our garden. It just felt more natural, you know. Ah, yes, gardens. My wife and I used to spend hours in ours when we were younger, tending to our roses and all. Gardens! Did you guys visit those pretty ones in Yorkshire? I did once, it was amazing. Yes, we did! For a holiday, years ago. One of the places we stayed at was this youth hostel in York. Was pretty quaint and fun for all of us. I've always wanted to travel to the provinces, but never had the chance. Like, take a look at this, all these places I'd love to see. But... I know what you mean. Travel can be a bit challenging when you have mobility issues. Though, I do remember this one time our family went on a guided tour of the London underground system. Fascinating, really. Yes, fascinating. I used to take our kids on them for school projects. They loved it. Of course, that was before all the disruptions and everything. Hah, yes, my grandson was on that London Underground for his school project. Imagine having to handle such a huge, bustling structure as a child! And now, they're trying to do global warming projects! It's all quite overwhelming. Yes, it is quite overwhelming for them and us too. The world has changed so much since we were young. The technological advancements and the global issues we're all facing now. But at the same time, I think that's the most interesting part. The youth today... they're already so aware and practical about these issues. Remember when we were young, it was so much simpler? Well, simpler in many ways, maybe. But also, we had youth hostels and hitch-hiking to discover the world in our way.

Right, so I'm going to book my flight for the trip. I have to make sure to leave enough time to get to the airport and clear security. Do you know which terminal my flight is going from? Hi Emma, isn't your flight from London Heathrow, Terminal 3? I think that's right, but you should probably double-check that. But even if it isn't, you can use the flight number to check which terminal it's at right? Yeah, that's a good point. But even so, it's better to plan ahead. I've got a few meetings before we leave, and I want to make sure I have enough time to get to the airport. Plus I've been told it's a 45-minute drive, depending on traffic. Oh, actually, let me just quickly check that for you. Ah yes, you're right. Flight LH304, terminal 3 at Heathrow. Thanks, that's a big help. Right, so now I need to think about transportation. Are you taking the Tube or perhaps a taxi or ride-sharing service? I don’t actually live in London so it's a bit of a different situation for me. But most likely I'll take the Tube. It's quick and efficient. Have you thought about that for yourself? Not yet, actually. It probably depends on the time of day and how much my stuff weighs . I could see it being an absolute nightmare dragging bags and cases on the Tube at rush hour. Yeah, can't say I'd fancy that either. But there's always the option of getting the train to the airport? Just have to make sure to give yourself plenty of time if you're planning to check-in a bag. That's true, I just don't want to risk it. I'd rather be confident I've got enough time. So are you planning to check in and drop off your bag now you've got your flight details sorted? Not immediately, I was thinking maybe the day before? Although I suppose if I do it now I'll have less to worry about tomorrow, but I don't like to leave things until the last minute... Well, the sooner the better usually. You could even do it online and just drop your bag off at the airport the day before.

Ah, marvellous weekend. I managed to get some blackthorn bushes planted today. The wildlife around there is quite something, isn't it? Do you remember the little hedgehogs that used to roam around Woburn when I was young? Yes, I do. Woburn was such a place for wildlife and nature. But even in Hitchin, we've noticed a decline in hedgehog sightings over the years, especially since those fractious developments started encroaching on their habitats. It's quite disheartening, really. Yes, but on a brighter note, have you heard about the new hedgehog highway plans? It's been in the news. They're creating safe routes for them to move among gardens. Oh, we need those! I've noticed a decline in wildlife generally here in Birmingham, too. It's not just hedgehogs, but birds and even the bees! It's ridiculous, innit? Bees are so vital to our ecosystem, and yet, they're struggling terribly. Absolutely. One side effect of urban sprawl and all these new developments is the destruction of natural habitats. And it's not just the wildlife; it's about sustaining the environmental balance. Speaking of balance... have you noticed how supermarket prices are climbing? I saw the price of my favorite brand of porridge had gone up again last week. It's near criminal really. That's certainly true. But you know what I've been noticing? The price of organic produce is actually becoming more comparable to non-organic items. Perhaps it's a sign we're moving in the right direction? More people are becoming conscious about their food choices, which is a good sign. However, it's still problematic if the prices are still so high that it excludes some people from being able to make sustainable choices. Yes, and we also can't ignore the pressure it puts on family budgets. I've had to start meal planning for weeks ahead just to make ends meet. Which brings me to an interesting thought. Money and finance – have you all thought about switching your mobile phone provider? The new package deal from the folks at EE seems quite competitive. Actually, I did just do that. Surprisingly, EE still seems to have the best coverage in our area. But it’s always worth checking. We could all share the best deals we've found? It might save us a bit of money, especially with the rising costs of everything else.

Yo, lads and lasses. What d'ye think's the grooviest thing about summer holidays? Oh, holidays are ace, innit? I particularly love just chilling out, maybe heading to some beautiful countryside and taking nice long walks with my dogs. Ah, dogs are just so cheerful isn't they? I've got a lovely pup at home, his name's Lucky. He makes the best travel companion, right? Definitely, he says. But I've got another keepsake that I dearly love - its my pet goat. It's quite eccentric, keeps me on my toes. [laughs] Goat's are a bit of a character, just like you, lol. Speaking of characters, what's the best vacation spot you've ever been to? Me? Oh, I've had a blast in South Africa. It's wild and free, man. You get these massive game reserves where you can see the big five up close. Ooh, that's a thrill-seekers paradise, ain't it? I'm a bit more of a city girl myself. I love urban escapes - if I can find good food and quirky shops, I'm happy. That makes two of us. But if I'm totally honest, there's something special about the sea. I love holidays by the coast, especially in Wales. The food is brilliant, especially the seafood. True dat, seafood really is the best, innit? Hartlepool's got fantastic fish and chips. But I also have a weakness for a nice steak - slow-cooked with lashings of that lovely Irish butter. Irish butter on steak? That’s genius! But the secret Irish ingredient is actually the Guinness, try it next time. [laughs] You're right, Guinness is a game-changer. But personally, my holiday snack of choice is always and will always be a great English roast - the caramelised roasties and gorgeous gravy can do no wrong. Roasts are brilliant, but you can't forget about scones with clotted cream, can you? I mean, those are essential for a proper English afternoon tea. [chuckles] Oh, the delights of traditional English food. Though if I'm being honest, I've had some amazing South African braais too, BBQs where they just throw everything on the grill and it all works out. So, what's the one food you all could eat every day? Definitely anything with cheese - but any type of cheese! Cottage, cheddar, brie, it really doesn't matter as long as it's cheesy.

Yo, I was browsing through some art books in the library and I stumbled upon these beautiful impressionist paintings. It really got me thinking about what art means to people, you know? That's really interesting, you've really got a good eye for art, haven't you? I kind of stuck to realism because it kind of makes me feel more connected to the world, but I suppose every type of art has its own meaning and beauty. Exactly! I think what I find truly fascinating about impressionism is how subjective it is. The way the artist portrays reality through their own perspective... it's almost like, okay, you're not seeing the world as it truly is, but as it's perceived by this individual. Yeah, it's like capturing a specific moment in time through the eyes of the painter. Exactly. And what about modern art? I mean, sometimes I feel like the intentions behind it are completely lost on me. It's creative and all, but sometimes I wonder whether it's just about triggering emotions rather than conveying something specific. I think that's the point, though. Art is a form of expression, it doesn't always need to be about conveying something "correct" or "real." Sometimes, it's just about evoking a feeling or stimulating thought. True, I guess that's the core of art. It's subjective. But it also makes me think about old age and whether current trends in art will be as significant then as they are now. Like, in 50 years, will people still care about modern art, or will there be something entirely different? That's a very good point. But it's the same with everything, isn't it? Just like technology or politics, art is a reflection of its time. Maybe people in the future will look at our art and see it in the same way we see, say, Renaissance art. I mean, it's not about whether it's valuable or meaningful now or then, but about its cultural resonance. That's a beautiful way to put it. It's really helped clarify my thoughts. Glad to hear that. Speaking of time, have you seen the assignment sheet for our upcoming essay? I'm struggling a bit with how to narrow down the topic. It's so broad! Oh, I’ve been thinking about that too.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to make pancakes for fifty people at that charity event last week? I don't know what I was thinking. No, you never did. That must have been a nightmare! But hey, pancakes are always kind of therapeutic don’t you think? What kind are we making tonight? I was thinking of making this new recipe I found online, with chia seeds and lemon curd. They recommend it as a stress-relieving recipe, so I thought it would fit our evening perfectly. Well, after dealing with patients all day, I could use some stress relief. Plus, your pancakes are always worth the mess. So, what's the plan for dinner? I'm making the pancakes and you can handle the sides. Maybe we can talk about our days, catch up on each other's lives while we cook? That sounds like a great plan! Did your day get any stressful at work? As for me, I had a really interesting session with a new patient today. He's facing this really common issue and it reminded me how much our role as mental health nurses is about helping people recognize positive habits in their lives, while also working through their negative ones. It’s really rewarding but also can be draining sometimes. Absolutely, it must be very emotionally demanding working in mental health. How does it impact your personal habits or friendships? Like does it ever feel like you're carrying that stress home with you? Actually, that's a big part of my postgraduate course - recognizing that it's not just about the patients but also about maintaining your own well-being. It's helped me develop some really good self-care habits. More power to you! I could learn from that. At work, we are so focused on our projects and getting things done, sometimes we forget to take care of ourselves. That’s so true! We actually have a team where we all take on making dinner for one another once a week to help out. It’s become a nice routine. Makes everyone’s day better. That’s so cute! I love the idea of sharing meals with colleagues. We should do that here sometimes too. Either way, I could use a break from this almost gone overdue pancake recipe. The recipe seems to still be going strong then.

Right, let's get down to business then. As you know, we have to ensure that the consent form is clear and concise for our students. Have we decided on what type of consent form we're going to use? Are we sticking to the standard one from our faculty or are we going to modify it a bit to fit the seminar questions better? I think it would make more sense to stick with the standard faculty consent form, at least for the basics. There's nothing wrong with it, and I'd hate to complicate matters by creating a new one that might cause confusion for students. However, would it not be sensible to add a note about confidentiality, especially considering the sensitive nature of some of our seminar topics? Absolutely, confidentiality is a must. But let's also consider making it clear to the students that any information they share will be used solely for educational purposes - that we're not looking to exploit any market insights or personal details they might share. Yes, that's very important. It also goes hand in hand with the discussion on the structure and content of our seminar. As it's on international business communication, should we emphasize the cultural differences in communication or go for something more general that covers various forms of international business interaction? I think it would be great to touch on both. Cultural differences in communication are huge, but so are other aspects like digital communication, language barriers, and the nuances within different industries. Maybe we can divide the seminar into sections - first, an introduction to global communication in general, followed by specific cultural considerations, and then, a practical session on overcoming barriers and using technology effectively. That sounds like a solid structure. We should also give the students some practical examples or case studies to work with during the seminar. It makes the learning process more engaging and they might even see some real-life applications. Right, and in that section, we could also cover the legal and ethical considerations in international communication. We don't want anyone to be surprised by the legal implications of their communication style once they enter the job market. Excellent points all around. Let's also remember to include some time for questions and answers. It's always beneficial to leave some space for the students to engage and express their interests or concerns.

I keep telling James to choose subjects he's passionate about, but today's class was just so much fun! The students clearly enjoyed it too, and talked about it all the way home. Made my day. I agree! You've always been great at engaging students. It kind of makes me want to join one of your classes, even though I've been "teaching" for a while now . Oh, it's not that hard... until you realize that every class is actually a performance . But we've been lucky to have a great deal of autonomy with our subject matter, so I can definitely choose topics that interest me. That makes a big difference. It's one of the perks of being a lecturer here in China. I suppose it's a bit easier than if we were back in the UK, where there's more pressure to stick to the syllabus... Definitely. Although, this semester's syllabus isn't that bad, I think. And the students here are so eager to learn... which can be both a blessing and a curse . Tell me about it! But seriously, have you started thinking about the research project again? You were going to look into the cultural nuances of teaching English in China, right? Oh God, yes, I still hope to do that. It's been on my list for ages, but I just haven't had the time. And with the "house" projects we've been dealing with since moving in... "The house projects"?! Oh, we've been meaning to discuss that. So, you've really decided on getting that flat? I worry it might be a bit too much. Well, initially we were just looking for a quick solution because of the commutes. But then it became this whole affair! We're changing the layout, redecorating... You'd think after all the renovations we've done in rental places, we'd know better! But it just feels right for us. It does sound like a project. But I know you both, and this is the kind of thing you love... once it's over . Exactly! The plus side is that we're not stressing about fixing something that isn't ours, so that's a plus. And it'll be great for the future, I suppose. Yeah, it's a bit of a compromise, I guess. We're really lucky to have this opportunity, and I know we'll make the most of it.

Oh, did I buy too much groceries again? Seems like it. You always say you're just buying the basics and then you end up with enough for a week's worth of meals. I know, I just can't help it. It feels easier to stock up, but of course, then I worry about food wastage. Absolutely, food wastage is a massive issue. But even worse is how backwards our approach to food in this country is. I mean, we've got all these 'use by' dates on food that aren't even based on any real scientific evidence. Yes, and then there's the absurdity of the 'best before' concept. I've had a loaf of bread last months after that date. It's ridiculous. It's a money-making scheme basically, forcing people to throw out perfectly good food. And considering that our grandparents grew up in a time when they never threw anything away, it's really sad to think how far we've come. Our grandparents, both our grandmas, especially. They always reused and repurposed everything. Right. If they ever had extra food, it was always given to the local community, or made into something else. Like that time Aunty made soup from all the veggie ends and peels. Yes! That was a 'closed-industry' approach to food - doesn't waste anything. But it's not just about the food though, is it? No, not really. What about career advice in schools? More specifically, do you think they focus too much on popular, stable careers and not enough on newer industries? Good question. I personally think they are quite slow to adapt in that respect. They tend to push science and engineering heavily because those are seen as 'guaranteed' jobs, but don't do a great job of highlighting some of the newer areas like software engineering or urban farming. Urban farming? That's a growing field, right? It is. Especially with the push for more sustainable practices and the urbanization of the population. There are all these new initiatives popping up in cities, using unused space for farming. That sounds fascinating. So, what stops more people from getting into it? In part, it's because lots of people think it's for hipsters or the environmentally minded, but it really has the potential to bring fresh produce into cities and reduce plastic usage. Plus, from what I've read, some private industries are starting to support it too.

I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Grace's school report? It arrives today and I'm curious about how she's doing. Ah, yes. I got a look at it earlier. She's doing really well, though a bit of a struggle in math this term. But overall, she's staying up her usual high standards. I'm glad to hear that. Now, speaking of high standards, how's your new job going? I remember when you mentioned it needed a lot of organising and routine... It's tough, as usual at the beginning, but I'm enjoying it. There's a lot of responsibility, but I think my research experience helps. Absolutely. Your work as a post-doc definitely honed those skills. It's great that you're applying them in this new context. Thanks, it's just good to be doing something a bit different. Although, it keeps me on my toes! I can imagine. I'm on my own roundabout when it comes to research. These peer reviews are always a battle. The waiting is the worst part. Absolutely, that's the worst bit. What's the project about? It's about stress and anxiety in healthcare workers during COIVD. It's quite timely, I suppose. That's really relevant. I've spoken to a few friends in NHS who've had it tough. I'm sure you've seen some awful things too in your time as a psychologist. Yes, it can be quite distressing. But it's also rewarding to do something that could hopefully make a difference. It will. There's definitely room for improved wellbeing for healthcare staff globally and it's great that you're looking into changing that. Speaking of stressful jobs, how was the family meeting you had with Tom's school this week? Ah, it was quite a meeting. They're introducing some new safety protocols and Tom's class needs to get used to them. I went in thinking it would be a simple meeting but ended up discussing this and that with the teachers. I'm sure it was a bit of a comprehensive overview then. Completely. But it was useful. Though, come to think of it, preparing for all this change can be stressful for the kids too. I need to make sure we don't add to that stress at home. You're absolutely right.

You know, I was thinking back today. The sea... it never fails to bring back such sweet memories from our childhood years. Right! The sound of the waves, the smell of the salty air... We used to have grand holidays there when we were young. That's a great point! I remember watching a documentary on TV about the impact the sea has on mental health. They said it can really help with depression. That's true. There's something about being near the water that seems to calm the soul, doesn't there? These days, though, I often find myself feeling a bit depressed. All the time I spent at home, not working... it gets to me. Oh, John... I know how you feel. It's the same for me, I suppose. It's not easy when you feel like you're not contributing in any meaningful way. You're not alone. Many people struggle with that sense of purpose after retirement or unemployment. However, there are ways to overcome it. Volunteering for instance, can give a new meaning to your days. I've heard about this organisation that looks after baby blue tits. You might find that fascinating. Baby blue tits? Yeah, tell us more! Well, I've got a friend who is actually involved in a local wildlife conservation project. They deal with these birds quite a bit. It might be something that could give you purpose and keep the feelings of loneliness at bay. That actually sounds quite appealing. Maybe I could try that? Definitely, John! And, if you need a buddy for it, I'm right there with you. Yes, that's a great idea! There's also another topic we need to touch on. You both shared about feeling lonely and depressed. I can tell you that it's a common issue that often ties back to feeling valued and seen. I guess that's true. When you're not working, it can feel like the world isn't needing you. Exactly. But maybe this could also be a conversation we need to have with our family? Let them know how we're feeling? I think so. Open communication about our feelings could really help. I know sometimes it feels like we're a burden to others... but we're all in this together, you know? We also need to talk about money problems. I find that discussing that really helps to ease the stress.

So, I've been meaning to try out this new brand of beauty products. I've seen so many good reviews online and I thought it would be nice to give it a go. Oh, which one? I've also been thinking of trying something new, as my usual brand is kind of expensive. It's called "Silkfeet". They say it's quite gentle on the skin and it has some really good reviews for sensitive skin like mine. I'll definitely check it out then. I have sensitive skin too and I'm always on the lookout for gentler products. Exactly! Also, they have this lovely little candle that accompanies some of their skincare products. It's just like aromatherapy. That sounds lovely. I do love a good home fragrance. Is the candle part of the skincare sets or is it a separate product? It's sometimes included in the set, especially in the gift sets, but you can also buy it separately if you want. It's not expensive for what it is - really calming. For me, a good home candle is essential after a long day at work. It just makes everything feel better. Where did you find it? I've seen it on Amazon, but I saw it in a few shops in town too. There's a small beauty shop near us that's very well stocked. Ah, yes! There is one isn't there? I remember walking by there once and it looked really well-stocked. Maybe I'll stop by and have a look. But it's not just about the products now, is it? It's about the whole experience. I mean, if I'm planning to treat myself, I want to go the whole hog - a gentle bath, maybe some nice music, the right products. Oh, absolutely. A bit of self-care is just what's needed, especially after a hard day at work. I often find myself wishing for longer evenings so I could sit back and do all that without pressure of time. I know! Our lives can get so full and busy, it's hard to take a step back. But those little moments for ourselves are so important. They definitely are. Did you have a chance to try any of this Silkfeet range? I actually bought a little travel set and I've been using it on my face for a few days now.

Yo, mate, been a while. How's work been treating ya? It's been okay, thanks for askin'. Just been deep into this case at the moment and it's been a right challenge. Plus, we're training a new team now, which is interesting but a fair bit of work. You know how it is. Yeah, totally. I've been keepin' my hair on with the students lately, teachin' 'em prepositions and past simple, and dealin' with all their quirks... So keeps me busy. You'll always be the word nerd. Haha! Idle remark, but I've been tryin' to get 'em into museums and things to make grammar more interesting. Good idea, actually. I've been thinkin' of takin' some of my clients out to the Walker Art Gallery, see if it helps them with literacy skills. You think creative activities would work in your classroom? Absolutely. I've seen it before. Visual aids and all that. Yeah. Now that I think of it, it might be quite good. I've also started thinkin' about maybe doin' the interview for that Master's. Still in doubt but the university is offerin' a scholarship, so it's tempting. That's great news! A bit more cash wouldn't hurt, right? Speaking of which, how's the money in your pocket been? Haha, well, all the money's been going into that interview prep course I'm takin', so it's been a bit... sparse. Yeah, preps like that can be pricey if you're serious about it. true enough, but it's worth it if I get in. The idea of bein' a confident academic is quite appealing. And you deserve it for all the hard work you've been puttin' in. You'd think after all the education I've had, I'd be comfortable with these kinds of things, but there's always room to grow, right? And besides, it's for a good cause – helpin' students learn English. Exactly. Anyway, what about you? Any big plans or just takin' life easy? I've been thinkin' about gettin' a new place soon. The rent in Liverpool isn't cheap, so I figure it's better to own rather than rent. Sure, there's a bit of upfront cost, but over the long run it makes more sense. That's a smart move. I've been feelin' the same about movin', but with the money situation how it is... Don't worry, mate, there's always time for that.

Evening, lovely to see you. How have you been?? We've not caught up in ages. I've been well, thank you for asking. Had the usual toddler chaos to deal with though haha! Oh, yes, I can imagine – always something, isn't there? So, how's your partner finding it, now that the little one's getting a bit more independent? Oh actually, that's a big part of what I wanted to talk about with you. He's finding it... interesting. You know, having to adjust to not being the one and only, so to speak. It's tough for him to see the little one sticking by me more at times. Absolutely, it's a big change, isn't it? But in many ways, it's a sign of their bond growing stronger, isn't it? I want him to see it that way too, but for now, it's...tough. It is tough. And it's understandable. Step parenting, or whatever we want to term it, or even just parenting in general, it's a journey of constant growth and change. That's so true. I feel like sometimes I'm assumed to have the 'divine right' to the child’s attention – and its so hard for him, not being the biological parent. It's like he's suddenly expected to drop into a pre-established family, no induction or anything silly like that! Exactly, and the guilt trips... 'You're not the "real" mum’… But it's not about "real" or not, it's about finding our places, roles, and all that. I remember when I first got into this. My side of the family was a bit... complicated about me, taking over the "parent" role. Oh, so it's quite universal then. Absolutely. But it's a bond that'll grow and strengthen if given time and patience. I try to talk to him but he often retreats saying he’s just trying to find his way. That’s understandable too. It takes time to adjust to anything new, and this is definitely uncharted territory for him. So, how do I encourage independence without him feeling left out? I don't want to push him away but still want the child to know he can go to both of us equally. Ah, that’s the million dollar question, isn’t it? For me... I found that any activity the child enjoys can be a great bonding experience if done together.

Oh, did I ever tell you about Kim’s birthday party? We basically re-enacted an episode of The Crown. You mean you didn't just decorate with the usual balloons and streamers and settle into a game of pintrest? That sounds quite the elaborate situation. Absolutely not! We had theme music, costumes, and even a fake speech written by someone pretending to be Winston Churchill. It was hilarious! And how did everyone react to that? I imagine people would either love it or find it too weird. Well, there were definitely a few confused faces at first, but I think we pulled it off pretty well. We even dressed like the royal family, including what we thought were appropriate hats. Was a bit tricky finding the right King’s crown without looking too comical. That does sound quite entertaining. We should try that sometimes with our creative friends. Although, in the Midlands, we might have to juggle the preference for something a bit less... theatrical. No judgment on that! But I suppose that's what keeps it interesting, right? The Midlands has a whole different vibe. More relaxed, earthy. Where did you get the idea for your birthday last year? It was a photo booth setup at the local pub followed by a trivia night. Everyone loved it. We're thinking of doing something similar this year perhaps, although I feel like we've already done the photo booth in several forms. I'm sure you're right, but that can't stop us from coming up with new ideas! But it proves the point - the possibilities are endless when it comes to finding fun themes to bring everyone together, no matter what region you're from. True enough, and it’s all a bit like the various popular TV shows we talk about. We’re constantly searching for the next interesting or unique concept to engage us. Exactly! And you noticed how lately everyone seems to be watching so much TV? We could sit here all day talking about our favorite shows. Did you finish that new series on Netflix? I did! It was fantastic! The way they combined reality with fiction was quite clever. And have you seen the latest episode of that drama show on BBC? It was right on the edge of my seat almost the whole way through. No, I haven't caught up yet, but I've heard it.

Oh, did you find anything else exciting on eBay today? Or is it just more of those intriguing light fittings? Well, I did see a beautiful ceiling rose fitting that really caught my eye. It's from the 19th century – do you have any idea how much one of those could cost? Honestly, I have no idea. I'm just browsing, seeing what comes out. But I'll give you a hint; if it's from the 19th century, it's probably not cheap. Oh, I'm not planning on buying it today. It's just fascinating to see what people are selling, and the prices they're asking. I feel the same way. And the houses on Rightmove? Have you found anything promising? We've been looking for ages, and yet we haven't quite found the right one. But this weekend, I found a house in a suburb we hadn't looked in before. It's quite charming, really. Oh, let me see! Where is it located? It's in Wimbledon. Good schools, quite a quiet residential area. Ah, yes, Wimbledon's lovely. But, have you thought about what you'd have to do to it? It might need a bit of work, I imagine. Well, there is a bit of work that needed doing, but the estate doesn't look too bad. Hmm, prices here can be high, and if it’s in need of renovation, we should factor that in. Absolutely. I was thinking we could discuss it further over dinner tonight. What do you think? I think it's a great idea. But first, let's finish browsing on Rightmove. Always the spoilsport. I'm just being realistic! That's what I love about you. And what I love about you is we can do this together. True. Now, shall we get back to it? Let's see what else we can find. Maybe we'll find the perfect house... or just dream a bit. That works for me too. Right, back to the screens then. [They both go back to scrolling through the internet, occasionally commenting on the what they see] Oh! Have you seen this? It's a house that's close to the new community garden project we've been attending. Really? That sounds like a bonus. But let's look closer. It does seem quite interested. Not too old, decent size. I think it could work.

Oh, did I tell you last night's shift was a whirlwind? No, what happened? Well, we had this one patient who... just wouldn't stop asking about the Queen. Now, questions are part of the job, isn't it? But seriously, every other minute it was "Does the Queen really like that brand of tea?" or "Is it true that the Queen never travels without her corgis?" As if. That's probably another one of those urban myths, isn't it? True, probably. But nonetheless, it kept the day interesting. Interesting in a good way or a bad way? Well, I suppose it gave the other patients something to chat about. Weirdly, it brought out all these stories about people meeting the Queen, or how her corgis might react when she travels. It was quite the distraction from the general chaos of a busy ward. I hope you didn't have to deal with any of this during a critical moment or anything. Not to the extent it was critical, but you get what I mean? It's these unexpected moments in a job that make you appreciate the other more routine, you know, tasks. Like, what are you hoping for, a job change? Ah, we’re always open to opportunities, but no, not necessarily that. But I've been thinking, might be nice to have a bit more control over the day-to-day, you know? I get that. As a career less stable side of things, you do have to keep an eye on openings. Exactly. I mean, job security isn't as secure as we'd like it to be in care and nursing, but we know that. Yes, and we do what we do for the satisfaction of helping people, that’s for sure. But sometimes you wish there was just a bit more flexibility. Flexibility like deciding when to take your 20-minute break? Yeah, or just being able to set your own pace sometimes. Speaking of jobs, did any of us hear about the new care home that's just opened up in town? No, hadn't heard... I came across a bit about it in the local news. It’s supposed to bring like 30-40 new jobs to the area. That’s quite a number. You know, maybe there’s something suitable for us all? It's worth a look. There’s never any harm in seeing what’s out there, especially with jobs that align with what we do.

So, I was browsing through some scientific journals over the weekend and found this fascinating study on getting a good night's sleep. You know, about how the noise around us, the light exposure, the whole routine of going to bed. It's got me really rethinking my habits now, especially considering this research is kind of new. Oh, isn’t that interesting? Sleep is definitely an important theme for me at the moment, with our daughter starting pre-school this term, I want to make sure I’m well-rested for her morning routine. Exactly. This study actually found that our routine before bed could be just as, if not more, important than anything else. Apparently, creating a consistent, calming pre-sleep routine can significantly improve your sleep quality. That makes sense. I've actually been trying to do a bit more of that lately. What they said about avoiding screen time right before sleep made a lot of sense to me. Yeah, and not just screens. Even some types of light can affect it. Ever noticed how relaxing it feels to sleep in a room without major light pollution? Absolutely. Now that we live a bit out of town, it's easier for both of us to get a good night's sleep. There's just less ambient light around. Exactly. Anyway, the research also suggested avoiding caffeine or heavy meals right before bed. And interestingly, even some physical activity later in the day can help. I could see that. It makes sense that in order to fall asleep, your body should feel relaxed and not pumped full of adrenaline from earlier activity. For sure. And then there’s the whole ambient noise thing. I’ve been thinking of getting one of those white noise machines to drown out all the outside noise. Oh, have you heard of those? How do they work? They basically flood your room with a constant, soothing noise, like rain or waves, which can help mask any disruptions and make you feel more relaxed. That's interesting. It might be something we should try, especially over the weekend when there’s more chance of outside noise. Absolutely. Now, have you ever considered trying camping? I mean, if you want real darkness and quiet surroundings, there's no better way. Camping? Now that sounds like a fun idea. But I've never been camping in England.

Yo, lads and lasses. What d'ye think about's this? I just got a hamster from the pet shop n' I'm practising being a good 'mum'. Aww, you've got a new pet? That's so sweet! Hamsters are kind of cute, aren't they? Yeah, I've got a ginger hamster. It's so fluffy! Have you thought of a name yet, [Speaker_1]? Well, my mum always liked the name Callum, but it doesn't quite fit. You know how it is, right? You want a name that suits the animal. Maybe you should just pick something you've always liked. You know, like naming a puppy or kitten. Yeah, but it's a hamster! [Laughs] [Giggles] It's still an exciting process! I named my ginger hamster Ginger. It just seemed fitting. Oh, that's actually quite good. I might just stick with Callum. It sounds nice, doesn't it? Definitely! And it'll be different from all the Fluffies and Whiskers you see. Speaking of fluffy things, do any of you have a ginger brother or sister? They can be pretty fiery, can't they? Well, I do have a ginger cousin. She can be quite the character. Yeah, I've got a ginger friend and they are never short on energy. That's true! But it's not just the energy, is it? There's something about gingers that seems a bit more... spicy, if you know what I mean. [Laughs] Definitely, a bit more vibrant. I think that's a nice way to put it. They stand out, don't they? Definitely. While I'm on changing the subject, has anyone seen that new series they mentioned at school? I tried to watch it on the BBC site but I couldn't find it. Ah, you're talking about 'The Hamster Chronicles'? It's on the BBC iPlayer. You can watch most of it for free. Yeah, I just watched the first episode. I swear those hamsters were outwitting each other! It's hilarious, isn't it? I didn't expect hamsters to be that clever. They often are more intelligent than we give them credit for. Speaking of smarts, I was thinking of giving mine some toys that work like puzzles. They're supposed to help with brain development. That's a great idea! You know, maybe there's also some good advice online about how to train hamsters.

Right, so I'm losing to Speaker_3 again, and I've been playing this game so many times that I think I've memorized which countries supply which territories. It's just... the dice are against me today, I suppose. Right, voice recorder time. Notes on strategies for Risk: A player's luck and skill isn't always enough. You'd think I'd have won by sheer frequency of play by now. Well, if we're tracking your 'strategies', I think another keeps coming up: overconfidence. Remember last time, thinking you could take over the entire world with a single turn? I remember that. You've been thinking about Risk non-stop, Speaker_1. It's not fair! And the odds are always against me. Careful, or you’ll end up being one of those people who analyzes maps and probability too much. Sometimes, you just have to take risks and roll the dice. And risk losing everything, or as much as the game allows? I’m more of a stick and nothing else than a gambler, I guess. I prefer the certainty of planned invasions. But isn’t that what makes the game fun? The unpredictability? Oh, absolutely. Well, at least my luck might improve with a refill glass of whiskey? Speaker_3, still testing the old 'get inebriated and maybe get lucky' life hack? You can't win them all. How about I suggest something else to cheer you up instead? Chocolate? Actually, that's not a bad idea. We can take a break and the loser buys everyone chocolates. Okay, that’s a deal. If I lose this round, chocs on me. Because science has proven that chocolate improves mood and possibly even decision-making skills. I'm sure there's some study about that out there. Right. Alright, here's my move: I'll attack Australia to secure South America. That's almost as predictable as Speaker_3 defending the U.K. all the time. Careful now, or you’ll make me too confident. Well, I'll just have to risk it. Ugh, nothing but 3’s and 4’s. I’m never going to win. I may as well just concede and pay up those chocolates now. Wait, was that a subconscious attempt to convince us you're a worse player to avoid buying us all chocolate? Speaking of subconscious, ever wonder how when we were younger, we’d play for hours without worrying about winning or losing?

Oh, Lena, remember that first year's flatmate who thought she could handle every GCSE and A-level without a single slumped out study session? Turns out she barely scraped through her uni course. Oh, yes, I remember! We all thought she was some kind of genius at the beginning. But then her grades started showing up... And the funny part? I had a similar streak of hubris for my first semester too! I thought I could manage a part-time job, 15 credits, and a social life. Spoiler alert, I didn't. I can attest to that! I almost did the same with trying to fit in both university and work-life. It was a huge wake-up call. University can be overwhelming even without the extra responsibilities. Exactly! So, how are you coping with it all? Honestly? I barely am. But it's funny because it's so far from what I ever expected. I always wanted to study Psychology, but now I’m this close to dropping out or switching courses because it's just not sticking. I find the lectures pretty interesting but the heavy workload is daunting. I can relate to that feeling, really. What if I tell you that even professors and older lecturers often say they nearly or actually dropped out at some point? It's all about finding the right balance and in most cases, really learning to accept that it's okay not to be a superhuman. Really? That doesn't come across in all the university propaganda brochures we read! Nope, they don't want to scare away potential students with the reality of just how much work it is. But I've been speaking to a few older professors who confided that they’ve had similar struggles. That's a very comforting thought. It’s all about finding your own style, too. No one’s going to teach you that except experience. I know it seems like everyone else has it together, but trust me, they don't. It's all just a facade. This is so good to hear. I've been almost too afraid to speak up in my classes or ask for help because I thought I was the only one feeling that way. Exactly! We both need to remember that we’re not alone in this. I know that university often feels like this really high-stakes game, but most of our flatmates/friends are going through something similar if not identical.

Yo, mate, did you finish that history project? Nah, nearly. I just need to write up the conclusion and proofread it once more. You? Thinking about doing mine tonight. There's quite a bit to write on Black and White Britain, you know? Yeah, it's heavy stuff isn't it? I mean, people don't realize the complexity of poverty and history links that have led to current race and socioeconomic disparities. Exactly. Our school set it for us so that we'd realize that it's not just something in the past, it's still happening today, and it's a big deal. Definitely. I've been questioning a lot of stuff about society since we started the project. Like, what's the point of science if it doesn't ultimately help reduce global inequality? True that. One of our history teachers was saying that the scientific breakthroughs during the Industrial Revolution were sometimes made by creative thinkers who were poor, you know, like Faraday discovering electric induction in a barely funded lab. It's like, if we had more social equality, we could have much better scientific development that was actually for the benefit of all, not just the elite. Exactly, and it ties into this thing about consumerism too. We seem so focused on buying the latest gadgets and stuff but forgetting to look at the bigger picture, like who made it and how it affected them. It's like we're buying into this cycle where everyone's trying to climb this imaginary social ladder by owning stuff, but at the cost of our relationships and life around us. And politics isn't helping either. All the political talk doesn't seem to translate into action. It feels like the real issues, like fair pay, affordable housing, and education, get sidelined for who can tweet the most hyperbolic stuff or who's got the most expensive campaigns. Totally right. I mean, look at our local elections. The city council does some small things but they never address the core issues really. There's always talk of regeneration but it's changing the city to benefit more affluent people and businesses. True. I wish there was more emphasis on cultivating community. I mean, look at our walk here, it's so much nicer having friends to talk to about things like this than worrying about getting the latest smartphone or something.

Ah, I've been meaning to talk to you about the recording process. I've been working on some self-help books and found that recording my own voice has been a bit of a challenge. Oh, that sounds quite challenging! I never thought it would be hard to record oneself, but I do remember questions on this kind of thing at school. Exactly! But the actual part where my throat feels like it's been through a meat grinder at the end of a session... That's the surprising part. Right, recording can be surprisingly tiring! Even with all the breathing techniques and vocal warmups, by the day's end, I'm hoarse. It just shows how much we take talking for granted! Yeah, and now you can't speak even when you want to. Exactly! So, the other day, I went over to our neighbour Ron, who's a sound engineer, for advice. He was so helpful! Did I tell you his carpentry skills are on par with his musical ones? He fixed the shed for us last summer. No, I don't think so. That's interesting. He suggested some very specific throat soothers and maybe even seeing a voice coach if this goes on. Have you considered that? It might help manage the physical strain. I'm not sure I'd go that far, but throat soothers... I could try that. Alright, I'm sure you’ll find a way that works for you. But it's not just the voice; my joints have been playing up lately too. You know, middle-aged woes... I've been considering starting some physiotherapy. Oh, I see, so that explains the base of it. Speaking of woes, have you noticed how couple of years can really play on your body? Indeed! But I guess changing the clothes to something more comfortable could help, right? Definitely. I've had to start doing that for myself. I've gained some weight when I stopped working and so I've been having to buy new clothes that fit. Speaking of clothes and body changes, I could use some dietary advice. I've been noticing my weight has been creeping up. Ah, I've been trying out different diets, but the ones that work seem so restrictive. I know that feeling! You'd think it'd be easy, just eat less, right? But it's hard.

Right, so I'm going to make sure to grab beans from the groceries we got. I think we have some haricot beans and perhaps some broad beans left. Anything specific you want me to cook? Hi Emma, isn't it great just chilling out, cooking a meal together? That's something we haven't done in ages because of COVID. But, totally agree, haricot beans are fine. If we have some Lancashire cheese, I can whip up a nice bean and cheese pie. Lancashire cheese... that keeps coming up. You're really showing off your south-London roots here, seeing Lancashire cheese as 'local' . But yeah, that would be brilliant. I have some northerners in London who buy that just cos it's considered up North. I guess it's the South-East London stereotype. Though, have you heard about the cheese shop on Gloucester Road? The owner has connections back to Lancashire. No, I haven't. That's good to know. You're useful for things like that, for sure. So, back to cooking. You and me making Lancashire cheese and bean pies is quite different from anything the people at my place would typically do. I'm curious, where did you learn to cook like this? Ah, well, you can't beat the north for good grub, can you? My mum is brilliant at making Lancashire hotpot, so that's where a lot of my cooking inspiration really comes from. Plus, we'd always have a big Sunday roast with beans and that sort of thing. But it's not just about the food, I'm sure. It's about the community and family. Did you grow up seeing your mum cook the way you do now? Yeah, a lot of the times. Our family would sit down to dinner every night. It was a time to talk about our day, share stories. My mum's really insistent on family time, even when I was changing the world at uni. Change the world? What were you thinking? I know, just my usual idealism. I was studying Events Management at uni, trying to see how I could make events more community driven. That's kind of what led me to my current job as a Conference and Events Co-ordinator. That's awesome. You know, I came into Production Control with a similar idealism. I liked the idea of thinking ahead, organizing, making things run smoothly.

So, I watched "Tenet" last week. What did any of you think? Yeah, I saw it too. It was deep, but a bit confusing, right? I really understood it. It’s just inverting the entropy. Oh, did I ever have an exciting weekend! Paris was beautiful. The markets, the food, even the rain was charming. Well, most of the time at least. Sounds like a lovely trip. Yo, mate, how was your weekend? Did you manage to get any chill time or was it all work? To be honest, it was pretty much work. Or those kids who think they're going to be the next Shakespeare and their use of grammar is anything but!

Yo, Mum, can I give you a hand with dinner tonight? Of course, dear. How about we make some rice and curry together? It's simple and easy, and we've got a voucher here from the supermarket to use. Exactly, always check the packaging before using any food, especially meat or anything containing chili or spices which could be too strong if they've gone off. And remember, even if it smells fine it might still be off. Sometimes it's the bacterial content that's what you can't smell. Now, let's get this rice going. If you're using a pan or a pot, just make sure it's covered and then turn the heat down once it starts boiling. This is where having salt and fats is important. A little salt to taste, and a bit of oil helps prevent it sticking. But don't put too much olive oil in because that's just bad for you, like having too many jalapenos or too much salt in your meal. Makes sense. So let’s stick with a bit of oil then. Yes, and don't forget to rinse the rice.

Alright mates, dinner is served. We've got some delicious shepherd's pie and cottage pie courtesy of yours truly and Speaker_3's grandma who wouldn't let the two of us help out but somehow still managed to give us the leftovers. I might be looking at some courses or events to further my skills as a support worker.

Right, so I had this absolute nightmare of a day at work. We have this big conference coming up and everything was super last minute. This conference could make or break my reputation in the company. Well, you’ve got to remember that everyone makes mistakes, including the people above you. Right, after dinner and a good game of table tennis, I thought it was high time we had a bit of a chat. There are a few things I've been meaning to tackle. Speaker_2 : Sure, Mum. Fire away. Oh, did I ever tell you about the time we had our laundry done for us by some people who thought they were doing us a favor? No, but I need to hear this. Now, questions are flying already! But for me, I have to say, I'm always happy to help with such events. I've heard it'll be fun though, lots of games and such. Yea! I'm looking forward to it. Mum, I've been meaning to catch up with you for ages. How have you been? You know, aside from work. Oh, thanks for asking, dear. Mum, I was thinking that over the summer holidays, instead of binge-watching 'Stick with Mick' all day, we could do some outdoor activities. You're right, honey. Bro, did you ever notice how often's film uses dentists as the bad guys? You're right! I mean, like who's not afraid of a dentist? There’s a great gig at the Liverpool Music Festival last week. It was this local band, they’re really good, check it out if you can. Ah, lovely to see you, darling! How's life treating you these days? You've been quite busy, if I recall correctly. It's treating me just fine, thanks! I've actually got quite a bit to talk about. I started this new job as a primary school teacher and it's been absolutely overwhelming but so rewarding at the same time. That sounds like a lot of work, but also incredibly fulfilling right? Okay, just to make sure I've got all the ingredients right... Yeah. The spices are important - make sure you've got a mix of all spice, cinnamon, nutmeg... I see. Okay, I might just... try and find any of the older recipes you've got?

Ah, lovely to see you, Sarah. How have you been? We have so much to catch up on, haven't we? I've been alright, thanks for asking. Life's been pretty busy, you know how it goes. Now, this leads me to another topic.

Yo, anyone got any ideas for the Seder tonight? Usually, Dad uses Grace Abounding by John Bunyan, but I thought it would be sweet if we had something a little more... diverse, you know? As for a non-Italian option, how about we do it as a fusion dish? Matzah pizza with some kosher Italian salami or maybe even some artichokes and spinach? You know, it's interesting to think about jewish food originating in Italy. We often talk about the Ashkenazi or Sephardic traditions but often overlook the Italian. I think it could be fascinating to explore those recipes further, maybe even learn a bit of Italian to understand the context. Or perhaps we can go all in and try to make some kosher versions of traditional Italian dishes.

Right, so I brought this weekend's topic to discuss first. We've been watching so many great TV shows lately. Did either of you watch the new season of "Broadchurch"? Oh, yes! I guess, but I was kinda hoping for a more...modern experience. Modernity is in the eye of the beholder, my dear. Besides, we're in Finland, the land of Nokia.
